source: The Mandaean Book of John — trans. Charles G. Haberl & James F. McGrath (De Gruyter, 2020)

1.1: Truth stands by the worlds’ entrance, asking questions to the world.
1.3: “Tell me, how wide is the earth?
1.4: How high is it from the earth to the vault of heaven?
1.5: Whence came Adam? Whence came his wife, Eve?
1.6: Whence came Pitcher-Wine and Spring-Water, who transcend the worlds?
1.7: From whose settlement has this Oil, White Sesame’s son come to me?
1.8: From whose headwater do these rivers of living water come?
1.9: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies sit beneath the vine Yusmir?
1.10: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies sit beneath the vine Shar?
1.11: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies sit beneath the vine Pirun?
1.12: Who called out a great cry, and roused Intellect from its place?
1.13: Who set into motion the great conflict, which will not be resolved for an eternity?
1.14: Who caused the high breach, which will not be plugged for an eternity?
1.15: Who will be the guardian of the house, as far as the enclosure of the worlds?
1.16: Tell me, upon what is the bed of the great and powerful Intellect supported?
1.17: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies sit to the right of the great and powerful Intellect?
1.18: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies sit to the left of the great and powerful Intellect?
1.19: Tell me, how many thousands of excellencies stand before the great and powerful Intellect?
1.20: Tell me, what are the names of the three robes of splendor, light, and glory?
1.21: Tell me, who revealed speech and hearing to the excellencies in their settlements?
1.22: Tell me, who among the excellencies takes the incense holder,
1.24: Tell me, who among the excellencies accepts prayer and praise,
1.25: and takes them to store in his treasury?
1.26: Tell me, when the fetus is formed, in whose bosom is it formed?
1.27: When its mother has it, whose scent does it inhale?
1.28: Who among the liliths dwells in the beds of pregnant women?
1.29: {Tell me, who is the guardian of the house, as far as the enclosure of the worlds?}”
1.31: “I shall tell you the truth, and explain to you just as it was.
1.32: Twelve thousand leagues is the width of the earth.
1.33: Twelve thousand leagues is the distance from the earth to the vault of heaven.
1.34: Adam was made from clay. His wife Eve came from her own source.
1.35: This Oil, White Sesame’s son, came from the settlement of Splendid Yusmir.
1.36: These are living waters; they come from the reservoir of the Jordan.
1.37: Twelve thousand excellencies sit beneath the vine Yusmir.
1.38: Twelve thousand excellencies sit beneath the vine Shar.
1.39: Twenty-four thousand excellencies sit beneath the vine Pirun.
1.40: Yushamen set in motion the great conflict, which will not be resolved for an eternity.
1.41: Abator caused the high breach, which will not be plugged for an eternity.
1.42: I, Ptahil, am the guardian of the house, as far as the enclosure of the worlds.
1.43: The bed of the great and powerful Intellect is supported upon the word of Life.
1.44: To the right of the great and powerful Intellect sit twelve thousand excellencies.
1.45: To the left of the great and powerful Intellect sit twelve thousand excellencies.
1.46: Before the great and powerful Intellect stand twenty-four thousand excellencies.
1.47: As for the names of the three robes of splendor, light, and glory,
1.49: Excellent Shunglan takes the incense holder
1.51: Excellent Samandirel accepts prayer and praise,
1.52: and brings them to store in his treasury.
1.53: When the fetus is formed, it is formed in the bosom of its father.
1.54: It is taken from its father’s loins, and moved into its mother’s womb.
1.55: While the child is within its mother’s womb, it inhales the scent of Life.
1.56: The lilith Zahriel dwells in the beds of pregnant women.”
1.57: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
1.58: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

2.1: Truth stands by the worlds’ entrance, asking questions [to the world].
2.3: “Who revealed the secret of the Great, and started the fight with the Light?
2.4: Who shook the settlements, and caused the rumbling in Senyawis?
2.5: Who bound Ur? Who cast Yushamen down from his place?
2.6: Why did they make Abator a judge? Why was inequality created in the world?
2.7: Who told Spirit, and who revealed the truth to the world?
2.8: Who brought calm, and who created strife on high?
2.9: Who corrupted the great justice, and who declared war against the world?
2.10: Who caused the works to be destroyed, and who revealed the secret of the Light?
2.11: Who disturbed settlements, and who spoke the word when it did not exist?
2.12: Who brought a great weapon, and waged war against the world?
2.13: Who seized praise, divided it up, and put it in each place?
2.14: Who offered praise, and recited it to Life’s voice from start to finish?”
2.15: When Truth had said this, my son Yukashar searched his memory,
2.17: “I shall tell you the truth, and I shall explain to you just as it was.
2.18: Yushamen revealed the secret of the Great, and started the fight with the light.
2.19: Hibel shook the settlements, and caused the rumbling in Senyawis.
2.20: He caused the rumbling in Senyawis, and revealed darkness’s secret.
2.21: Ur was bound by Life’s word with the ties that are endless.
2.22: Yushamen was cast down because he wanted to make an attack
2.23: and start a fight with the Mighty’s house.
2.24: He hatched wicked schemes and was bound, so Yushamen might stay put for eternity.
2.25: He cast down his own mouth, because he was not orderly.
2.26: He had no concern and was not humbled, and was not called forth like the excellencies.
2.27: They made Abator a judge, because Excellent Hibel cast him down.
2.28: He saw his son in the black water, he summoned him to his settlement,
2.30: “I am a king’s son, so therefore I shall be called a king’s son,”
2.32: “I shall place a seal on my settlement, so that my strength will be doubled.”
2.33: He summoned his son Ptahil, and raised him to sit in his settlement.
2.34: Abator wronged his ancestors and my house, he was humbled and vanquished from his throne,
2.35: and he went to become the scales.
2.36: Abator weeps and wails, and it rises up and reaches heaven,
2.37: “Whoever does good finds what is bad, whoever does evil finds good.
2.38: I said that I would be great, who has made me so small on Earth?
2.39: I said that I would be a king, who has set me up at the end of the worlds?
2.40: I said that I would be distinguished, who has placed the scales in my hand?
2.41: When I was gentle and meek, why did they call me one who is rebellious?”
2.42: Manda d’Heyyi told Spirit, and started the fight with Life’s house.
2.43: Gubran revealed the truth, and shook all the rivers.
2.44: Yukabar brought calm, and Yushamen started a fight and tumult.
2.45: Ptahil caused works to be destroyed, and the Cloud revealed the light’s secret.
2.46: Transplant disturbed the settlements, Behram said a word when it did not exist.
2.47: Ptahil brought a great weapon, and Sprout waged war against the world.
2.48: Excellent Hibel caught praise, divided it up, and cast it about in many places.
2.49: This was taken to the voice. He called on high, and the voice rose up.”
2.51: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

3.1: Splendor has come to me in plenty, and that which abounds in the world is light.
3.2: The plot is the first that the excellencies undertake to relate to me.
3.3: The man who cast me down from this place of mine to the earth [...] you will destroy them.
3.4: Do not destroy the excellencies’ construction, and do not drive the clouds from their places.
3.5: Do not tear up the great foundation, because it is to your right.
3.6: Do not toss those who disturb in the Jordan, lest anyone attain its strength.
3.7: Do not destroy the abode that I built.
3.8: The day they start a fight with you, your sons were taken to Glory’s Pride.
3.9: They came to wander around the settlements, wandering and seeking their father but not finding.
3.10: The brothers will rally to one another. The wicked will be instructed by one another,
3.12: “Our father has left the realm of Air; how shall we start a fight with him?”
3.13: Their elder brother Sam came, apprises himself of the situation,
3.15: “If I start a great fight, they will say the eldest is ill-raised.
3.16: You, however, go start the great fight, since
3.17: you are still immature excellencies. If you do it, you will succeed, and they will say,
3.18: “They will say they are immature excellencies,” and not take your mistakes up on high.
3.19: Come, start a great fight, and destroy the works of the Creator!
3.20: Arise, forge a great weapon, and wage a war for which there is no end!
3.21: Gird a sword, bring wrath, take the deadly arrows that do not fail!
3.22: Go down to the realm of Air, to your father’s settlements,
3.23: this one whose land is destroyed, and for whom there is no throne to occupy.”
3.24: Yushamen’s son spoke to Great Sprout, saying,
3.25: “Come, air king! Let us take swords unsheathed
3.26: against Sprout, the air king!” and he says to him,
3.27: “Who bound Yushamen before you, to end the fight with him?”
3.28: The air king spoke to Splendid Transplant, saying,
3.29: “The king commanded, and bound Yushamen. Who ends a fight with the kings?”
3.30: Splendid Transplant opened his mouth, and raged. He summoned Great Sprout, and said to Great Sprout,
3.31: “You are not fit, and neither is the clan from which you came.
3.32: Your father is not a powerful excellency.”
3.33: Great Sprout spoke to Splendid Transplant, saying,
3.34: “Damn you, and damn the clan of your father, the agitator!
3.35: You, who would end a fight with a king, are not fit for the Great Life’s house!”
3.36: Splendid Transplant drew a sword and fell upon great Sprout, the air king.
3.37: Splendid Transplant struck him once, but his sword did not cut through his splendor.
3.38: Splendid Transplant struck him twice, but his sword did not cut through his splendor.
3.39: Splendid Transplant struck him three times, but his sword did not cut through his splendor.
3.40: Great Sprout spoke to Splendid Transplant, saying,
3.41: “You son of a disgraceful father, the likes of me are not afraid of you!”
3.42: When Great Sprout said this, the twenty-one sons of Yushamen drew their swords.
3.43: The eldest had put on the weapon, and the youngest was battle-clad.
3.44: Shouting a challenge to Life, they set weapons upon one another.
3.45: The sound of their weapons and the sound of their gear:
3.46: their sounds reached the great light king, and he says,
3.47: “How did Yushamen cut through and ruin the prison?
3.48: Who started a fight with the excellencies and hid himself?”
3.49: Excellent Gubran saw, and said to the light king,
3.50: “It is the twenty-one sons of Yushamen, they are starting a great fight that won’t be resolved.”
3.51: Then the light king said to Gubran,
3.52: “Arm yourself and mount the great scorpion Parahiel!
3.53: Take and set out for the realm of Air. See whether they are the sons of Yushamen.”
3.54: Then Gubran took a great weapon, mounted the scorpion Parahiel,
3.55: and went to the realm of Air.
3.56: Then Gubran opened his mouth, and said to Splendid Transplant,
3.57: “Yushamen’s son, do not start a war with the Mighty’s house,
3.58: and go seek forgiveness for your father, my son.
3.59: If he accepts your request, how beautiful it is! If he doesn’t, become a servant before the king!
3.60: Splendid Transplant, your father spoke to your eldest brother and was not heard.
3.61: See how sublime is the chinstrap he has given me!
3.62: Now, you will destroy the earth with the king’s word,
3.63: if you start a conflict with the lightworlds and frighten them.”
3.64: Then Splendid Transplant let loose an arrow, and Gubran caught them in his right hand!
3.65: Splendid Transplant let loose two arrows, and Gubran caught them in his right hand!
3.66: Splendid Transplant let loose three arrows, and Gubran caught them in his right hand!
3.67: The fourth arrow settled in Pahriel’s paw.
3.68: Pahriel shouted out loud, and his shout reached the light king.
3.69: Then the light king opened his mouth, with endless light and splendor.
3.70: He cast his voice to the 444,000 excellencies that stand beyond,
3.72: “Arm yourselves, take hold of your gear, and mount your steeds!
3.73: Grab the blade, and destructive arrows forcefully!
3.74: Grab the sword wrathfully, and mount your steeds!”
3.75: The light king summons and orders them with a splendor and light that never wane,
3.77: “When you arrive at the realm of Air, fetch the head of Splendid Transplant,
3.78: in the bosom of his mother, Lady Shine.
3.79: Stage the attack in their midst, so they say, ‘The excellencies have been sent!’”
3.80: Then 440,000 excellencies went down to the realm of Air.
3.81: From the peak of Air’s realm, Intellect’s enclosure, they reached Yushamen’s settlement.
3.82: With a lofty weapon, the excellencies fall upon the realm of Air,
3.83: like a sword borne wrathfully or deadly arrows forcefully.
3.84: Then Splendid Yawar slew with his sword twelve sons of Yushamen.
3.85: Behram took as many as they have, nine sons of Yushamen, with his sword.
3.86: One of the brothers, Yukabar, Yushamen’s most precious son, shouted out loud,
3.87: to his father Yushamen he shouted and his shout went forth,
3.88: it reached his father Yushamen, and Yushamen said,
3.89: “Who has killed my son, and who has held my beloved behind?”
3.90: With the shout that Yushamen shouted, he lifted the bonds from his hands and feet.
3.91: Broken were the bonds and the chains that the light king had commanded upon him.
3.92: He took to the great conflict, and remembered the great rage that was in his heart.
3.93: From the Nether Gate, to the realm of Air,
3.94: all the settlements he reached, he destroyed them.
3.95: When he reached the realm of Air, he shouted to the lady.
3.96: The excellencies fell upon their faces, and did not take to the heights from their steeds.
3.97: Their swords fell from their hands, and they did not hold tight to their steel arrows.
3.98: The swords of the excellencies were broken off, and their bowstrings snapped.
3.99: They threw themselves down upon their faces. Yushamen dismounted his steed,
3.100: grabbed 24,000 excellencies, and threw down those who were still standing upon their feet.
3.101: Then 360 realms arrived before the Great king, saying,
3.102: “Cut off is the head of Gubran, who is at the right hand of the light king!”
3.103: Lands quake, mountains shake, and the king rose from his throne,
3.104: and shouted out Life’s call to Yushamen. He lifted from him the splendor,
3.105: the great strength, the fight, and the fury that were in his mind,
3.106: that his sons’ heads with the lady, Splendid Transplant’s mother, were torn from them.
3.107: He dispatched 904 chains of zeynā, which is heavier than iron,
3.108: and they set him beside the Nether Gate, until Eighth of Darkness is summoned forth.
3.109: For seven hundred and fifty years, he will wait in the great shackles,
3.112: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

4.1: “By my own authority, by my own prayer and praise,
4.2: I have made the time of kings, and I ordain the time.
4.3: I called the time, and the time told me, your time is up.
4.4: I took up the sword and the blade; the world I did not create, I shall destroy,
4.5: and the settlements I did not set up, know I have thoroughly disturbed,
4.6: so they might not raise a great sound, and I started a fight on high.
4.7: I reduced the works that were fixed in their places.
4.8: The war, which the mighty did not want, came to me from myself.
4.9: I stirred up a disturbance and brought myself to confinement.
4.10: Splendid Plant spoke to Yushamen, saying,
4.11: “Did I not tell you not to act out of rage and start a fight in the Jordan?
4.12: It was not written for you to wage a war.
4.13: You were small, you were smart. Now, they call you a fool.
4.14: You had a seat at the head. Now, they have put you at the Nether Gate.
4.15: You have destroyed the things you have done since your childhood,
4.16: so that among your first born, you have not given company to even one.
4.17: You have destroyed your lands and buildings, you removed your beds from their places.
4.18: Ladies were married by you, and ladies have been taken away from you.
4.19: From you has been taken the first stability, that the First [Life] bestowed upon your mind.
4.20: You have disturbed your great nest, and you destroyed the well-ordered works.
4.21: You have crushed the great nest, and are between the two kings.
4.22: Your double will be released, but the kings will judge you not to be released,
4.23: they didn’t fix the great thing that was ordered, and won’t correct the deeds that were ordered.
4.24: You stand without judgment, Yushamen, neither humility nor concern came to your mind, and
4.26: You were not given orders or instructed, and you did not seek wisdom from the First [Life].
4.27: You didn’t worry about the Jordan’s clarity or seek teachings from the ladies.
4.28: You know full well, Yushamen, the word that the king heard.
4.29: When it left the mouth of the world, it stopped recounting endless wonders.
4.30: Did you not know, Yushamen, that the destruction of a thousand years
4.31: cannot be restored even in twenty-four thousand years, to just as it once was?
4.32: Your offspring were taken through disputes, and you put the great shackles upon your feet.
4.33: You multiplied their sighing, and sadness will never wane from you.
4.34: You have put tears in your eyes, flowing down like the waters of the Jordan.”
4.35: Yushamen spoke to Splendid Plant, saying,
4.36: “By my own hand, I sought sorrow. Now I shall take and never relinquish
4.37: the sublime one’s truth, and guard it until the Great [Life] does all that it wants.”
4.39: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

5.1: As my father Yushamen plotted in the shackles, wrathfully and defiantly,
5.2: he plotted in the great wilderness, “Let me start a war up on high,
5.3: let me see the Great Life waging this war with me.
5.4: Now I shall pick a great fight with him, and he has created trouble for himself.
5.5: If he comes and escapes from me, I shall see that there is none greater than me.
5.6: Who is worse than me on high, than me in the place of light?
5.7: I am the greatest, my splendor is great, and there is no end to my glory.”
5.8: As soon as Yushamen had said this, the Great Life knew, and he said,
5.9: “I shall cover up the accomplishments of that good-for-nothing Yushamen.”
5.10: He summoned Manda d’Heyyi, he wrote a letter and sent it.
5.11: He gave him a severe warning and told him, “Look at his splendor, what will overwhelm him?
5.12: Did he not say, ‘Great Sprout hated me, and the light king raged against me?’”
5.13: Manda d’Heyyi went forth, and he came to Yushamen’s house.
5.14: Manda d’Heyyi arrived at Yushamen’s house, he arrived and spoke to Yushamen, saying,
5.15: “When you were not great, weren’t you nonetheless still drawing breath?
5.16: You were never great, so why do you stake an attack against him?
5.17: I am worried and pained about you, Yushamen, who is caught in the fetters of the Great Life.
5.18: Your prayers are completed, your anxieties overwhelm you,
5.19: you forget your words, and a tear falls from you to the ground.
5.20: I am telling him what they told him on high, ‘I made Yushamen dwell on the ground,’
5.21: and just like they told him, I am saying, ‘I summoned Yushamen.’
5.22: There is no truth in your perception and no truth in your speech.”
5.23: When Manda d’Heyyi had said this, Yushamen spoke, saying to him,
5.24: “Were you not a messenger they sent, and had I come (instead),
5.25: I would have struck you with a great blow and put an end to your speeches;
5.26: your splendor would not shine, and the light in which you stand would falter.”
5.27: When Yushamen [had said this] Manda d’Heyyi saw Yushamen,
5.28: his abundant strength his ancestors blessed, then Yushamen knocked upon his dwelling.
5.29: “I covered up my splendor, and the man cast me within the tower.
5.30: Then I and my brothers, the excellencies, did not change the things the kings had said.”
5.32: Blessed is the name of Manda d’Heyyi! And Life triumphs!

6.1: On the day the lord taught Yushamen, Yushamen rose from his throne,
6.2: Yushamen rose from his throne, left for Manda d’Heyyi, and said to him,
6.3: “King of the Excellencies, blessed is your splendor, which is risen over us!”
6.5: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

7.1: When I, Yushamen, thought, I sought splendor, light,
7.2: revelation, and explanations without end, in the first treasure,
7.3: and sought to learn from the saying that my father has given me.
7.4: I set my mind to do battle with the Great. I bundled up my rage and venom in my mind.
7.5: I said, “I shall do battle with the First Life, the Second Life,
7.6: and the Life before which none come.
7.7: I shall wage war with the light, and I’ll make the tumult of battle.
7.8: In the midst of the Jordans I’ll make a great battle that is without end!”
7.9: {The first time} When Yushamen plotted, he did something disgusting, that was inappropriate,
7.10: and then the excellencies were in concerns, that grew and which they gave to me.
7.11: They sent me a messenger about him, that he had covered himself in wrath and battle.
7.12: The messenger, who brought the great king’s letter, they put Yushamen in the great shackles
7.13: for as long as the Great [Life] wants.
7.14: When the messenger brought the letter, he did not greet him. He said to him,
7.16: There was fear in his mind, and he spewed bile before him.
7.17: He got up from his throne, sat upon the ground, and said,
7.18: “Who will put the bonds on Yushamen, since the king has sent for him in rage?”
7.19: Yukashar got up from his throne, and placed the bonds in his right hand.
7.20: Yushamen opened his mouth, saying to the messenger,
7.21: “How long haven’t you seen my likeness and stature, and not drunk from a cup with me?
7.22: How long haven’t you eaten a morsel from my plate, not woven the wreath, and not set [it] on your head?
7.23: How long haven’t you seen my form, and my brightness hasn’t spread over you?”
7.24: The messenger opened his mouth, saying to Yushamen,
7.25: “Do not say I came to you for my own sake; the king sent for you in anger,
7.26: and I couldn’t very well say to Yushamen, ‘Bliss and serenity from men.’
7.27: The very good took pride when they don’t act according to an evil inclination.
7.28: Yushamen took pride in his fortresses and his buildings;
7.29: but his sons will be destroyed, entering a brawl, and his ladies will leave him for some tail.
7.30: His splendor and his constant light grew dim, and his accomplishments will be abandoned.
7.31: The wrath that the king has released will not dissipate for generations.
7.32: You, Yushamen, you will settle down, you will go to the Nether Gate.
7.33: Your glory will be taken from you, the crown that the Great [Life] gave you.
7.34: The constant light will be taken from you, and darkness will settle upon your construction.
7.35: The fortresses of your sons will be destroyed, and your thrones will be empty,
7.36: as long as the Great [Life] wills for you. Your wife, who will raise your clan for generations,
7.37: will not be your own wife.” They will bring down all his studs’ clans.
7.39: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

8.1: A voice came to me in the Jordan, and light was abundant in the world.
8.2: Splendid Plant came from the realm of Air, going to Glory’s Pride.
8.3: He arrives at Glory’s Pride, at the messenger who guards the gate, saying,
8.4: “Leave, messenger, and tell the Great king ‘Splendid Plant is standing at the gate!’
8.5: This message, that comes from his mouth, give to him with all due fidelity,
8.6: and may relief be summoned yonder.” The messenger went forth.
8.7: He rose before the light king, but the light king did not see the messenger.
8.8: The messenger bowed down once before the light king, but the king did not see the messenger.
8.9: The messenger bowed down twice before the light king, but the king did not see the messenger.
8.10: The messenger spoke, saying to the great king,
8.11: “Splendid Plant, Yushamen’s son, stands at the gate, and seeks relief from your insight.”
8.12: The light king spoke, saying to the messenger,
8.13: “Open the gate in splendor, open it, and may he ground his feet
8.14: completely upon the truth!” The messenger opened the gate in splendor.
8.15: Splendid Plant stood tall. Splendid Plant spoke to the king, saying,
8.16: “You are relaxed and pleasant, your speech abounds and never flags,
8.17: your splendor watches silently, your light and your enlightenment abound and never flag.
8.18: You have no peer in your crown and no partner in your rule.
8.19: You are a glorious connoisseur, a bottomless vessel,
8.20: you are a glorious guide, who reveals lessons without end.
8.21: Your baptism in the Jordan is established, and all your accomplishments are your own.
8.22: If I tell you, don’t become angry, but let gentleness settle upon your mind.
8.23: Your vigilance, with which you ponder, is sublime, and is unending,
8.24: The man who is taken out from his fortress, and driven with weapons from his homes:
8.25: his sons were killed in a brawl, and his ladies wander about in filth.
8.26: His Jordans will be stirred up, and his settlements will be driven from their places.
8.27: His home, building, and throne were destroyed, and he was set at the Nether Gate.
8.28: Those who disturb his world were captured, and they put misery on his mind.
8.29: If you desire in your plot, I shall settle and calm his mind on the spot,
8.30: set him straight through your baptism, and mention your name over him.
8.31: Let Yushamen be, and he will recognize he has not been forsaken by your name.
8.32: The light king, who was angered, is calm, and forgiveness is on his mind.”
8.33: When the light king heard this, he was thoroughly delighted with Splendid Plant.
8.34: Manda d’Heyyi rose from his throne, and spoke to the light king, saying,
8.35: “The man taken from his land and settlement: you were not authorized to forgive him.”
8.36: When the light king heard this, he said to Manda d’Heyyi:
8.37: “You, from your first day, have not been proper to Yushamen.
8.38: From your first day, you hated him, since you sought a lady from his family, and he wouldn’t give you.
8.39: You hold onto a great grudge; for generations it has not been released.
8.40: You have destroyed and ruined his household, and yet you still hold onto the grudge for ages!
8.41: Who has had done to him since the beginning, what has been done to Yushamen?
8.42: The man who was taken away from his land, and from the chinstrap that the Great gave him?
8.43: Out of his firstborn sons, not one among them remains,
8.44: and his ladies wander about in filth.”
8.45: Then the light king said to Splendid Plant,
8.46: “I shall reveal secrets to you, so that you will hold in clarity,
8.47: the perception that is from your ancestors, and the wisdom that was allotted to your mind.
8.48: Precious are you, precious is your Jordan, and precious is the family, from which you came.
8.49: Both you and the place from which you came will have abundant serenity.
8.50: Bring your father soothing words, and set his heart to rest upon its support.
8.51: Tell him that the Great Life was filled with kindness for you.”
8.52: And Life is praised, Life triumphs, and the man who went here triumphs!
8.53: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

9.1: “Whom shall I call, who would answer me, and whom should I give a word?
9.2: To whom should I give a word, so that which I said will not change?
9.3: Neither he whom I gave my response, nor he whom I told my speech, has heard.
9.4: It pained and oppresses me; it has oppressed and will oppress me abundantly.
9.5: How long shall I live at the Nether Gate, and how long shall I dwell in sorrow?
9.6: When will my quarrel come to a resolution, and will these chains of mine come undone?
9.7: What offense have I given on high, and what have I done in light’s place?
9.8: What have I done, among my deeds, that no other has done?
9.9: Now it pains me, and it grieves my heart.
9.10: How long shall I sigh, and grieve the front of my face?
9.11: How will it shed tears, that one who is like me could not hold back,
9.12: all of whose sons were driven away, and to whose voice none respond?
9.13: I am like a lofty cedar, which the carpenters have surrounded and chopped down.
9.14: Like a cedar that iron has surrounded, the words of my enemies surrounded me.
9.15: Neither my brothers, out of pity nor my friends, out of my friendship,
9.16: remembered to extend truth[’s hand]. my salt and cup were completely overturned by them.
9.17: They forgot the day of my reckoning, and do not recall even one of my days.
9.18: How long have I climbed tall mountains, and how long have I plumbed valley roads?
9.19: I had a thousand friends, and two thousand shared my platter!
9.20: Now I don’t have anyone to take me by my hand.
9.21: On what day did I say that I would be sitting here?
9.22: My mind has not been revealed to me, and none among the excellencies taught me.
9.23: These fortresses of mine are devastated, and my sons have been taken away through strife.
9.24: My home is deserted, and my messengers won’t meet one another.
9.25: These desirable ladies of mine go barefoot, even though they are wholesome women.
9.26: This oppresses and constrains me; my heart sinks in mourning and lamentations.”
9.27: As Yushamen said this, Manda d’Heyyi says,
9.28: “The one who does good, finds good, and the one who does bad things, finds evil.
9.29: Had you been meek, your splendor would not have left its place;
9.30: now that you have thought evil, the place in which you sit is the right one!”
9.31: When Manda d’Heyyi said this, Yushamen spoke, saying,
9.32: “My son, I know who bound me in the bounds that are upon me.
9.33: If only the chain were not heavy upon me, and one lighter than me were encircling me,
9.34: I would have bellowed my great roar, and destroyed all of the mountains.
9.35: I shall do to my enemies what one hasn’t managed to do to the other,
9.36: until the day will come when the prayer will be [fulfilled] for me.
9.37: If this comes to be, namely that my throne is re-established,
9.38: I shall repay a debt, so that evil will become good.
9.39: Nevertheless, I took solace in the fact that I know that I am not alone.
9.40: I heard from my father that the elders will be added to the youth,
9.41: and the youth will be held responsible for their sins, but parents do not hate their children.”
9.42: When Yushamen said this, the Great Life delighted in his words.
9.43: He sent Splendid Plant, the guardian who resides in each and every place.
9.45: “Go forth to Yushamen, set his heart upon its support,
9.47: ‘You are from our creation, we shall not leave you alone.
9.48: Do not say, “I am alone.” Your settlement was set in honor and glory,
9.49: and your fortresses and buildings will rise like they were.
9.50: Your sons will be raised up, and your messengers will guard your settlement.
9.51: Your throne will be fixed up and set like it was, and you will be called ‘king’ in your home.’”
9.52: When Splendid Plant heard this, he went forth to Yushamen,
9.53: he said to him, “Yushamen, listen to the words that I shall say.
9.54: Don’t be concerned, don’t be enraged, and don’t let error enter your mind.
9.55: Why should it be destined to be so, that you should destroy the mighty?
9.56: The Great sent me, and told me, ‘Go to Yushamen,
9.57: calm Yushamen, and tell him to enlighten all his excellencies.
9.58: He will be supported, but humbled, and know that he is established among us.’
9.59: Now you, Yushamen, listen to the true word,
9.60: [listen] to serenity, and stand apart from rebellion.
9.61: Now, the stench is fleeing from your home, and a pleasant wind blows upon you.
9.62: A pure breeze is coming, and then you will forget the trouble.
9.63: You will shine and gleam; you will be raised up and become a king in your world.
9.64: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

10.1: I said that I would be great, who has made me so small on Earth?
10.2: I said that I would be king, why did they cast me down from my throne?
10.3: Great Sprout hated me, and my mother Steady hated me.
10.4: I have destroyed my world, and ruin has come to my house.
10.5: When I was gentle and meek, why did they call me rebellious?
10.6: When they rewarded me as a righteous man, why did they call me the author of wrongdoing?
10.7: When I was diligent and accomplished, why did they call me feckless in the world?
10.8: When I was king at the lightworlds’ beginning, why did they set me at the end of the worlds?
10.9: They set me down at the end of the worlds, and I am waiting in the shackles.
10.10: Why have they called me rebellious, even when I summoned the gentle from within me?
10.11: When I was king in the worlds, why did they call me the author of strife?
10.12: In such a manner it happens to every man, who listens to ladies’ chatter.
10.13: The excellency who listens to ladies’ chatter, after that he will be cast down from the world.
10.14: When I was distinguished among excellencies, why did they call me the Eighth One?
10.15: Why did they separate the light from me, and carry off my splendor?
10.16: They lifted my garments from me, and bound me on the spot
10.17: on which I seek my ancestors, and my glance does not meet theirs.
10.18: I seek my wives, but my wives do not meet my glance.
10.19: I seek my sons, the excellencies, but they do not meet my glance.
10.20: When it pains and oppresses me, I weep for myself.
10.21: Of all the excellencies who have done wrong,
10.22: they repaid me for the wrong I did not do.
10.23: When I was gentle before the king, why did he cast me down from my throne?
10.24: Woe is me, whose mouth brought him down, and whose tongue was an affliction to him.
10.25: They set me in bondage, called me a wanderer,
10.26: and for my mouth’s treachery cast me down from my throne.
10.27: When I was king, they made me an excellency before whom is the king.
10.28: When I was gentle and meek, all the excellencies who were mine hated me.
10.29: Woe to all the droplets of whom all belonged to me.
10.30: They have become enraged with me, with a great wrath,
10.31: and they have bound me to a single place.
10.32: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
10.33: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

11.1: I am a shepherd who loves his sheep. I tend the sheep and the lambs.
11.2: The fold is around me, and from the village and the fold they do not wander.
11.3: I do not bring them down them to the seashore, lest they see the maelstrom;
11.4: lest they come to fear the water, and not drink when they thirst.
11.5: I come bringing them water from my palm, until they drink and graze.
11.6: I bring them to the good fold, and they graze with me from the Euphrates’ mouth.
11.7: from the Splendid Euphrates’ mouth, I brought them a boon which is sublime.
11.8: I brought them myrtle and white sesame, and I brought them shining banners.
11.9: I brush them and I wash them, and I make them smell the scent of Life.
11.10: I bind a girdle to them, which wolves see, and take fright.
11.11: No wolf leaps into our fold, and they need not fear the fierce lion,
11.12: they need not fear the wind, or the thief that cannot enter our place.
11.13: A thief cannot enter their folds, and they need not fear the iron knife.
11.14: While my eyes were resting peacefully and my head was upon the threshold,
11.15: a fissure opened in the heavens and thunder boomed behind me.
11.16: Clouds overtook one another and the boisterous winds broke loose.
11.17: Rain fell in heaps and an elephant-killing stone,
11.18: a mountain-destorying stone, and winds bluster for an hour.
11.19: The seas came and overflowed the whole world.
11.20: There, beneath the waters, the lowlands did not differ from the highlands.
11.21: From the mouth, the waters carried off those who didn’t have wings and feet.
11.22: One goes and doesn’t know he is going, just as one comes and doesn’t know he came.
11.23: I leaped up and entered the fold, to refresh my eyes from their places.
11.24: I filled my eyes, I saw the sea, I saw the raging wind,
11.25: I saw the rain clouds, that give no peace to one another.
11.26: Myriads upon myriads of dragons were in every single cloud.
11.27: I weep for my sheep, and my sheep weep for themselves.
11.28: The little lambs weep, who cannot exit the gate of the fold,
11.29: While they are entering the house like so, I have risen up and stood upon the highest place.
11.30: I call out to my sheep; to my sheep, so that they be with me.
11.31: I call them and whistle to them and make them hear so that they come to me.
11.32: I whistle for them with my whistle, I beat the waters with my purifier.
11.33: I say to them, “My sheep! Come, my sheep! Head for my voice!
11.34: Head for my voice, so that you may be saved from the dragons!
11.35: Come, come, to me, I am a shepherd, who is swiftly coming in my ship,
11.36: coming in my splendid ship, and I shall come and lift my sheep and lambs.”
11.37: Everyone who heeded my call, heard my voice, and turned her face towards me,
11.38: I will hold in both my hands, and raise up with me to my ship.
11.39: Every ram and ewe that was caught, the maelstrom brought down.
11.40: The voracious waters will devour, and whoever did not heed my voice sank.
11.41: I rose to the highest point of the vessel, the bow stands close to the marker.
11.43: “How greatly am I distressed by my sheep, who have sunk down from the scum!
11.44: The maelstrom, the rolling maelstrom, has pulled them down from me.
11.45: How distressed am I for the rams, the wool of whose flanks it has pulled down!
11.46: How distressed am I for the little lambs, whose bellies are not filled with milk!
11.47: Out of a thousand, I found only one, and out of an entire generation, I found only two.
11.48: Blessed is the one swept away by the water, who doesn’t get any water in his ear!
11.49: Blessed are the big rams, who kicked with their feet!
11.50: Blessed is the one who is saved from the Seven and the Twelve who steal sheep.
11.51: Blessed is the one who didn’t lie down and fall asleep, and who did not love deep sleep.
11.52: Blessed is the one who, in this age, though weak, has come to his end intact.
11.53: Blessed is the one who has put on a laurel, and has put on a turban besides.
11.54: Blessed are the female disciples, who are free from Spirit’s snares,
11.55: free from the pollution, the snare, and the chain that never ends.
11.56: My chosen ones! Everyone who is at the end of the Age of Mars,
11.57: may his mind become a support for him. He will come rise to the everlasting abode,
11.58: the place where the sun never sets, and the lamps of light do not grow dim.
11.59: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
11.60: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

12.1: An excellency calls from beyond, saying,
12.2: “Come, be a shepherd’s helper for me, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for me!”
12.3: “So, shall I be a shepherd’s helper for you, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for you?
12.4: How full the world is with wickedness, and sown about with thistles and thorns!”
12.5: “Come, be a shepherd’s helper for me, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for me!”
12.6: “What if I bring to you splendid sandals, to tread the thistles and thorns with?
12.7: Heaven and the earth will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.8: The sun and the moon will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.9: Stars and constellations will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.10: Wind, fire, and water will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.11: The house’s four winds will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.12: Fruits, vines, and trees will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.13: All that is made and done will come to nought, but the splendid sandals are everlasting.
12.14: Come, be a shepherd’s helper for me, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for me!”
12.15: “How shall I be a shepherd’s helper for you, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for you?
12.16: If a lion comes and takes one, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.17: If a wolf comes and takes one, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.18: If a thief comes and steals one, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.19: If one falls in a fire and burns up, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.20: If one falls in the muck and gets stuck, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.21: If one falls in the water and drowns, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.22: If one remains behind in the fold, from where shall I get a replacement?”
12.23: If one remains behind beside in the fold, from where shall I get a replacement?
12.24: “Come, be a shepherd’s helper for me, and tend a thousand out of a myriad for me!
12.25: If a lion comes and takes one, she’ll be the lion’s share.
12.26: She’ll be the lion’s share, because she worships the sun.
12.27: If a wolf comes and takes one, she’ll be the wolf’s share.
12.28: She’ll be the wolf’s share, because she worships the moon.
12.29: If a thief comes and steals one, she’ll be the thief’s share.
12.30: She’ll be the thief’s share, because she worships Mars.
12.31: If one falls in a fire and burns up, she’ll be the fire’s share.
12.32: She’ll be the fire’s share, because she worships fire.
12.33: If one falls in the muck and gets stuck, she’ll be the muck’s share.
12.34: She’ll be the muck’s share, because she worships the oily one.
12.35: If one falls in the water and drowns, she’ll be the sea’s share.
12.36: She’ll be the sea’s share, because she worships the seas.
12.37: If one remains behind in the fold, she will go be the foldergeist’s share.
12.38: She’ll be the foldergeist’s share, because she worships the gods of Nippur,
12.39: {but does not worship what the house worships.} If one remains and goes beside the foldergeist,
12.40: she’ll be beside the foldergeist’s share, because she worships the ‘Holy’ Spirit.
12.41: Come, be a shepherd’s helper for me, and tend for me a thousand out of a myriad!”
12.42: “Then I’ll be a shepherd’s helper for you, and I’ll tend a thousand out of a myriad for you.
12.44: Out of the myriad that bow down before him, some were lost to me;
12.45: I climbed tall mountains, and I plumbed deep ravines.
12.46: I went and found there was nothing to pluck. One by one, I take them with my right hand,
12.47: and I set them balancing in the scales. A thousand balance out of a myriad.
12.48: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
12.49: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

13.1: To you I am speaking and teaching, the chosen and perfect who are living in the world.
13.2: Don’t be part of the darkness, and set your eyes upon light’s place.
13.3: Separate yourself from the evil to the good, from the sinning evildoers of darkness’ place.
13.4: Love and teach one another, so that your sins and trespasses may be forgiven.
13.5: Watch, listen, and learn, and successfully rise to light’s place.
13.6: Good people sit and argue, and how they argue and learn!
13.7: Good people talk, deliberate, and say,
13.8: “Who will come and tell me? Who will inform me and teach me?
13.9: Who will come, and tell me, whether it was one king or two?”
13.10: Good people tell tales, instructing one another,
13.11: “There were two kings, and two principals were created:
13.12: the king of this world and the king of the worlds beyond.
13.13: The king of these ages assumed the sword and the crown of darkness;
13.14: He assumed the crown of darkness, and took the sword in his right hand.
13.15: He took the sword in his right hand, he began to slaughter his sons.
13.16: and his sons killed one another,
13.17: The king of the worlds beyond, and the king of the ages beyond.
13.18: The king of the worlds beyond assumed the crown of light;
13.19: He assumed the crown of light and took the truth in his right hand.
13.20: He took the truth in his right hand, he began to instruct his sons,
13.21: and his sons instructed one another.”
13.22: “Who will come, who will tell me: What came into being from here?
13.23: Before the firmament stretched forth, before the stars were formed within it?
13.24: Before the earth became solid, before the condensation fell upon water?
13.25: Before the sun and the moon go about within this world,
13.27: “When the soul was sitting in the vessel, it had neither hunger nor thirst.
13.28: When the soul was sitting in the vessel, it had neither diseases nor infirmities.
13.29: When the soul was sitting in the vessel, it had neither heat nor cold.
13.30: When the soul was sitting in the vessel, its locks were pleated
13.31: and a crown of air was set upon its head.
13.32: Its eyes were beams of light, gazing upon the place of the Mighty’s house.
13.33: Its mouth was pure perfection, which praised the king of light’s place.
13.34: From the day when the Evil One began to think, wickedness grew within him.
13.35: He grew extremely angry, and waged war against the fire.
13.36: A messenger was sent, to crush the strength of the rebels.
13.37: They brought the living waters and cast them into the still waters.
13.38: They brought the light that shines and cast them into the deep darkness.
13.39: They brought the gentle breeze, and cast it into the blustering wind.
13.40: They brought the living fire, and cast it into the devouring flame.
13.41: They brought the soul, the pure mind, and cast it into the mortal body.
13.42: From the fire and the water, a single firmament stretched forth.
13.43: From the fire and the water, they made Earth solid upon its foundation.
13.44: From the fire and the water, came fruits, vines, and trees.
13.45: From the fire and the water, were formed Adam in the flesh.
13.46: They baptized the messenger and made him lord of the ages.
13.47: He called out a proclamation into the chaos of the world.
13.48: Adam, the sleeper, awoke to the voice of the messenger;
13.49: Adam, the sleeper, awoke and went out to the side of the messenger.
13.50: ‘Come in peace, messenger, emissary of Life, who has come from my father’s house!
13.51: Is this what the precious and beautiful Life desires in its place?
13.52: Is this the throne set for me, (where) my dark double will sit in sorrow?’
13.53: The messenger spoke and said to Adam in the flesh, saying,
13.54: ‘Fair are the seats that are prepared for you, and here will your double will sit in sorrow.
13.55: All will remember you for good, and they wanted me and sent me to you.
13.56: I have come and shall instruct you, Adam, in order to save you from this world.
13.57: Take heed, listen, and learn, and you will successfully rise to light’s place.’
13.58: Adam listened and became faithful; blessed is he who listens and believes after you.
13.59: Adam made a pact; blessed is he who makes a pact after you.
13.60: Adam anticipated and rose up; blessed is he who rises up after you.”
13.61: Take heed, listen, and learn, perfect ones, and you too will rise to light’s place a winner.
13.63: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

14.1: Truth’s Shem begins teaching and instructing Shem, Noah’s son.
14.2: Truth’s Shem stands up, and he bows before the lord, and says,
14.3: “My span is complete, and I want to go, but I do not know who will guide me,
14.4: I fear to go, and do not know how long my path may be.
14.5: Among neither the good nor the wicked, is there one who has gone and returned,
14.6: and came so I can ask how long my path may be.
14.7: Among neither the mild, nor the restless, is there one who has gone and returned,
14.8: and came so I can ask how long my path may be.
14.9: Who will give me what I have given, and who will lend me what I have lent?
14.10: Clarity is gone, and murkiness has increased, and there isn’t anyone to come and question me.
14.11: Purity is gone, and pollution has increased, and there isn’t anyone to come and question me,
14.13: What have I done and what have I lent, that when I go, I shall carry as supplies for me?
14.14: I have heard this, this which came has fallen in my ear:
14.15: ‘Whosoever carries supplies with him, when he reaches the ferry, they will carry him over.
14.16: Whosoever does not carry supplies with him, he will sit and wait for the ferry.’
14.17: My head has grown white and I seek to go, like a grain whose harvest has come.
14.18: My eyes have stopped seeing, like a fortress whose roof has fallen,
14.19: My ears have stopped hearing, like a barren woman without a child,
14.20: My mouth has stopped speaking, like a river that dries up from its mouth,
14.21: My hand has stopped working, like a woman who does not raise her child,
14.22: My leg has stopped moving, like a dumb person who will not learn a lesson,
14.23: I ran day and night, I ran in the daytime just like the nightime,
14.24: I ran day and night, and I took a wife and raised children,
14.25: I took a wife full of the passion of this world,
14.26: I raised children here just like my father raised me,
14.27: I established a dowry within this world.
14.28: Why did I ever take a wife, and why did I ever raise children,
14.29: if my sons will not pay my way and my daughters will not carry me across the great Ocean?
14.30: My brothers will not come with me, and my sisters will not be my supplies.
14.31: As for my wife who loves me, if she is pained and remembers me,
14.32: and cries for me one hour each day, shall I be upheld by my deeds?
14.33: Shall I be supported by my handiwork?”
14.34: When Shem, Noah’s son, said so, a messenger, his creator, came to him and said,
14.35: “Fear not that you have taken a wife, fret not that you have had children.
14.36: Were it not for wives in the world, there would be no Heaven and Earth in this world.
14.37: There would be no Earth and no Heaven, condensation wouldn’t form and fall upon water.
14.38: Were it not for wives, the sun and the moon wouldn’t go here.
14.39: The sun and the moon [wouldn’t go] here, and their lights wouldn’t shine forth in this world.
14.40: Were it not for wives, the living waters would not have come.
14.41: The living waters would not have come, and there wouldn’t be sowing in this world.
14.42: Were it not for wives, the air would not have come here,
14.43: the air wouldn’t be planted, there would be no fire, and it would not blaze forth.
14.44: Wives are everything here, they are like Heaven and Earth in this world.
14.45: You have raised your children to be the record of your name in the world.
14.46: They will prepare your body for Sheol, they will come after you to the graveyard.
14.47: They will recite your ascensions for you, on the day that you depart the world.
14.48: They will give rewards on your behalf, so judgment will not be pronounced upon you.”
14.49: Shem, Noah’s son, spoke to the emissary who came from on high, saying,
14.50: “Perhaps they will commit adultery; then they will torment me!
14.51: Perhaps they will commit theft; then the judgment will fall upon me!
14.52: Perhaps they will sing satanic music; then the blazing fire will consume me!
14.53: Perhaps they will renounce the name of Life; then I shall die a second death instead of one!”
14.54: The emissary of Life spoke, and said to Shem, Noah’s son,
14.55: “The emissary has come from on high, so that adulterers may go to the fire,
14.56: and a great wrath may be upon the thieves,
14.57: and the singers of satanic music will be consumed by the blazing fire,
14.58: and those who renounce the name of Life will die a second death instead of one.
14.59: They have made you no leader over Earth, nor have they called you a judge over the world.
14.60: Had they made you a leader, they would not have brought Abator here.
14.61: He who immediately abandons the world, the fire will set him aflame and consume him,
14.62: and he will bring destruction to Earth when the perfect ones leave him.
14.63: Arise, rise to the Great Life’s house, to the place where the good dwell.
14.64: The place where its sun never sets, and where lamps never grow dim.
14.65: The place where there is no lie, and where there isn’t anyone flawed or lacking.”
14.67: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

15.1: Shem in Truth begins teaching, and instructing Shem, Noah’s son.
15.3: “What sin did I commit in the Great Life’s house, so that the defective age has come to me?
15.4: The Seven oppress me, and the Twelve are an affliction to me.
15.5: The First has forgotten me, and the Second does not inquire after me.
15.6: I have fallen into a great affliction and concerns that never cease.
15.7: Grief has come to me, and my tears flow without finish.”
15.8: Nemrus begins to plot, and says to her sons, the seducers,
15.9: “The chosen one has fallen into our hands; come, let’s trap him with our snares,
15.10: and make him hear a great noise, so that he might forget the sublime banners.
15.11: Let’s entrance him with our beryls and music, so he always will forget to worship.
15.12: Let’s seize him with our snares, and make him the head of us all,
15.13: Let’s hold him in dire captivity, and cast him into terrifying darkness,
15.14: Let’s detain him in our penitentiaries, so he forgets the place from which he came.
15.15: Let’s send something really terrifying after him, so that he will stray from the borderline.”
15.16: When the planets, the seducers of this world, had spoken,
15.17: the head of the ages, Shem, Noah’s son, spoke to them, saying,
15.18: “Go away! Go away, fiends, so that the fire may be your judge.
15.19: You won’t succeed, as you say you will. What you plotted against me won’t ever happen.
15.20: My eyes that gaze upon the light, won’t ever wink so.
15.21: My ears that listen to prayer and praise, won’t listen to useless music.
15.22: My mouth, filled with prayer and praise, won’t bring me any wicked music.
15.23: My hands that give rewards, won’t kill anything on Earth.
15.24: My heart, in which dwells the Great Life, won’t be corrupted by beryls and music.
15.25: My body and soul, made whole by the truth, won’t fall into the blazing fire.
15.26: My body that has not committed fornication, won’t fall into the trap of the Seven.
15.27: My knees that bend down and kneel to Life, won’t kneel to pagans, chapels, or idols.
15.28: My feet that walk on truth’s paths, won’t walk on the paths of treachery and deceit.
15.29: I perfected myself, and so I shall not fear. Life will remember you for good.
15.30: I perfected myself, and shall not fear Earth. I have sought the everlasting abode.
15.31: I lifted my eyes on high, and my soul looks to Life’s house.”
15.33: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

16.1: Shem in Truth begins teaching, and instructing Shem, Noah’s son.
16.3: “The Seven are my enemy, and the Twelve my affliction, and they say,
16.4: ‘Let’s keep him captive in our world, so that he will never see light’s place.
16.5: Let’s keep him in Earth, and he will never rise there, to the light.
16.6: Let’s unleash sadness and resent upon him, so he forgets the man, his creator.
16.7: Let’s take him by means of our great secrets, so he will not recognize his helpers.
16.8: Let’s imprison him in the great prison, so he will forget the sublime banners.
16.9: Let’s unleash a great sickness upon him, so he loses his lord from his memory.
16.10: Let’s teach him our singing and joking, so that he forgets his praying each time.
16.11: Let’s put him in great pain, and the cares of this world.
16.12: Let’s release irritation against him, so that he forgets his evening devotionals.
16.13: Let’s trap him with our sinister snares, so that he never rises to the Mighty’s house.”
16.14: Once the Seven had said this, whose eyes will never see the light, [I said]
16.15: “Neither shall I fall for your secrets, nor shall I stumble upon your obstacles,
16.16: Neither shall I listen to your names, nor will your blazing fires consume me.
16.17: Neither shall I be detained in your abodes, nor shall I forget my helpers.
16.18: Neither shall I listen to your evil words, nor, out of my mind, shall I forget my lord.
16.19: Neither will your nuisances and tortures overwhelm me, nor shall I remove the sublime lessons.
16.20: Neither will your cares overwhelm me, nor shall I stop my evening devotionals.
16.21: Neither shall I be held in your abodes and schemes, nor shall I stop my prayers at any time.
16.22: Neither shall I forget the Great Life, nor shall I yearn for the mortal realm.
16.23: Neither shall I forget the hidden excellencies, my brothers, nor shall I be held in seduction’s abode.
16.24: Neither shall I forget my ancestors’ praise, nor will your nuisances overwhelm me.
16.25: Neither shall I forget the secret texts, nor shall I yearn for useless music.
16.26: I shall never forget those prayers of mine, and I have blocked your plots
16.27: to make me forget my lord. My name will not be something perishable.
16.28: Who would forget his own home, and lust after the mortal realm?
16.29: Who would forget Life’s name, the Great Life’s praise,
16.30: and the devotionals he said and heard, in exchange for the treachery of this world?
16.31: Who would forget the prayer and his ancestors’ praise,
16.32: and dwell within a fleshy body, which is entirely filled with pain and flaws.
16.33: When the Great Life wants me, my double will rise to its settlement.
16.34: The body holds back its owner, and his entire house is darkness.
16.35: He will beat the heads of his servants. I shall rise to the Great Life’s house,
16.36: reside at the head of his enclosure, and never forget my helpers.
16.38: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

17.1: Truth’s Shem begins teaching and instructing Shem, Noah’s son.
17.3: “I am not a son of the house, nor is my double one of the mortals.
17.4: My tribe is not from the world, and the wicked will not injure me.
17.5: The Seven raise me up again, and say to me,
17.6: ‘Strange man, who has no master or mistress!
17.7: In the place in which the wicked abound, what are you doing all on your own?
17.8: If they unleash a great sickness upon you, who will be your healer?
17.9: If the wicked confine you within their fortress, who will be your savior?
17.10: If they set snares for you along your road, who will be your redeemer?
17.11: Who will be your redeemer, and who will be your helper?
17.12: It is the house, whose lord has abandoned it, and whose architect has risen from it.
17.13: Life has reckoned it among its numbers, and all have risen to light’s place.
17.14: Now, you have fallen into the hands from which you will never fall again.
17.15: You have been chained in our fortress, from which you will never be released.
17.16: You have been held in our grasp, and blocked by our work, in our fortress,
17.17: where neither will your helper come to you, nor will the man, your creator, inquire for you.’”
17.18: When Shem, Noah’s son, heard this, his tears came to him and did not stop, and he says,
17.19: “Life does not exist in light’s place, nor is Manda d’Heyyi there.
17.20: Shelmey and Nedbey have risen, and Sunday has gone up on high.
17.21: The Daybreak has left me behind, and the excellencies that brought me here.
17.22: My baptisms are all for nothing, and my signs go unmentioned in my father’s house.
17.23: My lessons and books are forgotten, and my devotionals are useless.
17.24: The secret watchers have abandoned me, and those who brought me here left me behind.”
17.25: When Shem, Noah’s son, had said this, the messenger, his creator, took off and came.
17.26: The great creator went, the savior whom Life had sent.
17.27: He broke open their penitentiaries, and made an opening in their fortress.
17.29: “Why do you weep, Shem, Noah’s son? Like the twinkling of an eye I have come here!
17.30: What have the wicked done to you, and how have the sinners injured you,
17.31: whom all excellencies love, for whom the realm of light is a helper?”
17.32: The chosen ones summon, and instruct the man Shem, saying,
17.33: “What have the wicked done to you, so that your heart became divided,
17.34: and you said, ‘There is no Life, nor is Manda d’Heyyi in light’s place.
17.35: The Lord has abandoned the house, and its architect has risen from it.
17.36: Shelmey and Nedbey have risen, and Sunday has gone up on high.
17.37: My baptisms are forgotten, and my signs go unmentioned in my father’s house.
17.38: My lessons and books are forgotten, and my prayers for each time are held back.
17.39: My prostrations are in vain, and my evening devotionals are useless.
17.40: Life has reckoned me among its numbers and completed its measures for all time.’
17.41: Shem, who said you are captive here, and the wicked bind you in their fortress?
17.42: He whose name is written in the Great Life’s house will not be trapped in the sinners’ abode!
17.43: Everyone who seeks his helper will not be caught in the clutches of wicked mortals.
17.44: He will not go down to the wicked’s penitentiaries, the blazing fire will not consume him.
17.45: Remember us and summon us so we may seek you, come to your side, and set you up in your settlement.
17.46: The Seven who torture you are worthless, but you will rise to the light.
17.48: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

18.1: A child was transplanted from on high, a secret was revealed in Jerusalem.
18.3: An utter silence fell upon the Eulaeus, an utter silence fell upon Jerusalem.
18.4: Early in the morning, he went to the Temple.
18.5: He opened his mouth for evil, and his lying lips.
18.6: He opened his mouth for evil, saying to all the priests,
18.7: “I saw in my night visions, in my vision when I lay down—
18.8: I didn’t sleep, rest or lie down, and sleep did not overtake me in the night.
18.9: I didn’t sleep and I didn’t rest— that a star came to Elizabeth,
18.10: a fire rose, burning over elder father Zechariah,
18.11: three lamps appeared, the sun set and the lamps shined forth.
18.12: A fire hung about the synagogue, and smoke wreathed the Temple.
18.13: A sound rumbled on the chariot, the Earth shook from its place.
18.14: A shooting star burst over Judaea, a shooting star burst over Jerusalem.
18.15: The sun appeared at night, and the moon shined forth during the day.”
18.16: When the priests heard, they tossed dust on their heads.
18.17: The priest Jacob cries, and Benjamin’s tears flow.
18.18: Shiley and Shalbey toss dust on their heads.
18.19: Eleazar opened his mouth, speaking to all the priests,
18.20: “Who holds the Book of Dreams, and upon whom is the Book of Visions bestowed?
18.21: Who holds the Book of Dreams, who interprets for you dreams you have seen?”
18.22: Eleazar opened his mouth, and speaks to all the priests, saying,
18.23: “Jacob interprets dreams, yet he does not understand them.
18.24: Benjamin interprets dreams, but he is not a man who will keep your secrets.
18.25: Tabiomin will not reveal to us what you tell him to say there is or isn’t.”
18.26: All of a sudden, the earth murmurs, and is revealed among the spheres of heaven.
18.27: The earth opens its mouth, and speaks to Eleazar, saying to him,
18.28: “Go to the place of Lilioch, who will interpret for you the dreams you saw.”
18.29: Eleazar opened his mouth, speaking to all of the priests,
18.30: “Who will go to Lilioch, to interpret for you the dreams you saw?”
18.31: They wrote a letter, and put it in Tabiomin’s possession.
18.32: Tabiomin took the letter and went straightaway to Lilioch.
18.33: Lilioch sleeps upon his bed, having not yet broken his sleep.
18.34: There was groaning in his heart, and it broke his heart from its support.
18.35: Tabiomin went over to Lilioch’s side. Tabiomin drew near and went up to Lilioch.
18.36: Rousing him from sleep, Tabiomin told him the dreams the priests saw.
18.37: “[An utter silence fell upon the Karun,] an utter silence fell upon Jerusalem.
18.38: Early in the morning, he went to the Temple.
18.39: He opened his mouth for evil, and his lying lips.
18.40: He opened his mouth, saying to all the priests,
18.41: ‘I saw in my night visions, in my vision when I lay down—
18.42: I didn’t sleep, rest or lie down, and sleep did not overtake me in the night.
18.43: I didn’t sleep and I didn’t rest— I saw a star came upon Elizabeth,
18.44: a fire rose burning upon elder father Zechariah,
18.45: three lamps appeared, the sun set and the lamps shined forth.
18.46: A fire hung about the synagogue, and smoke wreathed the Temple.
18.47: A sound rumbled on the chariot, so that the earth shook from its place.
18.48: A shooting star burst over Judaea, a shooting star burst over Jerusalem.
18.49: The sun appeared in the night and the moon shined forth during the day.’”
18.50: When Lilioch heard so, he tossed dust upon his bare head.
18.51: Lilioch stood up from his bed, and brought forth the Book of Dreams.
18.52: He opens and reads it, seeing what is written within.
18.53: He opens and reads it, and interprets them in his heart but not aloud.
18.54: He writes them in a letter, and explains them in a scroll, saying to them,
18.55: “Woe to you, all you priests, Elizabeth is giving birth to a child!
18.56: Woe to you, rabbis, a child is being born in Jerusalem!
18.57: Woe to you, primary teachers, Elizabeth is giving birth to a child!
18.58: Woe to you, Mistress Torah, Johannes is born in Jerusalem!
18.59: Johannes will take the Jordan, and will be called a prophet in Jerusalem.”
18.60: Lilioch writes them in a letter, and says to them,
18.61: “The star that came and rose over Elizabeth: the child was transplanted from the upper heights,
18.62: and he came and was given to Elizabeth.
18.63: The fire that burns upon elder father Zechariah: Johannes is born in Jerusalem.”
18.64: Tabiomin took the letter and quickly set off for Jerusalem.
18.65: He went and found all the priests sitting mournfully.
18.66: He took the letter and placed it in Eleazar’s hand.
18.67: He opens and reads it, seeing the strange words within it.
18.68: He opens and reads it, seeing what is written inside it.
18.69: He reads it in his mind, but does not explain it to them.
18.70: Eleazar picked it up, and in the hand of elder father Zechariah he placed it.
18.71: He opens and reads it, seeing what is written inside it.
18.72: He reads it in his mind, but does not give any response.
18.73: He picks up the letter and tosses it to Eleazar’s hand.
18.74: Eleazar opened his mouth, and says to elder father Zechariah,
18.75: “Elder father, leave Judaea, lest you cause trouble in Jerusalem.”
18.76: The elder father lifts his right hand, and struck Eleazar on his head.
18.78: “Eleazar of the Great House, head of all priests.
18.79: If you really knew [your mother], you would not be able to go to our synagogue.
18.80: If you really knew [your mother], you would not read the Torah,
18.81: because your mother was an adulteress.
18.82: She was an adulteress, who didn’t remain a virgin for her father-in-law’s house.
18.83: Since your father did not have the zuzim hidden away,
18.84: to write her divorce papers, he should have left her immediately without asking.
18.85: Will there ever be a day I’ll come, look about, and not see Moses, Amram’s son?
18.86: Yes, will there ever be a day I’ll come, and not pray in your congregation,
18.87: that you weren’t set and established, and you’d tell me some word you haven’t heard?
18.88: Can a dead man be brought back to life, if Elizabeth can be pregnant?
18.89: Can a blind man have his sight restored, and can a cripple grow legs,
18.90: and can a deaf mute learn to write, if Elizabeth can be pregnant?
18.91: It has been fully twenty-two years, since I last saw my wife;
18.92: nevertheless, neither I nor any of you, have made Elizabeth pregnant!”
18.93: All the priests started to speak to elder father Zechariah secretly, saying to him:
18.94: “Sit and calm down, elder father, and may the peace of the good be upon you.
18.95: Elder father, if there are no dreams in Judaea, if there are no visions in Jerusalem,
18.96: then all that Moses said is a lie, but on the contrary your word and ours are kept.
18.97: This is a dream that we saw:
18.98: Johannes will take the waters of the Jordan and be called a prophet in Jerusalem.”
18.99: The elder father left their presence, and Eleazar came out after him.
18.100: Three lamps appeared, going away from him.
18.101: They ran and seized him by the shirt, and said to the elder father,
18.102: “Elder father, what’s that in front of you, and what is behind you?”
18.104: “Eleazar of the Great House, head of all the priests,
18.105: I do not know whom the lamps that go in front of me guard.
18.106: I do not know whose is the fire that came behind me.
18.107: Neither I, nor any of you, have made Elizabeth pregnant!”
18.108: All the priests started to chatter about elder father Zechariah, and said to him:
18.109: “Elder father Zechariah, be still and calm and certain,
18.110: that the child that from the upper heights was transplanted and given to you in your old age.
18.111: Johannes is born, will take the Jordan, and be called a prophet in Jerusalem.
18.112: We shall be baptized according to his rite, and we shall be marked with his pure sign.
18.113: We shall take the morsel, drink the spring-water,
18.114: and rise with it to light’s place.”
18.115: All the priests started to chatter about elder father Zechariah,
18.116: “Elder father, let’s talk to you about your home and your ancestors, from whom you came.
18.117: Moses, Amra’s son, was from your clan;
18.118: Shiley and Shelbey came from your clan;
18.119: Abraham and Israel came from your clan;
18.120: Ebney and Benjamin came from your clan;
18.121: Rishey and Rath came from your clan;
18.122: Rishey and Bazrey came from your clan;
18.123: Zackey and Zackuney came from your clan;
18.124: Ramesh and Mahramir came from your clan;
18.125: Rabin and Judah came from your clan;
18.126: the Great Ezra and Razey came from your clan;
18.127: The ones who built the Dome of the Priests,
18.128: and shaped the idols and images within it, they too came from your clan.
18.129: Hanney and Hananiah came from your clan.
18.130: Sab is from your clan. The man who wrote the Torah,
18.131: whose name is the Great Peacock— he came from your clan.
18.132: Ramah and Ishmael came from your clan;
18.133: Rab Hanney and Hananiah came from your clan;
18.134: Benerisa and Ishmael came from your clan;
18.135: Tabiomin and the teachers came from your clan.
18.136: The rulers who were your ancestors are blessed, elder father—
18.137: none of those ones took a wife, or had children except in their old age.
18.138: Each one who had sons, who became prophets in Jerusalem.
18.139: If a prophet is coming from you, then you should take this clan as your own,
18.140: since Johannes is destined to come into being, and be called a prophet in Jerusalem.”
18.141: Eleazar opened his mouth, and spoke to the elder father,
18.142: “Elder father, if Johannes comes into being, and takes the waters of the Jordan,
18.143: I will be his humble servant, baptized with his rite,
18.144: and marked with his pure sign.
18.145: We shall take the morsel, drink the spring-water,
18.146: and rise with it to light’s place.”
18.147: The elder father opened his mouth, and said to all the priests,
18.148: “If the child comes from the upper heights, then what will you do in Jerusalem?
18.149: They brought him from the Jordan’s reservoir, and placed him in Elizabeth’s womb.”
18.150: And Life triumphs, and the man who went here triumphs!
18.151: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.
18.152: John teaches in the night, and says,

19.1: I shine forth in the name of my father, and praise the man, my creator.
19.2: I delivered my soul from the world from the works that are evil and not right
19.3: The Seven question me, the dead who have not seen Life.
19.5: “By whose strength do you stand, and in whose praise do you teach?”
19.7: “In my father’s strength I stand and in praise of the man, my transplanter.
19.8: I have built no house in Judaea, and set no throne in Jerusalem.
19.9: I did not love the rose garland, nor intercourse with lovely women.
19.10: I have not loved defects, nor the intellect that drank wine.
19.11: I did not love physical sustenance, nor has envy found any place with me.
19.12: I have not forgotten my evening devotionals, nor have I forgotten the sublime Jordan.
19.13: I have not forgotten my baptism, nor have I forgotten my pure sign.
19.14: I have not forgotten Sunday, nor has the Daybreak condemned me.
19.15: I have not forgotten Shelmey and Nedbey, whose domain is the house of Greatness.
19.16: They purify me and raise me up, and know that is no flaw or imperfection in me.”
19.17: When John had said this, Life was thoroughly pleased with him.
19.18: The Seven greeted him, and the Twelve bowed before him,
19.19: and said these things to him,
19.20: “Out of all you said, John, you have not lied about anything.
19.21: Your voice is pleasant and lovely, and no one compares to you.
19.22: Beautiful is your speech within your mouth and precious is the word given to you.
19.23: The mantle, which the First Life gave to Adam, the first man,
19.24: the mantle, which the First Life gave to Ram, the man,
19.25: the mantle, which the First Life gave to Shorbey, the man,
19.26: the mantle, which the First Life gave to Shem, Noah’s son,
19.27: he has now given to you, he gave it to you, John,
19.28: so you might rise, and it with you, the house will be left in the shackles.
19.29: All those who are found without sin will rise with you to light’s place.
19.30: All those who are not righteous will be interrogated in the penitentiaries.
19.32: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.
19.33: John teaches in the night and says,
19.34: In the name of the sublime, strange one!

20.1: The sun sat in its seclusion, and the moon reposed in an eclipse.
20.2: The four winds of the house grasp one another’s wings, and breathe not.
20.3: The sun opens his mouth, and says to John in Jerusalem,
20.4: “You have three halos, a crown worth the whole world.
20.5: You have a ship from the perfect, which travels here in the Jordan.
20.6: You have the Greater Pəlugtā, which goes here between the waters.
20.7: If you go to the Great [Life]’s house, remember us before the Great [Life].”
20.8: John opened his mouth, and spoke to the sun in Jerusalem,
20.9: “You have surely requested the halos, and the perfect guard your crown.
20.10: This perfect ship is Glory’s Pride.
20.11: They formed Pəlugtā, which goes between the waters.
20.12: The king’s seal was placed upon her, so she cavorts in your name,
20.13: and goes to the place of dunghills.
20.14: She fights with her own spouse, she seeks her sons but does not find them.
20.15: When her vows were completed and she left, she was not worthy of Life’s house.
20.16: She was not worthy of Life’s house, and was not raised to the everlasting abode.
20.18: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night
20.19: John teaches in the night and says,

21.1: “Did I not go away alone and return? Which prophet is like me,
21.2: and who teaches with my lessons, and who speaks with my sublime voice?”
21.3: When John said so, two women cry:
21.4: Meryey and Elizabeth cry, and the tears of the two women flow.
21.6: “We shall go, and you will stay, see that you do not make us stumble.
21.7: I shall go, and you will stay, see that you do not make me stumble.
21.8: I shall go, and you will stay, see that you do not let grief take me.”
21.9: John opens his mouth, and says to Elizabeth in Jerusalem,
21.10: “Who is there, to replace me on high? Who is there, to replace me in the Great’s house?
21.11: Who is there, to replace me on high, so that you can ransom me?
21.12: If you can ransom me, bring your gems and purchase me.
21.13: If you can ransom me, bring your pearls and purchase me.
21.14: If you can ransom me, bring your gold and purchase me.”
21.15: Elizabeth opens her mouth and speaks to John in Jerusalem,
21.16: “Who is like you in Judaea, and who is like you in Jerusalem,
21.17: so that if I saw him, I’d forget you?”
21.18: “Who is like me? Who is like me,
21.19: that you’d see me, and forget me?”
21.20: From my voice and the sound of my lessons, the Torah has become void in Jerusalem.
21.21: From the sound of their refrains, reciters do not recite in Jerusalem.
21.22: The adulterers forsake their adultery, and women do not go out for tail.
21.23: Brides come in their veils, and their tears reach the earth.
21.24: The child in its mother’s womb hears my voice and weeps.
21.25: Merchants do not trade in Judaea and fishermen do not fish in Jerusalem.
21.26: The women of the sons of Israel do not wear colorful fabrics,
21.27: Brides do not adorn themselves with gold, and ladies do not put on charms.
21.28: These women and men do not see their faces in the mirror.
21.29: At my voice and the sound of my lessons, water rises and stands in a pillar.
21.30: At my voice and the sound of my lessons, fish offered greetings.
21.31: At my voice and the sound of my lessons, winged birds prostrated in worship, and said,
21.32: ‘Blessed are you, indeed blessed are you, John and blessed is the man whom you worship.
21.33: You were saved and you were set free, John, and naked you have left the world behind.
21.34: Women did not seduce you into their adultery, and their words did not panic you.
21.35: You did not forget censers, and incense for your Lord did not leave your mind.
21.36: You did not become drunk with wine, and you did no deeds of abomination.
21.37: Infidelity did not snare you in Jerusalem. You were saved and you were set free,
21.38: and your throne has been set up for you in Life’s house.’”
21.40: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.

22.1: He called out a proclamation to the world, and said,
22.2: “You, who stand in wickedness, come, buy a path before you!
22.3: You, who compound interest upon interest, come, buy a path before you!
22.4: You, who sleep in fragrant wreaths, get up, and buy a path before you!
22.5: You, who wear roses and silk, get up, and buy a path before you!
22.6: You, who are lying down in flattery, get up, and buy a path before you,
22.7: since the righteous elect’s children will rise up, and Life’s voice will not approach the world!
22.8: The ascensions will rise up, but the pure turban will not be confirmed!
22.9: The living baptism will rise up, but the sublime sign will not be there!”
22.10: When John said this, Jacob, Benjamin, and Meryey
22.11: spoke to John in Jerusalem, saying,
22.12: “By Life, whom you worship, John, I ask that you swear,
22.13: Again, I ask that you swear, John, by the Daybreak whose name is dear,
22.14: Will the righteous elect’s children will rise up, and Life’s voice will not approach the world?
22.15: Will the ascensions rise up, but the pure turban will not be confirmed?
22.16: Will the living baptism rise up, but the sublime sign will not be there?”
22.17: When Jacob, Benjamin, and Meryey said this,
