22.18: John spoke to them in Jerusalem, saying,
22.19: “Once the priests are all slaughtered, and are no more, the Israelites will be slain.
22.20: Muhammad the Arab will be born, the adopted son, son of a foresaken son,
22.21: the son of the adopted son, Ishmael, and be called the son of Aminah and Abdallah.
22.22: He will remove all tents, and mosques will increase in the world.
22.23: He will remove stability and peace, and deceit and sin will increase in the world
22.24: He will remove weddings, and invitations from Earth.
22.25: He will remove the faith, and not seclude women in childbirth.
22.26: No a single bell will ring on Earth, none of them will ring.
22.27: They will hate the book of wisdom, so that they bring evil into the world.
22.28: They will hate adultery, but commit adultery, and hate theft, but commit theft,
22.29: and hate usury [and] compound interest, but give one and take nine,
22.30: They pervert their scales, and magnify their weights.
22.31: Some of them shave their heads, and some of them neglect their hair.
22.32: Some of them neglect their hair, and some of them henna their beards.
22.33: Some of them henna their beards, and rise to pray in their mosques.
22.34: When they see a man putting on a girdle, misery covers them from head to toe.
22.35: They start questioning and say, ‘Who is your prophet?
22.36: Tell us, who is your prophet, and tell us, which is your book?
22.37: Tell us, which is your book, and tell us, whom do you worship?’
22.38: They neither know nor understand. Accursed and disgraceful,
22.39: they neither know nor understand, that our Lord is the light king.
22.40: He is the one on high.”
22.42: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night,
22.43: John teaches in the night, and says,

23.1: Beware for me, my brothers, beware for me, my friends,
23.2: beware for me, my brothers, of the pits that women dig.
23.3: all their pits will be filled, and all the pits will become foundations.
23.4: The pits that women dig, will not be closed up for a thousand millennia.
23.5: She who gets polluted but is not made right, the dark mountain will devour her.
23.6: She who gets polluted but is not made right, she will not taste the great Ocean.
23.7: She who gets polluted but is not made right, her skirts will be empty,
23.8: She who gets polluted but is not made right, she will have dead sons.
23.9: She will curse heaven and earth, because she polluted the clear waters,
23.10: and revealed the hidden secrets, brought them out and tossed it on a dunghill,
23.11: The sun and the moon curse with an evil curse.
23.12: When you are sleeping in your beds, toss water on yourselves.
23.13: Before you pour water on yourselves, wash to the top of your heads.
23.14: Since if any hair is left on your heads, then you cannot say,
23.15: “We do wash with water, in this world.”
23.17: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night
23.18: John teaches in the night, and he says,

24.1: “I was in the house of my seclusion,” and he says,
24.2: “I was neither defective nor imperfect and you have not found fault with my mind.
24.3: I was not imprisoned by their works and I did not walk in their way.
24.4: I will call, instruct, and instruct my friends, whose settlements are in the world.
24.5: My chosen, be neither defective nor imperfect, and let there be no deceit in your speech.
24.6: Withdraw from Earth, and from the mortal abode.
24.7: Choose a wife, take a wife, but do not take a wicked girl as a wife.
24.8: A wicked girl, do not take as a wife, lest the fire that blazes burns you.
24.9: She who gets polluted but is not made right, the fire that blazes will burn her.
24.10: She who gets polluted but is not made right, they give her empty arms.
24.11: She who gets polluted but is not made right, she will have dead sons.
24.12: She who gets polluted but is not made right, she will curse heaven and earth,
24.13: because she polluted the clear water, and revealed the hidden secrets,
24.14: and went and threw them on the dung heap.
24.15: The sun has come, and moon has risen upon her, and cursed her with a great curse.
24.16: My chosen, save yourselves from the mortal abode.
24.17: When you approach your wives, wash yourselves in water,
24.18: and purify yourselves from the top of your heads.
24.19: If any hair on your heads is left, then you are still not purified, my brothers.
24.20: Save yourselves from the pits that women dig;
24.21: all their pits will be filled, and all the pits will become foundations.
24.22: The pits that women dig, for a thousand millennia will not be closed up.”
24.24: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night,
24.25: John teaches in the night and says,

25.1: Noble men, who are sleeping, and noble women, who are not awake,
25.2: noble men, who are sleeping, what are you going to do, on judgment day?
25.3: When the soul strips off the body what are you going to do, on judgment day?
25.5: whose men will die, and whose deceitful book will be stopped,
25.6: where is Adam, the first man, who became the head of the generation here?
25.7: Where is Eve, his wife, from whom the world was wakened to life?
25.8: Where is Shitel, Adam’s son, from whom are worlds and generations?
25.9: Where are Ram and Rud, from the age of the sword?
25.10: Where are Shorbey and Sharhabiel from the age of fire?
25.11: Where is Shem, Noah’s son from the age of the flood, of water?
25.12: All of them left and did not return, and watchers were set on Earth,
25.13: looking like the good day upon which ages and generations gaze.
25.14: The planets are fattened cows, as they stand on the day of slaughter:
25.15: The earthlings are fattened rams, as they stand in the markets and are sold.
25.16: May there be mercy upon those who worship Life, may their sins and trespasses be forgiven them.

26.1: The ages took no pleasure in me, and neither did all the worlds.
26.2: The age[s] took no pleasure in me,
26.3: […] in a true letter, which came there.
26.4: They take the letter, and place it in the Jews’ hands.
26.5: They open it, read inside it, and see what’s inside is not what they want,
26.6: and is not what their souls desire.
26.7: They take the letter, and put it in Johannes’s hands.
26.9: “Rab Johannes, take the true letter, which came to you from your ancestors.”
26.10: Johannes opens, reads, and sees within it sublime writing.
26.11: He opens and reads within it, and was filled with Life, and he says,
26.12: “This is what I wished for, and this is what my soul desires.”
26.13: Johannes came forth from his body. His brothers taught the teachings.
26.14: His brothers taught them on the mountain, Mount Carmel.
26.15: They took the letter and took it up the mountain, Mount Carmel.
26.16: They write them by letter, and explain the scroll to them—
26.17: to Jacob, Benjamin and Ishmael, who assemble on the mountain, Mount Carmel.
26.18: […] Manda d’Heyyi, who is far from heaven,
26.19: I have come to you, Soul, whom Life has sent to Earth.
26.20: In whose garb have I come to the world?
26.21: In Life’s garb, I have come to the world!
26.22: I have come to the Seven’s garb, I have come to the Eight.
26.23: There, I took the Seven’s garb, and each of the Eight by hand,
26.24: I took, I am taking, and I will take and not let go.
26.25: I took each, and I will take them, the demons, and they will become virtuous.
26.26: Why do you weep, o ages? Why do you weep, o nations?
26.27: Why does your glory diminish? To you I have brought my likeness,
26.28: I went to the midst of the world.”
26.30: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.
26.31: John teaches in the night, and says:

27.1: “Is there anyone greater than me? My deeds ought to be measured,
27.2: my wages and wreaths ought to be counted, and my praise lifts me up with the joy of my embrace.”
27.3: Jacob has abandoned the synagogue, Benjamin has abandoned the Temple,
27.4: Eleazar of the Great House has abandoned the Dome of the Priests.
27.5: The priests spoke to John in Jerusalem, saying,
27.6: “John, leave our town! Johannes, leave our city!
27.7: The synagogue shook from the sound of your voice, and the Temple shook from the sound of your lessons!
27.8: The Dome of the Priests has shaken from the sound of your refrains!”
27.9: John spoke to the priests in Jerusalem, saying,
27.10: “Bring a fire and burn me, and bring a sword and cut me!”
27.11: The priests spoke to John in Jerusalem, saying,
27.12: “A fire will not burn you, John, since Life’s name is mentioned over you.
27.13: A sword will not cut you, John, since Life’s Son is unleashed upon you.”
27.15: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evening of the nights
27.16: John teaches in the night, and says,

28.1: “Lofty strongholds will fall, and houses that are raised will be destroyed.
28.2: Is there none to whom they say, ‘Have a nice day!’ who would not immediately say, ‘Go to Hell!’
28.4: Jews gathered, and went to John.
28.6: “We ask that you swear, John by the light king whom you worship.
28.7: We ask that you swear, John, by Sunday and the Daybreak,
28.8: whose name is precious and great:
28.9: The one who lapses into adultery, with what will he be tried?
28.10: The one who lapses into theft, with what will he be judged?
28.11: Whoever sleeps with his friend’s wife, with what will he be judged?
28.12: Every man who lets one go and keeps one, with what will he be judged?
28.13: Every woman who commits adultery, with what will he be judged?
28.15: and false astrologers with what will he be judged?
28.16: Everyone who drinks wine in a tavern,
28.17: and commits drunkenness and harm within it, with what will he be judged?
28.18: Everyone who goes to a songstress,
28.20: and she gets pregnant by him, takes poison,
28.21: goes out to the marketplaces, and tosses it,
28.22: and the eyes of the child see its mother,
28.23: but the mother does not see the child, with what will he be judged?
28.24: Everyone who sleeps with his wife,
28.25: and does not wash himself with water, with what will he be judged?
28.26: A woman who does not wash with water, with what will she be judged?
28.27: Everyone who sleeps with his wife,
28.28: that first day when she washes away
28.29: uncleanness and menstruation, with what will he be judged?
28.31: and charges interest on gold and silver, with what will he be judged?
28.32: Everyone who loves gold and silver, with what will he be judged?
28.33: Everyone who loves gold and silver, and does no good with it,
28.34: with what will he be judged?
28.36: but does not mention over it Life’s name, with what will he be judged?
28.37: Everyone who does disgusting deeds, with what will he be judged?
28.38: Everyone who dyes his hand and foot
28.39: and distorts the likeness his Lord ordained, with what will he be judged?
28.40: Everyone who loves colorful fabrics and colors, with what will he be judged?”
28.41: When the Jews said this, John cried out with a loud cry, and said,
28.42: “God forbid that the great and mighty light should seek a garment from the dregs!
28.43: Everyone who lapses into adultery, his trial will be in the fire.
28.44: Everyone who lapses into theft, will be bound in the dark mountain.
28.45: Everyone who sleeps with his friend’s wife, his trial will be in the fire,
28.47: Everyone who sleeps with a widow should be bound in the dark mountain.
28.48: Everyone who sleeps with [an unmarried] bride, will be tortured to his limit by twin wheels,
28.50: Everyone who abandons one and takes another will be tortured in the fire-pots.
28.51: The woman who commits adultery will become kindling for an oven,
28.52: and should not behold Life’s house.
28.53: Everyone who goes to fortune-tellers, and false astrologers,
28.54: will be tortured in vessels of ice.
28.55: Everyone who drinks wine in a tavern, and gets drunk,
28.56: engaging in drums, revelry, and whoring within it,
28.57: they should tear him apart with asphalt rakes, and he should not behold Abator.
28.58: Everyone who goes to a songstress and sows his illegitimate seed,
28.59: and she gets pregnant by him, takes poison, goes out to the dung heap, puts it down,
28.60: and digs a hole and buries it, and with her heel she tramples it,
28.61: and the eyes of the child see its mother but the mother does not see the child.
28.62: The child will die in the dung heap, and its mother will weep secretly for it.
28.63: She will be interrogated in that penitentiary of the enraged and furious dogs.
28.64: She should be interrogated [in that penitentiary of] the deaf and mute,
28.65: and she should not behold Abator, and her name should be erased from Life’s house.
28.66: Everyone who approaches his wife, and does not wash in water,
28.67: will dwell in the bowels of Leviathan.
28.68: The woman, who does not wash in water, should be beaten with blow upon blow,
28.69: and the pure name should curse her, and there will be no final release for her.
28.70: Light’s watcher should strike her, and her name should be erased from Life’s house.
28.71: The man who sleeps with his wife, that first day when she washes away
28.72: uncleanliness and menstruation, they should raise him into clouds of darkness.
28.73: Everyone who practices usury, and charges interest on gold and silver,
28.74: They should raise him into the dark mountain.
28.75: Everyone who loves gold and silver, and does no good within it,
28.76: should die twice instead of once, and get cut off.
28.77: Everyone who breathes in Life’s scent and does not mention Life’s name over it
28.78: should be interrogated in Abator’s house.
28.79: Everyone who does disgusting deeds, will be taken by the Seven’s sword and blade.
28.80: Everyone who dyes his hands and feet, and distorts the likeness his Lord ordained,
28.81: He will hold the coals in his hand, and he will kindle the flame with his lips.
28.82: He will seek death but not die.
28.83: Life will not approach him, and neither let him die,
28.84: nor relieve him from his suffering to rise to see light’s place.
28.85: He has not been condemned in sin’s abode, because of the baptism he received.
28.86: Everyone who loves colorful fabrics and colors will be clothed in darkness.
28.87: They will cover him with gloomy shrouds, and put blazing sandals on his feet.
28.88: Darkness goes out before him, and gloom comes after him.
28.89: He will have demons beside him, because he loved colors and colorful fabrics
28.90: He will be bound in the penitentiary until his spirit becomes perfect.”
28.91: To you I am speaking and explaining, the souls of my righteous elect who testify to Life.
28.92: Do not do disgusting deeds, lest you sink to darkness’ place.
28.93: The victorious Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs,
28.94: so that those who love them are not condemned, and Life triumphs!
28.95: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified.
28.96: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evening of the night,
28.97: John teaches in the night, and says,

29.1: “I shine with the name of my father, I shine and enlighten,
29.2: in praise of the man, my creator.
29.3: I am delivered from Earth, from the mortal abode,
29.4: from the eye that winks, from the lips that speak deceit.
29.5: Our Lord, see us, deliver us, and rescue us from hateful and improper deeds!
29.6: Beware for me, my brothers! Beware for me, my friends!
29.7: Beware for me, my brothers, from hateful and improper deeds!
29.8: Beware for me, my disciples! Be gentle and meek.
29.9: Love Sunday, and honor the Daybreak.
29.10: Give rewards, more precious than wife or children.
29.11: Wages and rewards ought to be sought on the road, like a hand that provides for the mouth.
29.12: Wages and rewards ought to be sought on the road, like a blind person that seeks a guide.
29.13: For the one who has no wages or rewards, no cable is stretched across the rivers.
29.14: For the one who has no wages or rewards, there is no crossing upon the sea.
29.15: For the one who has no wages or rewards, he will not behold Abator.
29.16: Woe to the evil and deceitful ones, who forgot rewards and did not give them!
29.17: They forgot and did not give rewards, and they forgot the man who saves them.
29.18: My chosen! Love rewards and love Sunday, so that a crossing may be put upon the sea.
29.19: May a crossing be put upon the sea, and a thousand thousands stand on the shore.
29.20: On the shore a thousand thousands stand, and out of a thousand he carries across one.
29.21: One he carries across out of a thousand! Out of two thousand, he will carry two.
29.22: He carries the souls who are worthy and deserving to light’s place.”
29.23: May your name be praised, my Lord, the light that won’t condemn whoever loves his name.
29.24: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.
29.25: John teaches in the night, and says, “May splendor shine upon the worlds!”

30.1: Who told Jesus? Who told Jesus Christ, Mary’s son?
30.2: Who told Jesus, so he came to the Jordan’s banks, and told him,
30.3: “John, perform your baptism over me, and pronounce over me the name you pronounce!
30.4: If I become your disciple, then I shall mention you in my epistle.
30.5: If I do not become your disciple, then erase my name from your scroll!’”
30.6: John spoke, saying to Jesus Christ in Jerusalem,
30.7: “You have lied to Jews, and you have deceived men, the priests.
30.8: You cut seed off from men, and labor and pregnancy from women.
30.9: You loosened the Sabbath that Moses ordained in Jerusalem.
30.10: You lied to them with a horn and played different things with a trumpet.”
30.11: Jesus Christ spoke, saying to John in Jerusalem,
30.12: “If I have lied to Jews, then may a burning fire consume me.
30.13: If I have deceived the men, the priests, then may I die two deaths instead of one.
30.14: If I have cut seed off from men, then may I not pass the great Ocean.
30.15: If I have cut labor and pregnancy from women, then may a judge be established in my presence.
30.16: If I have undone the Sabbath, then may a burning fire consume me.
30.17: If I have lied to Jews, then may my path be through thistle and thorn.
30.18: If I played different things with a trumpet, then let my eyes not fall on Abator.
30.19: As for you, baptize me with your rite, and pronounce over me the name you pronounce!
30.20: If I become your disciple, then I shall mention you in my epistle.
30.21: If I do not become your disciple, then erase my name from your scroll!”
30.22: John spoke, saying to Jesus Christ in Jerusalem,
30.23: “A deaf man will not become a scribe, and a blind man will not write a letter.
30.24: A ruined house will not prosper, and a widow will not become a bride.
30.25: Putrid waters will not become pleasant, and a stone will not get wet in oil.”
30.26: Jesus Christ spoke, saying to John in Jerusalem,
30.27: “A deaf man will become a scribe, and a blind man will write a letter.
30.28: A ruined house will prosper, and a widow will become a bride.
30.29: Putrid waters will become pleasant, and a stone will get wet in oil.”
30.30: John spoke, saying to Jesus Christ in Jerusalem,
30.31: “If you can give an explanation of this to me, then you are a wise messiah.”
30.32: Jesus Christ spoke to John in Jerusalem, and said,
30.33: A mute person becomes a scribe: an offspring that comes from a woman in labor,
30.34: grows up and becomes big, and sets up wages and rewards.
30.35: Wages and rewards, he sets up, and he rises to see light’s place.
30.36: A deaf person writes a letter: A wicked man became a good man.
30.37: He forsook adultery and forsook theft, and believed in the Mighty Life.
30.38: A ruined house prospers: A nobleman who became humbled
30.39: forsook his roots and passions, and built a house by the sea.
30.40: By the sea, he built a house, and he opened two doors in it.
30.41: Whoever comes down, he brought him, opened the door for him, and welcomed him.
30.42: Whoever comes up, he brought him, opened the door for him, and welcomed him.
30.43: If he wants to eat, then he sets him a dish in Truth.
30.44: If he seeks to drink, then he mixes him a cup of juice.
30.45: If he wants to sleep, then he spreads out a bed for him in Truth.
30.46: If he wants to go, then he guides him on a path of Truth―
30.47: He guides him on a path of Truth and faith, and he rises to see light’s place.
30.48: A widow who becomes a bride: A woman who was a widow from her youth
30.49: grasped her skirts and settled down, until she raises her son.
30.50: When she goes to a groom, she will not dishonor her late husband.
30.51: Putrid waters which become pleasant: A prostitute, who becomes a lady,
30.52: goes up to town and goes down from town and the veil is not removed from her face.
30.53: A stone gets wet in oil: A pagan, who came down from the mountains,
30.54: forsook sorceries and forsook witchcraft, and came to believe in the Mighty Life.
30.55: He found an orphan, an old man, and filled the arms of a widow.
30.56: And you, John, baptize me with your rite, and pronounce over me the name you pronounce!
30.57: If I become your disciple, then I shall mention you in my epistle.
30.58: If I do not become your disciple, then erase my name from your scroll!”
30.59: You will be held responsible for your sin, and I shall be held responsible for mine.”
30.60: When Jesus Christ said this, a letter came from Abator’s house,
30.61: “John, baptize the deceiver in the Jordan!
30.62: Bring him down to the Jordan to baptize him, bring him up to the bank to confirm him!”
30.63: Spirit took the form of a dove, and made a cross in the Jordan.
30.64: She made a cross in the Jordan, and lifted up the waters in every way,
30.66: “Jordan, you will make me holy, and you make my seven sons holy!”
30.67: The Jordan in which the Christ is baptized, I have made into a blank of the font!
30.68: The morsel which the Christ takes, I have made into a blank of the Eucharist!
30.69: The spring-water which Christ takes, I have made into a blank of the Eucharist!
30.70: The turban which the Christ takes, I have made into a blank of the priesthood!
30.71: The staff which the Christ takes I have made into a blank of the crozier!”
30.72: Beware for me, my brothers, beware for me, my friends,
30.73: Beware for me the Romans, who are like offshoots of the cross
30.74: that they fix on the walls, and begin to worship the crucifix.
30.75: Beware for me, my brothers, the god framed by a carpenter!
30.76: If a carpenter framed a god, then who framed the carpenter?
30.77: And Life is praised, and Life triumphs!
30.78: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night
30.79: John teaches in the night, and says,

31.1: The spheres and the chariot trembled, the sun and the moon wept,
31.2: tears fell from Spirit’s eyes, and they said,
31.3: “John, you are like a parched mountain, that does not bring forth a blossom on Earth.
31.4: You are like a dried-up riverbed, in which plants are not planted.
31.5: You are like a ruined house, which all who see it fear.
31.6: [You are] a land without a ruler, you are a house without form.
31.7: You will be a wrongful prophet, after whom none is left to mention his name.
31.8: Who will prepare and provide for you, John? Who will go after you to the graveyard?”
31.9: When John had heard so, a tear formed in his eye―
31.10: in his eye, a tear formed, and he says,
31.11: “It would be pleasant to take a wife and precious to produce sons,
31.12: but what if I take a wife and sleep comes, and lust enflames me,
31.13: and I spoil my nightly devotions?
31.14: What if, being enflamed with lust, I put my lord out of my mind?
31.15: What if lust enflames me, and I spoil my devotionals all the time?”
31.16: When John said so, a letter came from Abator’s house,
31.17: “John, take a wife and get established, and see that you attend to Earth.
31.18: Monday morning and Tuesday morning― see to your marital bed!
31.19: Wednesday morning, and Tuesday morning― undertake your sublime devotions!
31.20: Friday morning and Saturday morning― see to your marital bed!
31.21: Sunday morning and the Daybreak― undertake your sublime devotions
31.22: on Sunday take three, and leave three,
31.23: take three and leave three, and see that you attend to Earth.
31.24: They gave a wife to John, from you, the people of the city of Truth!
31.25: From the first pregnancy were Handan and Steady.
31.26: From the middle pregnancy were Behram and Lovelife.
31.27: From the last pregnancy were Plant, Sam, Splendid Anhar, and Steady.
31.28: These three pregnancies occurred within you, the ruins of Jerusalem.
31.29: John opened his mouth, and spoke to Anhar in Jerusalem,
31.30: “You will teach your daughters, lest they perish,
31.31: and I shall instruct and explain to my sons lest they are hindered.”
31.32: Anhar opened her mouth and spoke to John in Jerusalem.
31.34: “I gave birth to sons on Earth― I did not give birth to [their] heart on Earth.
31.35: If they become disciples, they will rise to light’s place;
31.36: If they do not become disciples, a burning fire will consume them.”
31.37: John opened his mouth and said to Anhar in Jerusalem,
31.38: “When I depart from Earth, tell me, what will you do after me?”
31.40: “I shall not eat and I shall not drink until I see you.”
31.41: “Anhar, you have told a lie, and your speech has gone deceitful!
31.42: When a day has come and gone, You will eat and you will drink
31.43: and you will put me out of your mind. I ask you by the Great Life
31.44: and by the Daybreak, whose name is precious:
31.45: When I depart from Earth, tell me, what will you do after me?”
31.47: “I shall not wash and will not comb, until I see you.”
31.48: “Again you have told a lie, Anhar, and your speech has gone deceitful!
31.49: When a month has come and gone, you will wash and you will comb,
31.50: and you will put me out of your mind.
31.51: Again I ask you, Anhar, by the marital bed in which the two of us slept:
31.52: When I depart from my body, tell me, what will you do after me?”
31.54: “I shall not put on new clothes, until I see you.”
31.55: “Again you have told a lie, Anhar, and your speech has gone deceitful!
31.56: When a year has come and gone, you will put on new clothes,
31.57: and you will put me out of your mind.”
31.59: “How you speak to me, John, and how you strike at my whole body!
31.60: When you go, when will you come back, so that my eyes can fall upon yours?”
31.61: “When the living lie down in Sheol, and a bell is hung at the graveyard,
31.62: and they trace a circle in Sheol, and go out and water the graveyard,
31.63: when a bride gets married in Sheol, and her bridal bed is spread in the graveyard,
31.64: when groomsmen make pledges in Sheol, and the dowry will be in the graveyard.”
31.65: She says to him, “How, my lord, will this be?
31.66: When will the living sleep in Sheol, and a bell is hung at the graveyard,
31.67: and they trace a circle in Sheol, and they go out and water the graveyard?
31.68: When will a bride get married in Sheol, and her bridal bed is spread in the graveyard?
31.69: When will groomsmen make pledges in Sheol, and the dowry will be in the graveyard?”
31.71: “As you know, it will not be so. So why did you ask me when I shall come back?
31.72: I shall go and not come back. Blessed is the day that you see me!
31.73: If there were going away and returning, there would not be a widow in the world.
31.74: If there were going away and returning, there would not be orphans in the world.
31.75: If there were going away and returning, there would not be rabbis and teachers in the world.
31.76: If there were going away and returning, there would not be Nazoreans in the world.”
31.77: Anhar opened her mouth, and spoke to John in Jerusalem,
31.78: “I shall lavish you with a vault, and assemble a coffin for you in the graveyard.”
31.79: John opens his mouth, and speaks to Anhar in Jerusalem,
31.80: “Why are you lavishing me with a vault, and assembling a coffin in the graveyard,
31.81: so convinced that I’ll return that you say, ‘The dust won’t fall on him, I’ll lavish him with a vault.’
31.82: Go, give me some bread! As for the coffin you make in the graveyard,
31.84: Anhar opens her mouth, and speaks to John in Jerusalem:
31.85: “You will depart and forget me, and I shall be cut off in the sinful abode!”
31.86: “If it is you that I forget, I shall forget the everlasting abode.
31.87: If it is you that I forget, my eyes will not fall upon Abator.
31.88: When I rise to Life’s house, let your mourning be in the graveyard.”
31.89: And Life is praised, and Life triumphs!
31.90: John teaches in the night, Johannes in the evenings of the night
31.91: John teaches in the night, and says,

32.1: “The spheres and the chariot trembled, Earth and the heavens wept,
32.2: and tears flowed from the clouds.”
32.4: “My father was 99 years old, and my mother was 88 years old.
32.5: They brought me from the reservoir of the Jordan;
32.6: They took me, raised me, brought me, and placed me in Elizabeth’s womb,”
32.8: “Nine months I dwelt in her womb, just like all infants do,”
32.10: “No wise woman birthed me in Judaea, and my umbilical cord was not cut in Jerusalem.
32.11: They made for me no fake image, and they did not hang a wicked bell for me.
32.12: I came into being from Elizabeth, in Jerusalem the city quaked.
32.13: Jerusalem City quaked, so that the Wailing Wall was shaken.
32.14: Eleazar of the Great House, stood, and his whole body shook.
32.15: Jews gathered, and came to elder father Zechariah.
32.17: “Elder father Zechariah, it is necessary that you have a son.
32.18: Tell us, what name shall we give him?
32.19: If we give him ‘Wise Joseph,’ then will he teach the book in Jerusalem?
32.20: If we give him ‘Zatan the Pillar,’ then will Jews trust him and not accuse him of deceit?”
32.21: When Elizabeth heard, she spoke up. she cried out, saying,
32.22: “From all these names that you have said,
32.23: I do not desire to give him a single one No, I only want to give him the name
32.24: John-Johannes, which Life gave to him.”
32.25: When the Jews heard, they were filled with a wicked fury against her.
32.27: “What harm shall we do to him and his mother, so he might be slain by our own hands?”
32.28: Hearing this, Excellent Ennosh took him, and brought him to Parwan, the white mountain,
32.29: On Mount Parwan, where infants and children are raised on spring-water,
32.31: I learned all of my wisdom, and perfected all of my words.
32.32: They dressed me in garments of splendor, and covered me in a tunic of clouds.
32.33: They tied a girdle around me, a girdle of clear and shining water.
32.34: They sat me entirely in a cloud, a splendid cloud,
32.35: and on the seventh hour of Sunday, they brought me up to the city of Jerusalem.
32.36: A clamor of war in Judaea, A proclamation of war in Jerusalem!
32.38: “Who had a son and he was stolen away? Who made a vow and elevated it?
32.39: Who had a son and he was stolen away? That one has arrived, and she will seek her son.
32.40: Who told Battay, who instructed Battay,
32.41: Who told Battay, to go to Elizabeth and tell her,
32.42: “A child is coming to Judaea, a prophet is coming to Jerusalem!
32.43: A child is coming to Judaea, a guide is standing with him.
32.44: His mouth resembles yours, and his lips those of elder father Zechariah, his father.
32.45: His eyes resemble yours, and his eyebrows, elder father Zechariah, his father.
32.46: His nose resembles yours, and his hands, elder father Zechariah, his father.”
32.47: Hearing this, Elizabeth went out without a veil.
32.48: Seeing this, elder father Zechariah wrote her divorce papers.
32.49: The sun muttered from in the sky, and the moon from amidst the stars
32.50: The sun opened his mouth, and spoke to the elder father in Jerusalem,
32.51: “Elder father Zechariah, the great dotard whose reason has aged and gone,
32.52: like an Arab whose fate has abandoned him.
32.53: A child is coming to Judaea, a prophet is coming to Jerusalem!
32.54: A child is coming to Judaea, and yet you divorce Elizabeth?
32.55: When the child saw the woman, they disembarked down from the clouds.
32.56: They disembarked down from the clouds, and he kisses Elizabeth’s mouth.
32.57: Seeing this, Excellent Ennosh said to John in Jerusalem,
32.58: “What is written to you, John, and explained to you in your scroll,
32.59: to kiss a Jewish woman on her mouth?”
32.60: John speaks and says to Excellent Ennosh in Jerusalem,
32.61: “Nine months I dwelt in her womb, just like all infants do,
32.62: It wasn’t hard for her, now it isn’t hard for me to kiss a Jewish woman on her mouth.
32.63: Even so, let there be kindness upon kindness to the man who repays his father and mother.
32.64: The man who repays his father and mother, there is none like him in the world.”
32.65: When John said this, Excellent Ennosh knew that John was wise.
32.66: Excellent Ennosh spoke to the sun in Jerusalem, saying
32.67: “I kept the child safe, the man sent by an angel.
32.68: I kept the child safe, as long as we desired it.”
32.69: Excellent Ennosh spoke to the moon in Jerusalem, saying
32.70: “I kept the child safe, the man sent by an angel.
32.71: I kept the child safe, so long as we desired it.”
32.72: The victorious Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
32.73: John preaches at night, Johannes in the evenings of the night.
32.74: John preaches in the night, and says, “Do I not stand alone?”

33.1: At my voice, spheres shake, and chariots are overturned,
33.2: the storm grows silent, and settles down in the world’s wastelands,
33.3: the sun and the moon weep, and earth and heaven mourn.
33.4: Christ opened his mouth, and said to John in Jerusalem,
33.5: “I hereby ask you, John, by the Great Life and Sunday, whose name is precious,
33.6: I hereby ask you, John, by the way the righteous elect go, without being held back,
33.7: Tell me, the form of Sowriel’s knife, what does it look like?
33.8: When the soul leaves the body, tell me, with what is it dressed,
33.9: and what does it resemble within the mortal body?
33.10: Is the soul therefore not like the blood that warms the body and gets blocked within it?
33.11: Is the soul therefore not like the wind, which goes in the mountains, and gets blocked there?
33.12: Is the soul therefore not like the dew, which falls on the fruit and gets lost?”
33.13: When Christ said this, John cried out, tears come to him without ceasing,
33.15: “May the lofty king of light forbid a share to the dregs!
33.16: The soul is not like blood, which heats up the body and gets blocked.
33.17: The soul is not like the dew, which falls on the fruit and gets lost.
33.18: The soul is not like the wind, which goes to the mountains and gets blocked.
33.19: The soul is tightly wrapped and brought into the mortal body.
33.20: When the soul is yielded, it rises up in a splendid garment.”
33.21: As for Sowriel’s knife, there are three flames.
33.22: When he hurries to take her away, he releases the three flames against her.
33.23: One he releases against them in the evening, the other at the cock’s crow,
33.24: the third flame he releases against them at the coming of the rays.
33.25: When the fire burns, the soul slips out from the feet and knees.
33.26: From the feet and knees she slips, and she draws near the hip.
33.27: She slips from the hip, and comes forth. She grabs onto the heart.
33.28: Then, she falls on the breasts, and presses until she is weaned.
33.29: The eyes, face and lips shrink, and the tongue rolls back and forth.
33.30: Sowriel sits on her eyebrows. He says to her,
33.31: “Leave, soul! Why do you still guard the body?”
33.33: “If you would take me out of my body, Sowriel, then show me my robe,
33.34: dress me, take me out, and bring me.”
33.36: “First bring me your works, and your labor, then I shall show you your clothes and clothe you.”
33.38: “I did not know, Sowriel, that my time is coming,
33.39: and you are quickly sending for me, so I could do good works,
33.40: so you might bring forth my robe and clothe me within it.”
33.42: “Has no one died before you, and was no one carried out to the cemetery?”
33.44: “By the power of those dead before me, and the power of those taken to the cemetery.
33.45: The crying women and wailing men trembled, as the body was laid before them.
33.46: When the soul leaves the body, four go out to the graveyard.
33.47: The crying women and wailing men trembled, the shouting men shook until they laid it in the shaft.
33.48: They laid down and buried the mortal body, and the women rested from mourning.
33.49: They filled the shaft, and the grief-stricken men rose up.
33.50: The grief-stricken quickly left behind the body and the grave.
33.51: They came, grabbed a cup, ate some bread, and forgot about the mortal body.
33.52: Now, Sowriel, if you want, let me stay here for two days,
33.53: I shall sell all my possessions and distribute them among my children,
33.54: and I shall take my clothing with me, the garment that rises up to light’s place.”
33.56: “Has there ever been a child who left his mother’s body,
33.57: but was brought back to his mother, such that I would leave you in the wicked’s abode,
33.58: so you can divide things among your children? I shall carry you out of here,
33.59: so put on the robe of darkness,
33.60: since neither you were careful on Earth nor did you love your path to light’s place.
33.61: You will be held in the house of the wicked, until heaven and earth come to nought.”
33.63: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

34.1: Meryey am I, daughter of Babylon’s kings, daughter of Jerusalem’s mighty rulers.
34.2: Jews gave birth to me, and priests nurtured me.
34.3: They carried me in their hems, and brought me up to the disturbed house, the Temple.
34.4: Adunay placed into my hands and my two arms a burden.
34.5: I sweep and wash the house in which there is no stability,
34.6: no support for the poor, and no refreshment for tortured souls.
34.7: My father went out to the synagogue, and my mother went out to the Temple
34.8: As my father went out, he told me, and as mother went out, she ordered me,
34.9: “Meryey, shut your inner doors, and fasten the bolts on them,
34.10: See that you not go out to the royal markets, and my lord’s sun[light] doesn’t fall upon you.”
34.11: I heeded not what my mother told me, Meryey, and heard not what my father ordered my ear.
34.12: I opened the inner doors and left open the outer ones.
34.13: I went out to the royal markets and my lord’s sun[light] fell upon me.
34.14: I wanted to go to the synagogue, but my way took me to the tent house.
34.15: I went and found my brothers and sisters as they stood and taught.
34.16: My brothers taught lessons, and my sisters sung refrains.
34.17: With the sound of their lessons, and the sound of their refrains,
34.18: I settled down and slept on my spot.
34.19: My brothers went and did not wake me, and my sisters went and did not rouse me.
34.20: You, my Truth sister, woke me from my sleep,
34.23: Before the day dawns, and before the rooster crows!
34.24: Before the sun shines, and its splendor rises above the worlds!
34.25: Before the priests and priests’ sons go out, and sit in the shadow of Jerusalem’s ruin!
34.26: Before your physical father comes, and heaps a disgrace on you that isn’t yours!”
34.27: I, Meryey, conceal my petitions, and hide my refrains.
34.28: The day dawned early, The rooster crowed early,
34.29: The sun shone on it early, and its splendor shone upon the worlds.
34.30: The priests and priests’ sons went out, and sat in the shadow of Jerusalem’s ruin.
34.31: Then my physical father came, and heaped a disgrace on me that isn’t mine,
34.33: “Where did you come from, horny goat, on whom the bars and bolts are not drawn?
34.34: Where did you come from, bitch in heat, whose pegs and leashes are not secure?
34.35: Where did you come from, piece of sackcloth, which is patched onto my robe?”
34.36: “If I am a horny goat, then I’ll tear down your bars and bolts!
34.37: If I am a bitch in heat, then I’ll strike down the pegs and leashes!
34.38: If I am a fragment of sackcloth that is patched on your robe,
34.39: then cut me from your robe!”
34.42: who has forsaken Judaism, and went to love her lord.
34.44: who has left colorful fabrics and colors, and went to love her lord.
34.45: She has forsaken gold and silver, and went to love her lord!
34.46: She has forsaken phylacteries, and went to love a man in a turban!”
34.48: “God forbid I love whom I hate. God forbid I should hate whom I love.
34.49: God forbid I should hate my lord, Manda d’Heyyi, who is my support in the world.
34.50: In the world, he is my support, and a helper in light’s place.
34.51: Let there be dust in the mouth of the Jews, and ashes in the mouths of all the priests!
34.52: Let there be dung beneath horses’ feet for the master of the mighty rulers of Jerusalem!”
34.53: The victorious Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
34.54: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

35.1: Meryey am I, a vine, a tree standing at the mouth of the Euphrates.
35.2: The tree’s leaves are sweets, and pearls are the tree’s fruit.
35.3: The vine’s fruit is splendor, and its leaves are precious light.
35.4: It spreads its scent among the trees and went out into all worlds.
35.5: Birds smell it in the air. A flock landed in the tree.
35.6: Upon the tree a flock landed, and they seek to build their nest there.
35.7: They shelter in it and do not keep still.
35.8: They eat what falls from its branches, and from within it they drink juice.
35.9: They eat what was not reprehensible, and drink what was not fermented.
35.10: While the birds sit in the vine, winds and storms broke loose.
35.11: They shook the good birds, they battered the tree,
35.12: they made the vine’s leaves fall on all sides, and chased the birds away from their place.
35.13: There were many birds who do not fly off, but clung tightly with their claws and wings,
35.14: and held on until the winds and storms pass.
35.15: There were those who did not hold firmly, and some of their families went off.
35.16: Woe to them that do not hold fast, but are dashed from the tree and flew away!
35.17: How lovely is Life’s tree, and how lovely are the birds within it!
35.18: The winds and storms pass over them, and calm came over the world.
35.19: As the birds sit and twitter, and seek to build nests upon it,
35.20: so the birds can settle upon the vine, an eagle circles and flies around.
35.21: A white [eagle] came to look, and saw the birds. It circled and flapped its wings,
35.22: and came to sit upon the tree. The birds spoke with it, and said to it,
35.24: In this tree there are birds, so many to be without number,
35.25: but winds broke loose upon them, and angry storms came to the tree.
35.26: They shook them from the tree, until their wings are torn off.
35.27: There were some who held fast. The winds and storms didn’t uproot them.
35.28: There were some who flew off quickly.
35.29: We say to you, eagle, we ask you about the birds,
35.30: since you are one that travels around, so you have seen everything on Earth.
35.31: Those birds, our brothers, what have the winds and storms done to them?
35.32: What will you take to them?”
35.34: “Do not seek to see, my brothers what becomes of those birds.
35.35: Clay bullets tore them from me, and broke the wings they had,
35.36: and they were torn off and broken, and went to rest upon the banks.
35.37: A vulture and a hawk circled around them, tore pieces from their flesh,
35.38: and ate from the fattened ones.
35.39: Woe to them, whose lot was the water, they (now) belong to the passage.
35.40: Blessed are you, birds, who held onto this vine!
35.41: You became a companion for Meryey, the vine standing at the mouth of the Euphrates.
35.42: Look, and you will discover, birds, that I have come into your midst.
35.43: I came to my brothers, to be a support for them on Earth.
35.44: I came to heal Meryey, and bring water to the good plants
35.45: and precious vines, which stand at the mouth of the Euphrates,
35.46: I draw water in a white pitcher, and water my plants.
35.47: I carry and hold in splendor’s arms, which are my own.
35.48: I carry, hold, and drink. Blessed is he who drank from my water.
35.49: He drinks, finds healing and endurance, and grows two-fold.
35.50: The vines that drink my water, they have produced good fruit.
35.52: The vines that do not drink the water produce bitter fruit and brambles.
35.53: Woe to those who do not go on their way, and woe to those who do not pass a milestone!
35.54: They hated Life’s Treasure, Meryey, the precious Truth.
35.55: My brothers! Hold strong, and be a companion to Meryey,
35.56: whom I seek within the world, calling forth with Life’s voice,
35.57: and rousing and awakening the sleeping!”
35.58: The eagle flew away from the tree. It circles around and taught its friends,
35.60: “My brothers, hear my voice! Hold on and endure the persecution!
35.61: Be a companion to Meryey! For Meryey, be a companion!
35.62: Woe to the Jews, who brought persecution upon Meryey!
35.63: Woe to Eleazar of the Great House, the pillar that supports the Temple!
35.64: Woe to the pillar Zatan, who spreads lies concerning Meryey!”
35.65: All the Jews gathered together, the teachers, the great, and the small,
35.66: they came and said about Meryey,
35.67: “She ran away from the priests, loved a man,
35.68: and they took one another by the hand. By the hand, they took one another,
35.69: went and sat at the mouth of the Euphrates.
35.70: We seek to kill them, and despise Meryey in Jerusalem.
35.71: We shall make gallows for the man who ruined Meryey, and led her away.
35.72: There will be no day on Earth, in which strangers enter Jerusalem.
35.73: They will break open their dovecotes, and capture Jerusalem’s doves.”
35.74: All the Jews gathered around, and went after Meryey.
35.75: They went and found Meryey a throne was set for her at the Euphrates’ mouth.
35.76: A white banner was spread over her, and a scroll was spread across her lap.
35.77: She reads in the truthful books, and she stirs up all worlds.
35.78: A staff of water is held in her hand, a girdle is fastened around her waist.
35.79: Meryey prays in humility, and she preaches in a sublime voice.
35.80: The fish assemble from the sea, and the birds from the Euphrates’ mouth.
35.81: They come after Meryey’s voice, and have no desire to sleep.
35.82: They inhale the scent which is before her, and forget this world.
35.83: When they saw this, the Jews stood up before her.
35.84: Ashamed, they clenched their fists, struck the front of their breasts, and wept.
35.85: Meryey’s mother spoke, and tears fell upon her chest,
35.87: “Look at me, my daughter Meryey! Look at me, I am your mother!
35.88: You are my daughter, and the daughter of all the head priests,
35.89: [your] head is the great head of the Temple.
35.90: Do you not recall, Meryey, that the Torah was in your bosom,
35.91: you opened it, and read it, and knew what was written within it.
35.92: The outer keys were in your hands, while you put the inner ones in a chest.
35.93: All the priests and sons of priests came and kissed your hands.
35.94: If you wanted, he would open the door, and if you didn’t want he would return to his place.
35.95: A thousand would stand up, and two thousand would sit down.
35.96: They would submit to you like a castrated slave, and listen to your words in Jerusalem.
35.97: Why have you forgotten your brothers, and why is your heart estranged from the priests?
35.98: See, the brides are weeping in Judaea, and the women and men in Jerusalem?
35.99: They are removing their precious gold, and taking up mourning and wailing about you.
35.101: ‘We shall not destroy our possessions, until Meryey comes.
35.102: We shall crush gold with weights, and place desirable silks in baskets.
35.103: We will stand upon the rooftops, waiting to see you in Jerusalem.
35.104: We will make vows to you, if you come with me and we go.’
35.105: My daughter! Get up and come back to the city of Jerusalem.
35.106: Come, light the lamps which have stood unused since the day you left.
35.107: Do not wish for this man, who captivated you and carried you off
35.108: The man who is not from your town, leave him behind in the world,
35.109: lest he say, ‘I went and brought Meryey from her place.’
35.110: Come, teach the children, open it up and put it [in your bosom].
35.111: From the moment and day you hung it up, the dust has been its cover.
35.112: Shake it off, put it in your bosom, and let us hear your voice as it was.”
35.113: When Meryey heard this from her mother, she laughed and rejoiced in her mind,
35.116: Are Jews not those who stand and bow to a vault?
35.117: They shall be buried in darkness.”
35.119: “Go away! Go away, disgusting fools, you are not from the world.
35.120: I am not a woman to chase tail, and it is not that I love a man.
35.121: I did not leave to return to you, and see you, wicked skullcaps.
35.122: Go away! Go away from before me, who gave false witness against me!
35.123: You claimed adultery and theft against me, and made as if I were your equal.
35.124: Blessed is the man who freed me from my chains, and planted my feet here!
35.125: I did not commit adultery with him, and I did not commit theft in the world.
35.126: The testimony you testified concerning me, has become prayer and praise.”
35.127: While the priests rose up and spoke to Meryey at the mouth of the Euphrates,
35.128: There came a pure eagle, whose wings are world-filling.
35.129: He flew over the Jews, and flapping his wings he tied them up,
35.130: and lowered them to the water’s bottom, deeper than its stinking scum.
35.131: He sank them deeper than the devouring (waters), within the still waters,
35.132: and sank their ships to the bottom of the devouring water.
35.133: He destroyed the Temple, and set fire to Jerusalem.
35.134: He rained destruction upon them, and killed my disciples in Jerusalem.
35.135: He came down to her, he flapped his wings,
35.136: sat by her and spoke to her, and taught her, and loved truth from her.
35.137: He reached out and strongly embraced her, straightened her out, and put her on the throne.
35.139: “Meryey, consider me good, and mention me before Life.
35.140: I am your good helper, the man who heard your word.
35.141: I ask of you the lofty truth, the truth that the Jordans enlighten.”
35.143: “Good excellency, Life’s excellency, shed your splendor upon me!
35.144: Your light has shined forth and your glory is recognized in light’s place.
35.145: All who hear your voice, are enclosed in the pure place.
35.146: They are enclosed in Life’s Treasure, and your banner shines twofold.
35.147: For all who do not hear your voice, sleep and wakefulness are blotted out.
35.148: They will become servants to Jews, and all the priests, sons of maidservants.
35.149: You and I shall become great and successfully rise up to light’s place.”
35.150: And Life is praised and Life wins!
35.151: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

36.1: A fisher am I, a fisher chosen among fishers!
36.2: A fisher am I, chosen among fishers, and the head of all trappers.
36.3: I know the marshes, I recognize their inner trails and mounds.
36.4: I recognize the netting spots and marshes, and enter all the traps,
36.5: traversing the marsh in darkness, my ship does not cut [them] and I am not caught.
36.6: At night, I observe the fish on an embankment. I start on the way
36.7: in a crescent skiff that isn’t (made) out of iron.
36.8: I covered the prominence of the one who was an enemy to us.
36.9: I cleared out the flotsam which was blocking the way of life.
36.10: A helm is set upon my head, in whose shade the fish rest.
36.11: The spear in my hand is a wand, chosen in its place,
36.12: a staff of pure water, that the fishermen see and tremble.
36.13: I sit in a splendid vessel, and come to the mortal Earth.
36.14: I come by the beginning of the waters. I go through the beginning of the waters,
36.15: and the beginning of the courses, I come smoothly, at a calm and steady pace.
36.16: The waters are not tossed by my vessel, and its sound is not heard.
36.17: Before me is standing Hibel. At my side is seen Shitel,
36.18: whose name is sweet, close to me. Facing me, Ennosh sits and preaches.
36.20: “My father, the good fisher! My superior fisher, whose name is pleasant!”
36.21: Near our vessel, I hear the commotion of fishers,
36.22: fishers eating fish, and their putrid stench comes to me.
36.23: The sound of the fishers and their traders, who reproach one another and curse.
36.24: One confronts his partner, and says to the fisher,
36.25: “Sell your own fish, they are rotten, and nobody is buying from me!
36.26: You caught it in the deep sea, so that the loss fell upon its buyer!”
36.27: The fisher says and makes himself heard, making the man, his buyer, listen:
36.28: “Damn you, and damn your bell, and damn your worthless vessel!
36.29: You were the one who didn’t bring salt and put it on your fish that you buy,
36.30: so that your fish don’t stink in your casket, and yet you sell them for a great price!
36.31: Then you haven’t brought any flour or dates, and you haven’t brought any salt or thyme!
36.32: When you come empty-handed, no one of good virtue will join you.
36.33: Scram! Get lost, you crook who won’t buy from us,
36.34: and does business with your broken scales, which you hold and support with your elbow
36.35: for your crooked transaction, and take ten for the price of five.
36.36: Your trade bustles here, but it will be as if it never existed.
36.37: You will complain in oblivion, but those whom you do not mention fairly will rejoice.”
36.38: When the master of the fishermen, the leader of the living generation,
36.39: and the prince of all trappers heard this, he said to the helmsman,
36.40: “Come, bring me a lyre, so I can make a sound in the marsh
36.41: to wake up the fish of the deep, and set to flight the crafty bird
36.42: that is a torment to the fish!
36.43: I shall grab the great shoebill, and break off his wing on the spot!
36.44: I will take it from him, and I will dust inside my lyre!
36.45: The lyre is durable, because water does not mix with pitch.”
36.46: The fishers who heard the sound, their legs turned to jelly.
36.47: One cries to his associate, and says “Go to your blind,
36.48: because of the sound of the fisher, the fisher who does not trap fish!
36.49: Neither does his voice resemble a fisher’s, nor does his lyre resemble our lyre,
36.50: and neither does his voice resemble our voice, nor does his speech resemble this world’s!”
36.51: While the fishers stood in their blinds, the fishers did not take care to start thinking.
36.52: The fisher swiftly overwhelmed them, tossed out his net that extended over them,
36.53: and surrounded them in the marsh pools. He bound them with knots.
36.55: “Cast us from our fetters, so that your fish do not leap into our vessels!
36.56: We shall not catch those who mention your name!”
36.57: When the fishers said so to me, I struck them with an iron mace.
36.58: I tied up their merchant, a robber who doesn’t claim what they give him.
36.59: I bound them in palm-fiber cords, and ruined their ships for the water.
36.60: I burnt their entire dragnet, and the snare that ties dragnets together.
36.61: I put cauves on them, and dragged them behind my stern.
36.62: I made them promise and took their secrets, so that they would not take the good fish.
36.63: They will not steal from me, tie to a cane, hoist up, cut up,
36.64: and beat the cauves of fish and leaves,
36.65: and I made them swear that they would not stand and dip nets or leave a spear in the Jordan,
36.66: nor will they stand on dry land, and take captives in the marshes.
36.67: They will neither cast nets, nor take cauves and leaves.
36.68: I told them that they would eat cauldrons of the fish that is called “the eel.”
36.69: They will eat the catfish and the spider crab, and catch whatever rises up on its passage,
36.70: whom they restrained with cord upon cord, and bound (with) needle and thread.
36.71: I have trapped them in the marshes of deceit, and if they leave they will be trapped.
36.72: Neither do they drink the Eulaeus’ waters, nor do they know the way to the [un]fathomable river.
36.73: I have trapped them in their ships, and tossed my towline to the good.
36.75: “Put your raft here, it will not be on the embankment.”
36.76: When the head of the trappers said so, the fishers spoke to him, saying,
36.77: “May you be blessed, fisher, and may your vessel and vehicle be blessed as well.
36.78: How beautiful is this throw net of yours! How beautiful is the mesh that is in it!
36.79: Your cables and bonds are so beautiful, that you are not like the fishers of the world.
36.80: There are no weights in your mesh, and your spear does not catch fish.
36.81: Tell us where came from, so that we may work for you.
36.82: We shall bake and make porridge, and bring it before you.
36.83: Eat, and the morsel that falls from your hand, we shall eat and be satisfied.
36.85: “You scum-sucking fishermen! I am not a helper to those who catch fish,
36.86: and I was not called forth to be someone who eats scum!
36.87: I am a fisher of the souls who bear witness to Life.
36.88: I am a fisher who summons the poor, gathers them together, and gives them hope,
36.89: who calls them and tells them, ‘come gather by my side,’
36.91: ‘If you come, wanderers, you will be saved from the crafty birds,
36.92: I shall save my friends, raise them up, set them in my vessel,
36.93: dress them in splendid garments, and cover them in precious light.
36.94: I shall guide them with a crown of air and with the one of the Great on their heads.
36.95: They will sit in thrones and shine forth with precious light.
36.96: I shall take them and rise up, and you, the Seven, will stay here.
36.97: The fate of scum and filth will be your fate.
36.98: The day of light shall rise, and the darkness shall return to its place.
36.99: I and my disciples shall rise, and we shall see light’s place.
36.100: Life speaks and wins, and the man who went here triumphss!
36.101: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

37.1: A fisher am I, of the Great Life, a fisher am I, of the Mighty Life.
37.2: A fisher am I, of the Great Life, a messenger that Life has sent.
37.4: “Go, catch fish that do not eat filth, fish that neither eat horsebane
37.6: They approach neither chum, nor necklaces of marsh nets.”
37.7: Life tied a ring for me, and built an indestructible vessel for me,
37.8: a vessel whose bright sail flutters and flaps, but is not pulled off.
37.9: The vessel is a seed, and it travels through the heart of the heavens.
37.10: Its cables are splendid cables, and its tiller is one in which there is truth.
37.11: Sunday takes the punt pole, and Life’s Son took the tiller.
37.12: They travel with them to the settlements, and divide the light with the excellencies.
37.13: They set up thrones in them, and the Jordans came outspread.
37.14: Upon the prow are placed lanterns, which are not extinguished by adverse winds.
37.15: All the vessels that see me bow down and worship me.
37.16: They bow down, and worship me, and they come to me abasing themselves.
37.17: On the prow stands the fisher, teaching sublime lessons.
37.18: Near him are lanterns, the wicks of which do not move around in a commotion.
37.19: There is no stench, he has nothing false, and he is clothed in white garments.
37.20: He summons the fish and tells them,
37.21: “Beware for me in the world! Beware for me for yourselves,
37.22: on account of the crafty birds that are among you!
37.23: If you beware for me, my brothers, I shall undertake to be a helper,
37.24: a helper for you and a support, from the place of darkness to that of light.”
37.25: The victorious Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
37.26: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

38.1: The fisher put on bright garments, and set on his shoulder an axe
38.2: for wolves and the wicked magian, and there is no rust on the axe.
38.3: Whenever fishers saw the fisher, they would come and gather around him.
38.5: “You are a lucky fisher, who has not caught the fish of the marsh!
38.6: You have not seen the seafood, the food they gather within them.
38.7: You are a measured support, and we shall enroll you among the fishers!
38.8: You will be our key shareholder, and you will take a share like ours!
38.9: Give us a share in your vessel, and you will take a share in our vessel!
38.10: Come, take a share from us, and give us a share in your vessel!
38.11: You will give us a share, and we will give you a share!
38.12: [We will give you] from what we have, so join your ship with our ship,
38.13: and wear black just like we do, so when you lift up your lamp, you’ll find
38.14: that the fish do not see your reflection, and your vessel will bring in the fish.
38.15: If you listen, you’ll catch fish, you’ll throw them in your boat, and do business.
38.16: If you don’t listen to our shareholders, you will eat salt.
38.17: If you do what we ourselves do, you will eat oil and date syrup.
38.18: You will make porridge and fill up cups, and distribute them to all the fishermen,
38.19: and we shall make you leader of us all! They will gather by your side, leader of us all!
38.20: The principals will come to be behind you.
38.21: They will be your humble servants, and you will take a portion of what we have.
38.22: Our father will be your servant, and we shall be called obedient to you.
38.23: Our mother will sit with your handmaiden and tie dragnets.
38.24: She will come and be your maidservant, and tie cords of every sort for you.
38.25: She will divvy up the rocks, and throw the lead (weights) in the netting.
38.26: The netting greatly sighed, that it is heavier than the world!
38.27: She will divide the water with the cord when the fish come, and they will be caught
38.28: They will not know the way that they’re going, and not know how to return back to their way.
38.29: Like walls that fall apart, they come and fall upon the good.
38.30: The fish neither leave to rise up, nor turn around to face the embankment.
38.31: They sink them down beneath the scum, and restrain them along with a circlet.
38.32: They carry them off in droves, and beat them back from its crown.
38.33: She has a fishing weir, which the fish enter and get held back,
38.34: against the bundles of the weir.
38.35: They have set up a lattice between the two wheels.
38.36: They have set up seines and set lines filled with chum,
38.37: the bait that offers a meal of death.
38.38: Woe to the fish whom they dazzle, whose eyes do not see the light!
38.39: Wise are the fish who recognize them, they will pass by all the baits,
38.40: The snares, the gillnets, and the seines are a lair for them there,
38.41: which only one out of a thousand will see, and only one out of two thousand will see twice.
38.42: They seized it, took it, and hung a bell over its entrance, a bell forged with evil,
38.43: that will captivate all the worlds. There, the waters commingle,
38.44: so that the jimsonweed overwhelms and the deadly arsenic intoxicates.
38.45: Woe to the fish who enter them!”
38.46: When the fisher heard this, he gave the prow a good kicking.
38.47: The fisher gave the boats of the fishers a good kicking.
38.48: The fishers floated on the marshes, clinging together like mice, and not getting up.
38.49: The cane strikes and splatters, and the fish of the sea land
38.51: The whirlpool whirled in the marsh water. He spoke, shrieking at the top of his voice.
38.52: He spoke with his sublime voice. He said to the fishers,
38.53: “You are before me, shameful fishers, poison-making fishers,
38.54: go, go and catch your own stinking fish.
38.55: Keep back, get down, leave your group, and go to the end of the line.
38.56: I am not a fisher who catches fish, and my fish are discerning.
38.57: They will not be caught with a hook of chum, a bait which my fish do not eat.
38.58: They will not block up gillnets in submerged nets or a deceptive lantern.
38.59: They will not go down from water’s surface, and they will not enter the deceptive weir,
38.60: and they will not share the water that seeks to fall upon the youth.
38.61: If the fishers throw a net upon them, they will break through the net and escape.
38.62: There will never be a day on Earth, in which fish fish fishers.
38.63: There will never be a day on Earth, in which the dove loves the crow.
38.64: Damn you crafty birds, and damn your worthless kind!
38.65: Woe to your father the shoebill, whose lair will be in the reeds!
38.66: Woe to you, starving kingfisher, whose wings will never dry on Earth!
38.67: Woe to you, stinking pelican, who will see the fish and sigh.
38.68: They cry out and weep with bitterness when they strike at the fish but do not catch it.
38.69: Woe to you, pied crow, who takes fish from the depths.
38.70: Blessed is the one who is saved from your talons, the talons that seize fish!
38.71: Blessed is the one who is saved from the men who watch Earth!
38.72: Go, Seven, go be part of your houses!
38.73: Water will not mix with pitch, and light will not be counted with darkness.
38.74: An associate of the righteous will never be called an associate of yours.
38.75: A good man keeps good company, and a bad man keeps bad company,
38.76: and neither will your boat join my boat, nor will your seal be set on my seal.
38.77: Such is the head of you all, so you will be food for him!
38.78: Such is your savage father, trapped in the black water!
38.79: As for your mother, who ties nets and the twin heavy wheels,
38.80: I struck her with a staff of water, and split her head down the middle.
38.81: I shall guide my friends, set them up in my ship,
38.82: and pass them over every tax collector.
38.83: I shall pass them over the den of inquity, the place where fish are caught.
38.84: I shall pull them away from the fish eaters, and you will perish in your settlements.
38.85: I and my true friends shall dwell in the settlement of Life.
38.86: He will lift them up in thrones beneath stainless banners.”
38.87: The Seven were defeated, and the stranger remained victorious.
38.88: The man of proven righteousness won, and he led his entire nation to victory.
38.89: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
38.90: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

39.1: It is the pure fisher’s voice, which calls and teaches in the marshes,
39.2: and it tells the fish of the seas,
39.3: “Set the group aright, rise up to the surface of the water,
39.4: so that your strength may double.
39.5: Beware for me the fishers of fish, the fishers who look over the Jordan.
39.6: Shelmey and Nedbey curse them, so go back and stay a league behind me,
39.7: and fish curse their nets, so revile them in their places.”
39.8: As the fisher said this, he admonished all of them,
39.9: the fishers who heard his voice. They come and gather near him.
39.10: They begin to question him, not knowing whence he came.
39.12: “Where were you, fisher, whose voice we do not hear in the marsh,
39.13: and whose vessel is not like our vessels, and she has not accompanied you among (us)?
39.14: Your vessel is not sealed with pitch, and you are not like this world’s fishers.”
39.15: Seeing him, the fishers blush, become ashamed, and stand in their places.
39.17: “For what reason do you fish but not catch? Your ship is not like our ship;
39.18: It shines like the sun in the night.
39.19: Your vessel is perfect in the air, and sublime banners are unfurled on it.
39.20: Our vessel goes by water, but your vessel moves between the waters.
39.21: The reeds of our marsh, which rustle together and break,
39.22: within them is an empty acre, in which there are no cisterns or fountains.
39.23: Your purifier, fisher, is the type that fish see and flee far away.
39.24: We never see fishers that resemble you, in whose vessel the wind dwells.
39.25: The fisher steered the sail-yard and the tiller that brings light to the marshes.
39.26: There is no cable in your cast net, and no draw-string encircles it.
39.27: It has no rocks that will be an artifice for the fish of the marsh pools
39.28: whom your cord has taken in its snare, and you have neither cudgel nor axe,
39.29: and you have not brought a fisher’s tools, you have neither chum nor poisons.
39.30: Your cord does not lie still in the water, and it is not submerged to snatch fish.”
39.31: When the fishers said this, the fisher spoke, saying to them:
39.32: “My fishing brothers and sons, get out of my sight!
39.33: Flee, get out, go up to your town, the ruin of Jerusalem!
39.34: Ask your father, who knows me, about me! Ask your mother, who is my maidservant, about me!
39.35: Tell her, ‘There is one fisher in the vessel, he has the four winds as a tiller,
39.36: and standing within it is a sail-yard, a scourge of afflictions and liberations.
39.37: They will destroy the land of Jerusalem.”
39.38: When they heard and recognized the fisher who went there, they say to him,
39.39: “Pity us, have mercy and be compassionate! May you forgive our sins and debts!
39.40: We are your servants, may you be lenient with us!
39.41: We shall take care of your fish, so not even one will be taken from them.
39.42: We shall be the servants of your disciples, who mention your name in good faith.
39.43: We shall stand by and take care of all who mention your name.”
39.44: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
39.45: In the name of the Great Life, and in the name of the precious Truth.

40.1: From beyond, an excellency preaches, and Spirit answers him from darkness’ gates.
40.3: “Who are you, among the excellencies, whose voice is so lovely, whose palate is so sweet?”
40.5: “May Life’s cry be against you, wicked Spirit, Spirit that always seeks evil.
40.6: I am Splendid Hibel! I am an iron shoe,
40.7: an iron shoe am I, which has trampled down the darkness!”
40.9: “Take from me precious gold, and silver worth more than a wife or children,
40.10: and sing me some of your lofty songs.”
40.12: “A well-prepared excellency am I, who comes to the demons!
40.13: I’ve come to trample the darkness.
40.14: A well-prepared excellency am I, whom Life has prepared and sent forth!
40.15: A well-prepared excellency am I, the king of the worlds!
40.16: A well-prepared excellency am I, whose power is hard against you!
40.17: A well-prepared excellency am I, who is better prepared than any other excellency!”
40.18: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
40.19: In the name of the Great Life, and in the name of the precious Truth.

41.1: From beyond, a man preaches, and Spirit answers him from darkness’ gates.
41.2: She brings gold in baskets, and puts pearls at the tips of her locks of hair.
41.3: She goes to him and says,
41.4: “Strange man! Take from me beloved gold
41.5: that is precious, and my sublime pearls, and sing me one of your sublime songs.
41.6: Bring forth Life’s Voice, and teach me from the ground up.”
41.8: “Leave and get away from me, Spirit, who is plotting evil!”
41.9: She goes and Namrus comes along, and she approaches him, and says,
41.10: “Strange man, bring me your wonderful sermon!”
41.12: “Stay still, Namrus, and keep your scorn to yourself.
41.13: I am not a minstrel, who entertains those who fall before me.
41.14: I am a man from another world, an iron shoe am I,
41.15: My words and singing are bats and clubs against the Evil Spirit.”
41.17: “May the truth heal you, good man, and may it heal the speech with which you spoke.”
41.18: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

42.1: It is the voice of Manda d’Heyyi that calls and teaches his friends.
42.2: He teaches the righteous elect about the secrets of this world.
42.3: “The world full of secrets and hints, the world is full of secrets,
42.5: The land’s secret is peacefulness. The foundation’s secret is the heavens.
42.6: The light’s secret is day. The darkness’ secret is night.
42.7: The water’s [secret is] life. The salt’s secret is the soul.
42.8: The sword’s secret is fire. Death’s secret is sleep,
42.9: The world’s secret is Adam. The First’s secret is his son.
42.10: The dome’s secret is the righteous elect’s, who would not stand for it for all the worlds.
42.11: Kindness’s secret is to shut the eyes, and to know a hundred and one.
42.12: The baptism’s secrets are to say one thing, and to hear one.
42.13: The pearl’s secret is to say one thing, and to listen to one.
42.14: Love’s secret is to shut the eyes on the way and to know.
42.15: Poverty’s secret is to be sent out in the world.
42.16: The elect’s secret is the myrtle, and the body’s secret is the rose.
42.17: For just as the myrtle refreshes, so too will the elect surely refresh,
42.18: and just as the rose decays, so too will the body surely decay.
42.19: The body will surely decay, and the world’s measure will become full.”
42.20: “From where have you come, truthful man, you who lists this world’s abominations?”
42.21: “I am a man from another world, upon whose head the mark is set.
42.22: The mark is set upon my head, and I will bring it up to light’s place.
42.23: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

43.1: It is the voice of Manda d’Heyyi, who comes as a judge to the world.
43.2: He has judged the treasurers, and enraged the chiefs of the tent.
43.3: He has judged those who expect Truth begging with the wages and rewards he gave them.
43.4: He gave them wages and rewards, and they took them to their treasury to hide.
43.5: They took them to hide in their treasure house, because Life’s speech has gone from their senses.
43.6: It is the voice of Manda d’Heyyi, who calls forth and teaches all his friends,
43.7: “Let me warn you, my brothers, let me warn you, my friends!
43.8: Let me warn you, my brothers, from the death the chiefs of the tent will die.
43.9: As soon as their mouths open, they will die, and when their eyes close,
43.10: they will be held to account for their souls, who will have to pass a test there.
43.11: There, they will have to pass a test.”
43.13: “Bring me their teachers, who demand much from them, do not give, and throw them down.
43.14: Bring me their scholars, who teach them, but they do not learn.
43.15: There, he judges father and son, teacher and student, judges mother and daughter there,
43.16: There, he judges mother and daughter-in-law, servant and master, employee and employer.
43.17: All cases will be judged, and all will be settled,
43.18: save for the case of the husband and wife, until the Great ordains it.
43.19: and Manda d’Heyyi will absolve him, raise him up to set him in perfection’s house.
43.20: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

44.1: Life’s herald calls forth, “Blessed is he who understands himself.
44.2: A man who understands himself has no equal in the world.
44.3: Blessed are you righteous servants, who have kept away from all evil.
44.4: Shame on you, wicked heart, within which evil governs,
44.5: and which Evil does not let celebrate a blessing with goodness,
44.6: and its thought is full of wrath, which is from Satan’s wrath.
44.7: The guts that jealousy loosens will dwell in the depths.
44.8: The mouth that opens to curse will not look upon light’s place.
44.9: Those who raise their hands to strike will kill their own masters with the sword.
44.10: Shame on you, big belly, which nothing from this world will satisfy.
44.11: You men who give rewards, I call out to you and say,
44.12: ‘If you give, then do not report it! If you report it, then do not repeat it!
44.13: If you give with your right hand, then do not tell your left hand!’
44.14: Shame on the wise man, whose wisdom has taught him nothing.
44.15: Shame on the builder, who has built no building for himself.
44.16: Shame on the pathmaker, who has paved no path for himself,
44.17: and he will not rise up to see light’s place.”
44.18: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

45.1: Life’s herald calls forth, the Mighty Life’s herald.
45.2: Life’s herald calls forth everone who prepares himself.
45.3: Blessed is he who knows himself, and whose heart is a builder for him.
45.4: Blessed are Truth’s people; they will rise up to see light’s place.
45.5: Shame on the advisor, who has not given himself any advice.
45.6: Shame on the pathmaker, who has built no path for himself,
45.7: on which he goes and does not slip.
45.8: Shame on the builder, who has built no building for himself.
45.9: Shame on the evil eye, since the wicked were not satisfied with this world.
45.10: Shame on the big belly, which does not fill despite all the belly eats.
45.11: Shame on the forked tongue, which gives two different decisions to the same case.
45.12: Shame on the students, who are taught, but do not learn.
45.13: Shame on the foolish idiots, who get stuck in their idiocy.
45.14: Shame on the wise man, who has not taught his wisdom.
45.15: Shame on the rulers, who rule over the forsaken,
45.16: and do no good deeds. They will fall into the blazing fire,
45.17: and stoke the coals with their hands, and kindle the fire with their lips.
45.18: Shame on the wicked heart, within which evil governs,
45.19: Wickedness governs within it, and it will end with of the world.
45.20: It will end, and not see light’s place.
45.21: Blessings on whoever has done good; “Shame, shame!” calls whoever has done evil.
45.22: Shame on whoever has had a bounty, and has done no good with it.
45.23: He has committed sins for himself, and piled provocations before himself.
45.24: Blessings on whoever has had good, and has done good with it.
45.25: He has made a reward for himself. His works go before him.
45.26: His works go before him, and reach ahead of him on the way.
45.27: Your hands perform the truth, so rise up and see light’s place!

46.1: From light’s place, I left, from you, everlasting abode!
46.2: From the place I left, I was joined by an excellency from Life.
46.3: The excellency who joined me from Life’s house held a staff of living water in his hand.
46.4: The staff he held in his hand was entirely leafy from end to end.
46.5: He gave me some of its leaves, my sick heart found recovery.
46.6: Once again, he gave me some of it, and the books became full.
46.7: For the third time, he gave me some of it, and he fixed my eyes in my head.
46.8: Within my head, he fixed my eyes, and I saw my father and knew him.
46.9: I saw my father, I saw him, and I gave him three requests.
46.10: I asked him for a great heart, which can be carried by the big and the little.
46.11: I asked him for calmness, in which there is no rebellion.
46.12: I asked him for a level path, to rise to light’s place in peace.
46.13: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

47.1: From light’s place, I left, from you, everlasting abode!
47.2: I was dressed in resplendent robes, and a victory wreath was placed around my head.
47.3: I arrived and found the Nazoreans, standing on the banks of the Jordan.
47.4: I set up my throne and sat down, like a father sitting amidst his sons.
47.5: The good man sits and teaches his sons all the truth, in which there is no error.
47.7: See that you do not commit adultery; see that you do not commit theft;
47.8: those who commit stealing and adultery will not rise to Life’s house.
47.9: They will not rise to Life’s house; they will not look upon light’s place.
47.11: See that you perform no magic, and oppress the soul in the body.
