47.12: Magicians and liars will be tossed in cauldrons that seethe, and fire will be their judge.
47.14: See you do not shift boundaries. The day that you displace the great marker,
47.15: those who shift boundaries, their eyes will not see the light.
47.17: See you do not deliver a servant to his master or a maid to her mistress,
47.18: nor deliver the weak to the strong, to be bound in a remote place.
47.19: In the customs house, his eye will see only darkness, and his foot will find no solid ground.
47.21: See that you do not take a maid who has not been not set free,
47.22: and thus bring up your sons in her master’s house.
47.23: If the servant sins one day, on the day that his master judges him,
47.24: the sins committed by the servant will come upon the head of his father.
47.26: See that you are not informers and that your eyes give no hints,
47.27: since informers and snitches will be assigned to the penitentiaries.
47.28: To the penitentiary, they will be assigned, and they will surely be judged harshly.
47.30: See that you do not practice usury and compound interest,
47.31: lest you be judged in the dark mountain.
47.33: See that you do not worship idols and devils,
47.34: the Olympians, the paganism, and the impiety of this world,
47.35: because the idols and devils a harsh judgment will be upon them,
47.36: and those who worship them will not rise to Life’s house.
47.37: They will not rise to Life’s house, and they will not look upon light’s place.
47.38: See what I have commanded you, and surely do not bear a false and deceitful witness.
47.39: On account of a false and deceitful witness, they will be interrogated before the judge.
47.40: They will be interrogated before the judge who judges the entire world.
47.41: He judges every person as to his works and his merits.
47.43: Whatever is disgusting to you, do not do to your neighbor,
47.44: since the world to which you have gone has judgment and a great reckoning.
47.45: It has judgment and a great reckoning, in which safeguarded intellects
47.47: since all who are laden will rise, those who are empty-handed will be cut off.
47.48: Shame on the empty-handed one, who will stand empty-handed at the tollhouse.
47.49: When it was in his possession, and he gave not. He searched there in his lap, and he found not.
47.50: They will cast the wicked and liars in darkness. They will throw him into the blazing fire.
47.51: In the blazing fire they will throw him, in whose ear they called, and he listened not.
47.52: I showed it to his eye, and he saw not. I showed him, and he didn’t see with his eye.
47.53: And Life triumphs, and the man who went here triumphs!
47.54: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

48.1: Truth! I testify to you, as a man who seeks knowledge.
48.2: Upon you I let my eyes look, good man, the elect whom Life has moved here.
48.3: Tell my heart, so it may rest. Speak to my guts, so they may be turned.
48.4: Tell their minds, so they may be fixed, and stick to their places.
48.5: Tell the watcher of the sea, to save me a crossing over the sea.
48.6: Tell the watcher of the rivers, to stretch a cable for me over the rivers.
48.7: Tell the one who paves the mountains, to pave me a way over the mountains.
48.8: Tell the artisan, who crafts works of art and images,
48.10: Tell the body-builder, “Build your building with haste!
48.11: Hastily build your building, because you will have to leave it shortly,
48.12: since this world will come to nought, and its works will fall apart!”
48.13: Precious gold will be lost, and silver will be sought but not found.
48.14: Their hearts’ delight will be torn out, and their useless singing will go.
48.15: The king will abandon his crown, and the nobility will go into captivity.
48.16: The perfect will rise to the light, but the wicked will be detained here.
48.17: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
48.18: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

49.1: Way beyond, beside Truth’s barrier, there stands a plow plowing,
49.2: a plow that is no (mere) ox-plow and that has not been revealed by my clan.
49.3: The plow is Truth’s plow, which sows wages and rewards.
49.4: Sunday holds the plow, and Life’s Son holds the seeds.
49.5: These outstanding men sow and scatter gems; they scatter and toss pearls.
49.6: The good sow and scatter blessings; they have brought out and threshed for ages.
49.7: For ages, they have brought out and threshed, and set watchers over them.
49.8: Over them, they set watchers, sublime, blessed, and completely confirmed.
49.10: “Watchers, who have watched for an age, watch closely over your gates;
49.11: closely watch over your gates and paths, so you may take your gate in peace.”
49.12: Now Truth comes and goes, like a fan of living water,
49.13: he takes a fan in his hand, and they seek out the good in them.
49.14: Those zealous ones who are worthy, roadside misfortunes will drop [from them],
49.15: and once more those who are worthy, distressful scandals will drop [from them].
49.16: Those who are unworthy, they will fall from their folds;
49.17: from their folds they will fall, and approach the mouth of the stud.
49.18: Your souls are redeemed and saved, my good brothers, and my sisters who are faithful.
49.19: Perfect men and perfect women will be saved,
49.20: saved from the mouth of this stud, whose name is Ur, the Lord of Darkness.
49.21: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

50.1: He deals in wages and rewards and will rise to see light’s place.
50.2: Shame on the rulers who rule over the forsaken and do no good works;
50.3: they will fall into a blazing fire.
50.4: With their hands, they will stoke the coals, and with their lips they will kindle the flames.
50.5: Those who acquire to leave to their children, they will go to boil in the fire.
50.6: They will go and boil in the fire, and their pride will be kept from them.
50.7: Shame on the foolish fools, who are stubborn in their folly!
50.8: Shame on the students whom they teach, and they don’t learn true wisdom;
50.9: they will be settled in darkness.
50.10: Shame on the masters, who seek from them but give not.
50.11: Shame on the forked tongue, which gives two different decisions to the same case.
50.12: Shame on the evil heart, within which wickedness rules!
50.13: Wickedness governs within it, it will surely end on the End’s great day.
50.14: Shame on the wrathful one, who is filled with Satan’s wrath.
50.15: Shame on the builder, who has built no building for himself.
50.16: For himself, he has built nothing, on which he goes and is upheld.
50.17: Shame on the pathmaker, who has blazed no path for himself,
50.18: on which he walks and does not slip.
50.19: Shame on him who gives good advice, but has not given himself any advice.
50.20: Shame on him who had blessings, but did not give benefits from his blessings.
50.21: He will search in his lap and find nothing, since he had it in his hand and gave not.
50.22: He will surely end on the End’s great day.
50.23: The one who hides his eyes with his own hand, who should serve as a healer for him?
50.24: The one who destroys his own way with his horn, who should serve as a builder for you?
50.25: I tell and explain to you, the chosen who live in the world,
50.26: who will go to Life’s house, and then return to the abode of darkness?
50.28: See this world will surely perish, and its works will succumb to destruction.
50.29: Its works will come apart, and not draw near again.
50.30: Precious gold will be lost, and silver will be sought but not found.
50.31: The shadow of deception and the service of the world will vanish.
50.32: It will disappear like the scents and the things of this world.
50.34: Days, months, hours, and minutes will finish, and it will be as if they never existed.
50.35: The whole world will end and come to nought, it will be as if never existed.
50.36: The joyful vine will be uprooted, and their song will go there and vanish.
50.37: The king will leave behind his crown, and the nobles, the rulers of the world,
50.38: with the breaking of their hearts, they will leave the world.
50.39: The Earth will decay and come to a stop in the depths of the stench of darkness.
50.41: Do not have any faith in this deceptive world!
50.43: Blessed is he who has heard and believed; shame on him who is exhausted and asleep.
50.44: Blessed is he who heard and believed; he will rise up to see light’s place.
50.45: As for the wicked who heard but believed not, they set their faces toward darkness’ place,
50.46: the dark mountain will devour them.
50.47: Blessed is the one who knows himself and whose heart is his builder.
50.48: Whoever is mindful of himself has no equal in the world.
50.50: Stay firm and endure the world’s persecution, endure the world’s persecution
50.52: Worship me sincerely, so that I may aid you as a support.
50.54: The way souls must travel is long and without end.
50.55: On it, no leagues are measured, and no milestones are marked off in it.
50.56: Each league is a penitentiary, and upon each penitentiary,
50.58: The weapon is forged and set, and the iron is burnished and set.
50.59: The cauldrons are filled and seething, in which the souls of the wicked wait.
50.60: The scales are set and settled. Out of a thousand, he chooses one.
50.61: He chooses one out of a thousand, and chooses two out of a myriad.
50.62: He chooses and brings up the souls, that are worthy and deserving of light’s place.
50.63: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

51.1: Among those lying upon the shore, he cried out with a loud voice.
51.2: With a loud voice, he cried out, from both banks of the [un]fathomable river,
51.3: the river whose waters are dragons, and whose waves are scorpions.
51.4: In it are firebrands, upon its two banks are all worms,
51.5: at its mouth is set a vessel for the molts, and they grab and hold back.
51.6: Those who philander and steal will not cross the [un]fathomable river.
51.7: Wizards and witches will not cross the [un]fathomable river.
51.8: Informers and snitches will not cross the [un]fathomable river.
51.9: Those who shift boundaries will not cross the [un]fathomable river.
51.10: Those who move boundary stones will not cross the [un]fathomable river.
51.11: I, with that with which I am armed, because I am a son of Life,
51.12: shall plunge deep into the river, the [un]fathomable river,
51.13: The dragons did not strike me, nor did all the scorpions sting me.
51.14: Fire did not consume me, nor did all the worms destroy me.
51.15: They did not throw me into the vessel of molts, because I am Truth,
51.16: and Life’s scent is spread upon me.
51.17: And Life is praised, and Life triumphs!
51.18: In the name of the Great Life!

52.1: He shook and disturbed Yurba, the warrior man:
52.2: “Go, climb aboard your chariot! Climb aboard your chariot,
52.3: and go about in this world.
52.4: Go about in the world, and be a judge for all the worlds!
52.5: When you come in and when you go out (in the morning, he rose, at nightfall, he set)
52.6: do not flame nor rage nor sin against my sons.
52.7: Do not sin against my disciples, who live with you in the world.”
52.8: Yurba arose, and went down, until he came to Ptahil’s house.
52.9: There were three planets, who took words from their father.
52.10: They took words from their father, and worship and praise him completely.
52.11: Every day, three times, praise rises up to Ptahil.
52.12: The sun, with pride, takes 900 prayers,
52.13: the moon, the poor leper, takes 300 prayers,
52.14: Venus, the “holy,” with pride takes 600 prayers,
52.15: and they praise my father with 24 prayers.
52.16: As Yurba sits in his chariot, he comes and goes in the world.
52.17: Venus, the lying Spirit, came, and gave him worthless advice,
52.18: the two to whom she speaks wickedly about the children of the great family
52.20: when the watchers saw this, they went down to Life’s house.
52.21: They rose, went, and told Splendid Hibel about the things
52.22: Yurba had done in this world.
52.23: They tell Splendid Hibel to go and come to his brothers
52.24: he went and came to his brothers, and stood before the excellencies.
52.25: Splendid Hibel went up to the excellencies who were sitting and meditating,
52.26: struck Yurba with a club, and hurled Spirit down from her throne.
52.28: “What did I tell you, when you came to the fallen house?
52.29: What sins have my disciples committed, out of the wickedness you released against them?
52.30: You’ve released wickedness against them and frightened them in this world.”
52.31: I took the glory and light away from him, and lifted him into a dark cloud.
52.32: I took away the great crown, and struck his head with a rod,
52.33: [I took away] the four rays of splendor, light and glory,
52.34: and the watchers fled away from him. The Earth went to ruin,
52.35: the whole world perished. Yurba screamed and Yurba cried,
52.36: and he howled in his chariot from the rage that had come over him.
52.37: His face became dark and gloomy, and he stood there in his original form.
52.39: “If it pleases you, may your forgiveness be granted to me.
52.40: I swear by the 900 prayers, with which I praise my father Ptahil,
52.41: I swear upon that moment and time when he sought to swallow me and eat me up,
52.42: and when he sought to destroy me, and you were my salvation.
52.43: I swear upon the robe of splendor, light, and glory,
52.44: which you brought to me from a hidden place.
52.45: I swear upon the four wreaths of splendor, light, and glory,
52.47: I swear upon the Great Glorious Countenance, that was from the splendid canal.
52.48: I swear upon the two watchers who unfurl upon Mount Tarwan
52.49: banners of splendor from top to bottom.
52.50: They speak to me in kindness, and discourse upon pure teachings.”
52.51: Yurba swore strongly, and set a seal upon his oaths.
52.52: Then he handed him the robe of splendor, light, and glory,
52.53: which he had brought from a hidden place.
52.54: He gave him back the four wreaths of splendor, light, and glory,
52.56: He gave him the great crown, and he gave him splendor from head to toe.
52.57: He fixed him and seated him in his chariot, and returned to him the watchers who protect him,
52.58: who had been completely taken from him, he returned to him all the watchers.
52.59: Then a loud voice called out from the hidden, and made him listen in deepest darkness,
52.60: “Did you not know, Yurba, that my wrath is upon you?
52.61: Did you not know, Yurba, that I have lifted you up into the gloomy darkness?
52.62: Did you not know, Yurba, that I let loose a punch and a wrath against you,
52.63: and all the guards ran away, when I put an evil curse upon you,
52.64: and lifted you into gloomy darkness? Into gloomy darkness I have lifted you,
52.65: since no one will be your salvation.
52.66: Your mother, Spirit, and Christ, the planets, and the twelve constellations,
52.67: were hidden within clouds of darkness, and could do nothing against my powers.
52.68: Did you not know, Yurba, that I came here in the twinkling of an eye?
52.69: Did you not know, Yurba, you only shine in the world because of me?
52.70: Did you not know, Yurba, I gave my sons your strength and mindfulness?
52.71: Did you not know, Yurba, I can make your likeness darken and tremble?”
52.72: Then he wept in his chariot, and said to Splendid Hibel,
52.73: “If I have sinned against your disciples, then may torture and lashing be raised against me,
52.74: but on your life, Splendid Hibel, and the secret place from which you came,
52.75: on your life, Splendid Hibel, I have not sinned against your children.
52.76: I have not sinned against your disciples who live with us in the world.”
52.77: Splendid Hibel then rose to his place, and he condemned Yurba to the fallen house,
52.78: “Stay put and wait in the house, until Earth comes to nought.”
52.79: As Yurba drove out in his chariot, he spoke to him with pure teachings.
52.80: He grew afraid and said, “I wanted to do good for the sublime family’s children,”
52.81: Lying Spirit came along, and tells him sorcery and idle tasks.
52.82: She took it from him, then he became full of wickedness.
52.83: Then he was full of wickedness, and forgot to fear and tremble,
52.84: until the final day, on which justice will be pronounced upon them.
52.85: All the demons will fall into the darkness and die a second death.

53.1: When the shining was taken from his place, he came to the deficient world.
53.2: and they gave him entirely to the moon, the man who gave the shining.
53.3: He called him, equipped him, and thoroughly ordered him.
53.5: “I gave you the shining garment, to enlighten the darkness of the fallen house.
53.6: Whenever the sun’s splendor disappears, your shining will rise forth.
53.7: Whenever a man lies with his wife under your sign, it will result in a pregnancy,
53.8: and your witness will be inside of the pure race.
53.9: You must enlighten her face, and free her from diseases and infirmities,
53.10: and from those images that are improper, and the wickedness and suffering of the fallen house,
53.11: since the sown race of the house was entrusted to your possession,
53.12: You must shine and enlighten, and completely uphold its descendants.”
53.13: Then he spoke to the man who had clad him in the shining light,
53.14: “One day per month, I shall disappear, and my banner will be rolled up,
53.15: [rolled up] is my shining light, which two watchers are charged to protect.
53.16: When I am not there, and men lie with their wives,
53.17: as they receive on that day, tongue-tied and dumb children
53.18: and disgusting appearances will come forth from them.
53.19: When they receive on that day, deaf children and lepers
53.20: without hands and feet will come forth from them.
53.21: The planets will disturb the seed and make it entirely evil.”
53.22: The Man who had clad him in shining light spoke,
53.23: “Those who come into being on those days, are not fit to be our progeny.
53.24: They are neither counted among our number nor reckoned within our race.
53.25: It is thoroughly a race of darkness; it will return to the clan from which it came.”
53.26: He summoned, ordered, and prepared me, and left me stability and caution.
53.28: “Take care of the congregation of souls that we have left in the world.”
53.29: He bowed down, walked away from me, and went up to Abator’s house.
53.30: He went down to the penitentiaries; down to the penitentiaries he went,
53.32: On the day that he is withdrawn from Earth, and the hours that he is hidden from the world,
53.33: for the mistakes he sets against the disciples, he lets torture, crushing, and lashings upon him.
53.34: He shows him panic, fear, and terror until he dies,
53.35: and panic-stricken and darkened, he will look as if he never existed.
53.36: When he comes forth from the penitentiary, his color will have been removed.
53.37: His color will be drawn from him, and he will look as if he never existed.
53.38: Then he will sit in his chariot and put on shining rays of light.
53.39: They will spread a shining light over him, and he will walk out into the world.
53.40: On the first day, he will appear, he starts at the summit of the heavens.
53.41: He will come from heaven’s upper level, and be supported upon its lower level.
53.42: Until the second day, his gleam’s light will be over all of the worlds.
53.43: Until the seventh day of the month, the moon will speak with the voice of Life.
53.44: With the voice of Life, he will speak, since he recalled the fear and trembling of Life.
53.45: When he passes the seventh day, he will forget the fear and the trembling.
53.46: He will forget the fear and the trembling, and cast evil into the world.
53.47: I say, advising you, men who bear witness to Life,
53.48: to be strong and endure the persecution within the fallen house!
53.49: He told him that Earth would soon vanish, and the two mountains will bend over.
53.50: Bent over will be the two mountains, and light’s power will be taken from them.
53.51: Completely taken away will be all the stability that they had.
53.52: Now their appearance will be despicable, and they will look as if they never existed.
53.53: Before their souls howl, and scream and cry on the spot,
53.54: and he will say to them,
53.55: “When we were in this world, your splendor shone over all the worlds.
53.56: We bore witness to you, and worshiped and praised you completely.
53.57: Now your appearance is despicable, and it has grown dark and gloomy as if it never existed.”
53.58: The planets had no explanation to give to their worshippers about how it happened.
53.59: The planets, their worshippers, and their souls, worthy and unworthy, and all their creatures,
53.60: even the souls of the great family who acknowledge Life will sink to deepest Sheol.
53.61: They will fall to the great serpent, whose name is Ur, the Lord of Darkness.
53.62: From that day, our souls will be saved and redeemed,
53.63: and the souls of our good brothers, and those sisters who are believers.
53.64: The souls of the faithful and sincere will rise to see the great place of light.
53.65: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
53.66: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

54.1: I did not and do not want to go up to the town of Jerusalem,
54.2: A town that is a town of evil, and a city full of sinners!
54.3: A town of sinners, and the city built by Adunay.
54.4: The city which Adunay built, the Lie entered and filled it.
54.5: The Lie entered and filled it, and then came persecution against my disciples.
54.6: How displeasing and unpleasant it was for me, to go up to the town of Jerusalem.
54.7: As I arrived in Jerusalem City, Adunay opened his mouth,
54.8: and from the sky Adunay answered. He answered from the sky, and says to me,
54.9: “Are you are leaving, strange man, against whose will the city was built,
54.10: by whose will the city was not built?”
54.11: Since I had formed a faction within it, I spoke to Adunay,
54.12: so my feats would be fulfilled through him.
54.13: “I have Jacob and Benjamin, my brothers, the two golden sons,
54.14: and Meryey the perfect, who are worth ages and generations to me.”
54.15: When Adunay heard, he called Spirit, and says to her,
54.16: “Who among Life’s offspring came here? They are taking over from us!
54.17: Come, write a false and unlawful book to captivate ages and generations.”
54.18: Then Spirit and Mercury made a decree, and the Seven wrote and arranged the Torah.
54.19: They wrote the Torah, arranged it, and placed it in the hands of the sun, Adunay.
54.20: Through his feats, Adunay summoned him, Moses, Amram’s son, to Mt. Sinai.
54.21: He settled him there for forty days, and shut his mouth to food and drink,
54.22: To food and drink, he shut his mouth, and gave him the unlawful book,
54.25: I shall tell you about the Jews, how their book is.
54.26: It did not come from the light!
54.27: If their book had been from light, all of them would be of one kind.
54.29: I shall tell you about Arabs, that their book was taken from the Torah.
54.30: From the Torah, their book was taken, but they do not inform within the Torah.
54.31: They practice circumcision, like Jews, yet they heap curses upon the Jews,
54.32: not knowing that they are Jews.
54.33: Spirit has confused them, and sowed dissention among them.
54.34: Each one blames his companion, and they do not know whom they worship.
54.36: From the day Jerusalem was built, until the demon Bezbat came,
54.37: I was unable to dwell among you in the world.
54.38: My garb was not of the flesh, so I might dwell among you in the world.
54.39: I arose and stood, I settled upon the diverter, Truth,
54.41: “Blessed is he, and again blessed is he who takes care of himself.
54.42: Whoever takes care of himself, there is none like him in the world!”
54.44: “How troubled I am, about my disciples who live in this generation!
54.45: They despise the pearls, and make flaws and imperfections in me.
54.46: How troubled I am, about my disciples who live in that generation!
54.47: Spirit unleashes and lets loose upon them impurity and menstruation,
54.48: and hurls them down to darkness’ gates.
54.49: How troubled I am, about my disciples who are held captive in Spirit’s captivity!
54.50: Spirit unleashes and lets loose upon them waves of adultery, prostitution, and fornication,
54.51: and hurls them down to darkness’ gates.
54.52: How troubled I am about my children, the righteous elect!
54.53: Everyone who, in the demon Bezbat’s year, sets a turban upon his head
54.54: is worth ages and generations to me, worth more than a thousand to me!
54.55: When he departs from his body, he will be set among light’s excellencies.
54.56: Anyone who, in the demon Bezbat’s year, has the white banner, the call, and the proclamation,
54.57: and brings splendid banners out to the white Jordan, they will go towards him from light’s place.
54.58: Everyone who calls Manda d’Heyyi to himself, I, Manda d’Heyyi, will be a helper for him.
54.60: when you see Olympian feasts, put your mind to the test or they will change you.
54.61: because the First Age was entirely our families,
54.62: the Second Age was entirely our families,
54.63: the Third Age was entirely our families,
54.64: the Fourth Age is one that is entirely evil, from which evil proceeds.
54.65: This is the secret teaching that comes from my mouth, Splendid Hibel.
54.66: Everyone who hears and heeds it— how established will he be in his place!
54.67: Everyone who neither hears nor heeds it— how afflicted will he be in darkness’ place!
54.68: Hear and heed, my chosen ones, and raise your families to light’s place.”
54.69: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
54.70: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

55.1: “How can I rejoice? It pains me to rejoice in the abode of the wicked!
55.2: How can my heart rejoice at the things I have done within this world?
55.3: How long shall I go, and how shall I sink into all the worlds?
55.4: How long shall I enlighten the excellencies, and lift treasure to the Mighty’s house?
55.5: How can I rejoice, while my soul is yearning for my father?
55.6: How can I rejoice at the things I have done for the poor and the youth?
55.7: How long can I calm my heart, and how long can I settle my guts?
55.8: How long can I empower the excellencies, and bring word to the mighty in the world?
55.9: How long can I hold down demons, and how long can I slay the rebellious?
55.10: Who among you will save me, from Abator on high?
55.11: How long can I bear the things being done to me personally?
55.12: How long am I to reject Sunday, to drive him away,
55.13: How long am I to reject this world? How long am I to bring the power and truth,
55.14: that are lacking in the customs house? How long am I hold down the studs,
55.15: and bring them to the yoke? How long am I to plow and sow seed in the world?
55.16: How long am I to reap and sow, and how long am I to divide the mortals?
55.17: How long am I to triumph over evil, and cast fools into cauldrons to boil?
55.18: How long will the scales remain light, and how long will Abator judge in this world?
55.19: How long am I to beat the sun, and condemn him in this world?
55.20: How long am I to free the righteous elect who are living in this world?
55.21: How long am I to strike out penitentiaries, and the Moon within them?
55.22: How long am I to put him, month by month,
55.23: to put him into the seething cauldron?
55.24: How long will the land accept seed, and yield fruit in the world?
55.25: How long will the ships go down and up to light’s place?
55.26: How long am I to measure living water and pour it into still water?
55.27: How long must the excellencies dwell and endure pollution and wickedness?
55.28: How long will it become dark and bright and how long am I to give pearls to mortals?
55.29: How long am I to hang on my net, and raise up the poor and persecuted?
55.30: How long am I to beat the mountains, and clothe mortals in darkness?
55.31: How long am I to place chains and ropes, on adulterers and thieves of the world?
55.32: How long am I to strike, kill, and triumph, over the wicked and liars living in the world?
55.33: How long am I to make trouble for them, and how long will they kill each other?
55.34: When will the quarrel be resolved, and when will my heart be healed?
55.35: When will Earth come to nought, so that I may hide my fishing net from the world?”
55.36: When Splendid Hibel said this, Manda d’Heyyi spoke to him, saying:
55.37: “How long will you stumble, Splendid Hibel, and be persecuted in this world?
55.38: Out of all the deeds that wicked people have done,
55.39: what is there, upon your shoulders?
55.40: When Splendid Hibel heard so, he sprang up from his throne, stood,
55.41: and opened his mouth in sincerity, saying to Manda d’Heyyi:
55.42: “Upon whose shoulders should Earth, which I created, fall?
55.43: To whom among the excellencies shall I give the things I created and ordered?
55.44: When I created Adam and Eve his wife, and she was formed, persecuted,
55.45: and there was her departure, and I was their persecutor.
55.46: I set up the houses of detention, forged the Jews’ chains,
55.47: I appointed the tax collectors to do all they were commanded to do.
55.48: I have levelled a road from darkness to the everlasting abode.
55.49: I have raised witnesses in Abator’s garrison.
55.50: I brought Abator, and made him judge of the world.
55.51: I assigned him the scales, and gave him authority over the world’s affairs.
55.52: I called the [un]fathomable river into being, and settled Abator upon it.
55.53: I called into being Adatan and Yadatan, the witnesses were two,
55.54: and took them as scribes. I settled them with Abator.
55.55: I called into being the white fruit, in which souls are enveloped.
55.56: They blossom out of it, and they sit upon the scales.
55.57: I called into being streams of water, the Jordan in which souls are baptized.
55.58: I called into being in it a path, so they travel upon the water channels,
55.60: I made a ship for the good, a ferry of souls carrying them,
55.61: over to Abator’s house, who gives them strength and truth from head to toe.
55.62: I brought him to Sunday, and I set him over all the customs houses,
55.64: “Whoever carries a letter will pass by, but whoever does not carry a letter,
55.65: from you they will be hidden.
55.66: All evildoers and liars will be held in your penitentiary,
55.67: until a letter and knowledge from Earth rises to Life’s presence.
55.68: When the letter and knowledge rise to Life’s presence, then a letter
55.69: from Life will come to you.
55.70: When the letter arrives, then they will rise to Abator’s house.
55.71: I have established affairs, and created life and death in the world.
55.73: The souls of those worthy will rise to the light, and those unworthy will sink into the darkness,
55.74: since the seductress Spirit came to seduce the whole world.
55.75: When I saw the clear warning, I warned about her.
55.76: I made a boundary and raised it.
55.77: I tell the Nazoreans, sincere and faithful men
55.78: on the boundary, if they support the boundary, they will rise to see light’s place.
55.79: Whoever deviates from the boundary will support the marker.
55.80: Whoever deviates from both of them will fall, and there is no way back up for him.
55.81: He will fall and has no way back, and the mountain, the dark mountain, will engulf him.
55.82: He will request a second death, and his eyes will never see the light.
55.83: His eye will never see the light, and his foot will never find firm ground.”
55.84: You have triumphed, Manda d’Heyyi, and made all who love your name triumph!

56.1: Whoever stays perfect within it, his settlement will be at the apex of the light worlds.
56.2: The excellencies will gather near to him, and they will extend truth[’s hand] to him.
56.3: To him, they will extend truth[’s hand], and they will receive from him and by them.
56.4: On their heads, they will set a great crown, like the one who enlightens the worlds.
56.5: They will set for him a wreath, a victory wreath, and call him the illuminator of settlements.
56.6: His heart is not one of the Great (Life)’s, unless he is among those versed in truth.
56.7: The one in whom the truth resides, his mind is enlightened,
56.9: The one whose mind is unenlightened and whose heart is unawakened,
56.10: in the settlement of Spirit, the “holy” one, will be settled.
56.11: He will fall into dark cauldrons, and his form will not shine.
56.12: The one whose heart is awakened and whose mind is enlightened,
56.13: shined greater than the sun and the moon.
56.14: He shined greater than the sun and the moon, and set the name and the scent on Earth.
56.15: Each and every day, the disciples gather by his side,
56.16: and take from him the sign, and rise through his power,
56.17: because the power of his ancestors is safeguarded in him,
56.18: and the word of his ancestors resides with him.
56.19: When he rises to the penitentiary, he will not be interrogated,
56.20: and the Seven will not pronounce judgment upon him,
56.21: He will not go upon the “holy” path, and his eyes will not see the darkness.
56.22: He will pass on the righteous elect’s path, Sunday runs a run within it.
56.23: They will rise through secret words, which conceal the darkness from the mortals.
56.24: They will rise through secret mysteries, the likes of which are kept secret from the worlds.
56.25: Blessed and twice blessed is the one who separates himself from the world.
56.26: He will rise to view light’s place.
56.27: The one who did not, got exhausted, and slept, he will be settled in the guts of Leviathan.
56.28: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
56.29: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

57.1: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! A treasure am I—the Mighty’s Treasure!
57.2: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! A crown was I, before the Mighty!
57.3: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! I brought light to excellencies and settlements,
57.4: and was a glimmer upon the Jordan. A glimmer upon the Jordan was I,
57.5: for which there were no forerunners, in which excellencies shine.
57.6: The Great [Life] certainly instructed me, and made me into a garment.
57.7: They make me their garment every day, and praise the air continually.
57.8: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! A crown was I, for the glorious king,
57.9: in whose splendor excellencies shine, and whose appearance they continually praise.
57.10: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure, who is spread over the glorious king,
57.11: a shine that enlightens his mind, so that he is certainly instructed,
57.12: and his appearance shines brighter than the worlds.
57.13: When he shines and enlightens excellencies, and the settlements that are in the air,
57.14: the king clothed Splendid Plant with me. Splendid Plant took me and brought me,
57.15: he made me a garment for the Jordan. He made me a garment for the Jordan,
57.16: which enlightens the excellencies from head to toe.
57.17: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! The wicked are blind and do not see.
57.18: I summon them to the light, those entombed in the darkness.
57.20: “Wicked people, who sink into the darkness, in order to rise, do not sink down!”
57.21: I call out to them but the wicked do not hear, and they sank into the great Ocean.
57.22: Then the Jordan was a cable, a cable for the excellencies it became,
57.23: The excellencies had it and they cut them off, and cast the wicked into the great Ocean.
57.24: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! A crown became I, upon Manda d’Heyyi!
57.25: He put me in authority over the excellencies and the settlements there.
57.26: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! I was the illuminator of the light worlds.
57.27: Each and every day, I praise the Great, and through me they rise to see light’s place.
57.28: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! I was a garment for the worlds of light.
57.29: I am Life’s Treasure, who has advised the Nazoreans.
57.30: I have advised the Nazoreans to praise and confirm in my name.
57.31: They will praise and confirm in my name, and by my name they rise to see light’s place.
57.32: The righteous elect who don me, their eyes are filled with light.
57.33: With light, their eyes are filled, and Manda d’Heyyi dwells in their heart.
57.34: Whosoever dons me, Life’s Treasure, loves neither wife nor children,
57.35: loves neither gold nor silver, loves neither money nor possessions.
57.36: He does not love material food and envy has not fallen upon him.
57.37: Upon him fell no envy, and he did not forget the evening devotionals.
57.38: He did not forget his lessons and books, and did not turn away from his lord’s word.
57.39: He did not turn away from the love of his father, Manda d’Heyyi,and will not fall into the great Ocean.
57.40: He did not forget Sunday and did not neglect the morning prayers.
57.41: He did not forget the Great’s path, the one of reward and charity will be taken away.
57.42: He will be taken during the evening prayer, in the shining garments,
57.43: which the excellencies brought from the Great. He will fill what he lacks, carry him empty-handed.
57.44: When he bears a pure burden, he will be reckoned among the righteous elect.
57.45: He will be reckoned among the righteous elect, who meditate upon Yawar’s Name.
57.46: Life’s Treasure is upon them, she spread light upon their likenesses.
57.47: I will set a road to the Mighty’s house for them. I have called a proclamation and taught disciples there.
57.49: “The vine that is fruitful will rise, and that which is not will be cut off here.
57.50: Whom I taught and instructed will rise; he will see light’s place.
57.51: Whom I didn’t will be cut off; he will fall into the great Ocean.”
57.52: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

58.1: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! The Jordan set a throne for me.
58.2: The Jordans flow with my scent, and the waters rejoice in my splendor.
58.3: The living waters rejoice, and they frolic in the presence of my splendor.
58.4: My splendor and that of the Jordan, they grow strong within them;
58.5: within them, they grow strong, and their appearance shines from head to toe.
58.6: A mighty garment am I, which all who wore, rejoiced and gladdened;
58.7: those who wore me, their scent sweetened, and they became greater than the world.
58.8: A king’s garment am I. I magnify the king,
58.9: and conceal him from the excellencies.
58.10: With my company, he stands guard, and he delights in me and shines.
58.11: From head to toe, he shines with me and is distinguished by me.
58.13: will shine and his form will grow mighty like mine.”
58.14: I was a crown for the king, and at the head of his settlement,
58.15: he set a chair for me from beginning to end.
58.16: When he set a chair for me, all gave obedience to me.
58.17: All to me gave their obedience, they praised my appearance
58.19: Then he spoke to Great Plant, and made a pact with him.
58.20: From his clothes he dressed him, and he dressed me, Life’s Treasure, upon him.
58.21: He dressed me upon him, so that I concealed his appearance,
58.23: “Go with the power of Life’s Treasure. All your works will be secure.
58.24: Secure will be all your works, and you chose one who is like you and guards you,
58.25: since the one for whom the garment is destined, is destined to stand apart from you,
58.26: but he will give his obedience to you.
58.27: A treasure am I—Life’s Treasure! Life’s Sam, with their splendid tartabuna,
58.28: sent me to adamantine worlds, to adamantine worlds he sent me,
58.29: to be a garment for the king, to enlighten his form in his settlement,
58.30: to spread greater glory, so excellencies might shine in his appearance.
58.31: We ride forth and travel, we pass by in ships of light.
58.32: In light ships we pass by, and come up to the border region.
58.33: Our splendor shone upon adamantine worlds, they shone by the power of Life’s Treasure.
58.34: By the power of Life’s Treasure they shone, they came out before Life’s Treasure,
58.36: “Blessed is your arrival, Life’s Treasure, in whose perfume excellencies delight,
58.37: and within whom the settlements are bright.”
58.38: Then Great Plant installed her whose advice the Great has vindicated,
58.39: and whose secret name is kept for Yukabar.

59.2: Life’s Sam gave me a pure garment, within which worlds shine.
59.3: He gave me a girdle, a girdle of living waters, in which there are no pains or afflictions.
59.4: He gave me a great crown, in whose splendor the worlds shine.
59.5: He gave me a pleasing smell, so that the waters delight with my scent.
59.6: He gave me a great power, that shines forth and enlightens continually.
59.7: He gave me secret helpers, and appointed watchers over me.
59.8: He gave me a great victory, through which the Jordans were purified.
59.9: When they mention my name over the Jordan, then they place my strength upon it,
59.10: and the Jordan rises up within me, and the excellencies have the truth.
59.11: It gives them speech and hearing, and purifies them from the mortal realm.
59.12: It gives them a shining appearance and my strength and heroics
59.14: It transplanted Great Plant, whom it clothed within me.
59.15: My power enlightens the worlds, and brings down water courses.
59.16: It brings down bodies of living water.
59.17: By my power and that of water and air, splendid lands took shape.
59.18: By my power and that of water and air, splendid settlements were founded.
59.19: By my power and that of water and air, excellencies have fruits, vines, and trees.
59.20: They planted for them splendid clouds, which brought speech and hearing.
59.21: They gave them a pure sign, consecrated by their power.
59.22: They will be consecrated by their power, and set upon the pure boundary.
59.23: They will be set upon splendid thrones, and called the heads of the worlds.
59.24: Each will be more magnificent than the last.
59.25: He with whom the secret of his ancestors and the words of his ancestors abide,
59.26: is more exalted than all the excellencies, and his form is exalted, shines and enlightens,
59.27: like the splendid sparks in light’s place.
59.28: By my power and that of water and air, order was given to all the worlds of light.
59.29: Order was given to all the worlds of light, and they had power over them.
59.30: We set them in order and enlighten them and made our works rise to the summit.
59.31: We made a passage for the excellencies, and they gave treasures to the worlds.
59.32: They gave a creation to the king, since it was created by them.
59.33: We sally forth and move on, and we come upon Big Sam.
59.34: We address Big Sam, and we say to him,
59.35: “Your splendor is constant, your form is bright, because it spread your beauty over us.”
59.36: We gave power to Big Sam, entirely over the settlements and the Jordans.
59.37: We sally forth and move on, and we come upon Splendid Yawar.
59.38: When we reached Splendid Yawar, we addressed Splendid Yawar,
59.39: “You are a father of excellencies, and lord of all the settlements.
59.40: [The Life] has surely created for you, and given you authority over the enclosure,
59.41: and over all the works of light’s place.”
59.42: Then Manda d’Heyyi clothed himself with us, and we placed our power and secret on him.
59.43: We sally forth and move on, and we come upon Yushamen’s house.
59.44: When we arrived at Yushamen’s house, our splendor shined forth upon Yushamen.
59.45: Upon Yushamen’s house shined our splendor. Yushamen was engaged in plotting.
59.46: When he was engaged in plotting, he left through the gate of his shell.
59.47: When we saw him, we address to him,
59.48: “You are our great father and the first one, and your splendor shines forth in passing,
59.49: Your movements are in Life’s house, and your deeds are recognized in light’s place.
59.50: They call you the arranger of ordinances, you are the lord of all goodness!”
59.51: I gave him light and clarity, and I set him up in his settlement forever.
59.52: We sally forth and move on, and we come upon Abator’s house.
59.53: When we arrived at Abator’s house, our splendor shined forth upon Abator.
59.54: Abator sprung up, rose from his throne, and made a petition to Life.
59.55: To Life he made a petition, on account of the wrongful deeds he had done.
59.56: The three excellencies said to him, “Ladies rejoice and rejoice,
59.57: that truth is in this man, who is dressed in the garb of splendor.
59.58: He is dressed in the garb of splendor, and light is cast over his shoulders.
59.59: Our father weighs with the scales, and signs with the pure sign.”
59.60: Then I appointed Abator, over the great Jordan of living water,
59.61: and over the souls that rise to the everlasting abode,
59.62: and over the goodwill and praise that rise from the world.
59.63: I posted him over the Seven and the Twelve, for him to command and be obeyed completely.
59.65: “Why do you fail, Abator, when you were transplanted from the hidden places?
59.66: Why do you fail, Abator, when you are from the pure splendor?
59.67: Why do you fail, Abator, and grow angry with Ptahil,
59.69: Now it is perversity and wickedness that come from the two of you;
59.70: the souls suffer from their faults and are turned away.
59.71: The one who stands firmly will rise on truth’s paths,
59.72: he will rise to light’s place.
59.73: The one who does not stand firmly, he will end up at the end of the world.”
59.74: I have concealed Abator from the Seven and protected his treasure, from top to bottom.
59.75: I gave him light and clarity. We put some of the air’s scent upon him.
59.76: We confirmed his deeds, and confirmed his speech, from start to finish.
59.77: We sally forth and move on, and we come upon Excellent Ptahil.
59.78: When we arrived at Excellent Ptahil, he was filled with love,
59.80: “If it pleases my father, Manda d’Heyyi, quickly send a boon to me,
59.81: that they lift the clouds of darkness for me. Each and every single day
59.82: brings perversion and wickedness to mind, need and failure,
59.83: because my father became angry with me.”
59.85: “The chosen one whom the Life sent to them, and set up a throne for him in light’s place,
59.86: we will surely enlighten him, and raise him to the everlasting abode.”
59.88: “If the disciples have made mistakes, if the Seven set stumbling blocks,
59.89: I will be surrounded within a cloud of darkness!
59.90: If the Great grows angry with me, will I be mentioned before the Great?”
59.91: Manda d’Heyyi spoke to Excellent Ptahil, saying,
59.92: “You will be held responsible for the stumbling blocks and the disciples,
59.93: since the planets came into being from your wrath, rage, and lust.
59.94: You have given them power over the disciples that sin against the Mighty and offend him.
59.95: He will set passion and lust upon them, and put them at the end of the world.
59.96: They will ply with intoxicants the world’s children who are held back.
59.97: If they sin against the disciples, it will be through your foolishness, Ptahil.
59.98: If your disciples sin, it will be through your foolishness, Ptahil.”
59.99: Thus spoke Manda d’Heyyi, and he responds to Excellent Ptahil,
59.101: “Our father, the chosen without flaw, desired that Yawar be a helper for you.
59.102: Yawar was a helper for you, and Sunday was a savior for you.
59.103: The Great [Life] knows your name, and has surely created the Jordan that sent you.”
59.105: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

60.1: To you I speak and teach, my perfect chosen people,
60.2: who are living within this world.
60.3: Don’t be part of the darkness, but set your eyes upon light’s place.
60.4: Distinguish death from life, and do not be a liar when you speak.
60.5: Distinguish the wicked from the good, and yourselves from the wicked sinners of darkness’s
60.7: Love and teach one another, and your sins and trespasses will be forgiven.
60.8: If you watch, listen, and learn, then you will successfully rise to light’s place.
60.9: Good people sit and argue, and how they argue and learn!
60.10: Good people talk and advise one another, and say,
60.11: “Who will come and who will tell me? Who will make me know and who will instruct me?
60.12: Who will come, and tell me, whether it was one king or two?”
60.13: Good people tell tales, instructing one another,
60.14: “There were two kings, and two natures were created:
60.15: The king of this world, and the king of the ages beyond.
60.16: The king of this age donned darkness’s sword and crown.
60.17: He donned darkness’s crown, and took its sword in his right hand.
60.18: In his right hand, he took his sword, and began to slaughter his sons.
60.19: He began to slaughter his sons, and his sons killed one another.
60.20: The king of the worlds beyond and the king of the ages beyond,
60.21: the king of the worlds beyond assumed light’s crown;
60.22: He assumed light’s crown, and took Truth in his right hand.
60.23: He took Truth in his right hand, and began to instruct his sons.
60.24: He began to instruct his sons, and his sons instructed one another.
60.25: ‘Who will come, and who will tell me: who and what were here,
60.26: before the firmament stretched forth, before the stars were formed within it,
60.27: before Earth condensed, before the condensation fell upon the waters,
60.28: before the sun and the moon go about within this world,
60.30: ‘When it was sitting in the vessel, the soul neither hungered nor thirsted.
60.31: When it was sitting in the vessel, the soul had neither diseases nor infirmities.
60.32: When it was sitting in the vessel, the soul had neither heat nor cold.
60.33: When it was sitting in the vessel, its locks were pleated,
60.34: and wreaths of air were set upon its head.
60.35: Its eyes were beams of light, gazing upon the place of the Mighty’s house.
60.36: Its mouth was pure perfection, and praised the king of light’s place.’
60.37: From the day the evil one began to think, wickedness grew within him.
60.38: He grew extremely angry, and waged war against the light.
60.39: A messenger was sent, to crush the strength of the rebels.
60.40: They brought the living waters, and put them into the still waters.
60.41: They brought the shining light, and put it into the gloomy darkness.
60.42: They brought the gentle breeze, and put it into the blustering wind.
60.43: They brought the living fire, and put it into the devouring flame.
60.44: They brought the soul, the pure mind, and put it into the mortal body.
60.45: From fire and water, a single firmament stretched forth.
60.46: From fire and water, they made Earth solid upon its foundation.
60.47: From fire and water, there came fruits, vines, and trees.
60.48: From fire and water, there was formed Adam in the flesh.
60.49: They baptized the messenger, and sent him to the end of the ages.
60.50: He called a proclamation out into the world’s chaos.
60.51: Adam, the sleeper, awoke to the messenger’s voice;
60.52: Adam, the sleeper, awoke and went out to the messenger’s side.
60.53: ‘Come in peace, messenger, Life’s emissary, who came from my father’s house!
60.54: How did the precious and beautiful Life plant after them?
60.55: How did they prepare the throne for me, and will my dark form sit here in sorrow?’
60.56: The messenger spoke and said to Adam in the flesh, saying:
60.57: ‘The thrones that they prepared for you are fair, but your form will sit here in sorrow.
60.58: All will remember you for good, and they took pleasure in me and sent me to you.
60.59: I have come and I shall instruct you, Adam, and I shall save you from this world.
60.60: If you take heed, listen, and learn, then you will successfully rise up to light’s place.’
60.61: Adam listened and became faithful; blessed is he who listens and believes after you.
60.62: Adam made a pact; blessed is he who makes a pact after you.
60.63: Adam anticipated and rose up; blessed is he who rises up after you.”
60.64: Take heed, listen, and learn, perfect ones, and rise up to light’s place in triumph.
60.66: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

61.1: “Who will come forth, and who will tell me? Who will let me know, and who will instruct me?
61.2: Who will come forth, and who will tell me?
61.3: Who opened the splendid Euphrates’ floodgates, and who excavated its two banks?
61.4: Who formed the earth, and stretched out the firmament completely?
61.5: Who stretched forth the bright banners, and enlightened excellencies in their settlements?
61.6: Who performed the living baptism, and who made the mark of the pure sign?
61.7: Who sowed seed within it, and who served as the watcher within it?
61.8: Who settled in it settlements, and who built within it tents?
61.9: Who proclaimed Life’s call, and brought light to the great palace?
61.10: Who achieved success with it, and wove the wreaths from start to finish?
61.11: Who set Aquarius within it, and was called ‘the healer’ therein?
61.12: Who chose the Great’s portion, and successfully brought it up to light’s place?”
61.13: “Life will surely know, Life will know without asking!
61.15: Yawar opened a mouth for the splendid Euphrates, and Yushamen excavated its two banks.
61.16: Ptahil formed Earth, and stretched out the firmament completely.
61.17: Behram stretched forth the bright banners, and enlightened excellencies in their settlements.
61.18: Shelmey performed the living baptism, and Nedbey made the mark of the pure sign.
61.19: Adam sowed the seed, and Shitel served as the watcher within it.
61.20: Excellent Ennosh set within it settlements, and built within it tents.
61.21: Hibel called forth with Life’s voice, and brought light to the great palace.
61.22: Yukashar achieved success with it, and wove the crown from start to finish.
61.23: Heyya-Shom set Aquarius within it, and was called ‘the healer’ therein.
61.24: Life’s Son chose the Great’s portion, and successfully brought it up to light’s place.”
61.25: And Life triumphs, and the man who went here triumphs!
61.26: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

62.1: When Earth did not yet exist, and the world had not been called into being,
62.2: When it had not yet condensed, nor had that which is solid been called into being,
62.3: When the waters were still black, Splendid Hibel went forth,
62.4: and Shitel, Shehlon, and Ayar, and they came to stand upon Earth.
62.5: Hibel set a boundary and measured the water, dividing it up inch by inch.
62.6: As Shehlon stood, his mind became filled with spite
62.7: against Splendid Hibel and Splendid Ayar, so he said to them,
62.8: “My brothers, you foolish excellencies, you excellencies without polish or beauty,
62.9: this world to which you have brought me, there will be for it no land out of it,
62.10: and out of it no firmament will be made up, the black water will not dry up,
62.11: and no land will be called up, from this world that you have called up.
62.12: How will Adam ever have Eve, his wife? How will Adam’s children ever exist?
62.13: How will they sink and rise? How will the shells and settlements exist?
62.14: How will he get his strength? How will he get his sweet scents?
62.15: How will fragrant herbs and aromas waft up to Adam from this black water?
62.16: {How will he ever find a wife?} How will the elder myrtle be planted,
62.17: and all the other fragrant plants, just as marjoram and tarragon are planted?
62.18: How will Splendid Qamamir exist here?
62.19: How will he plant here flowers, vegetables, medicinal herbs, and seeds?
62.20: How will they come from this black water? How will there be a muddy land?
62.21: Studs, cattle, and the plow, how will they be called into being?
62.22: How will the earth be plowed, and how will the seed fall on the ground?
62.23: How will the Adam’s children go forth, and with what will they reap it?
62.24: With what will they pound it, and how will Adam make the morsel and eat it?
62.25: How will the white ewe come into being? How will she go down and up?
62.26: How will she become pregnant and give birth? How will the wheels of light be summoned,
62.27: and grind for Adam so that he may eat? How will the firmament and the winged birds be?
62.28: How will the white dove be summoned, and become Adam’s companion?”
62.29: As Shehlon said this, Ptahil stepped forward and said to him,
62.30: “I will form that which is solid, and Ayar will breath upon it;
62.31: I will flush out the black water, and Hibel will make a drain for it.
62.32: I will create Earth, he will bring a garment from Ur,
62.33: Hibel and Shitel will stretch out the canopy.”
62.34: Shehlon became full of wrath against Ptahil and said to him,
62.35: “You are a wicked son of a bastard, Life will not accept your offering.
62.36: Who are you among excellencies and men, to call the world into being?”
62.37: As Shehlon said so, Ptahil plunged into the black water,
62.38: and the black waters flooded out. Shitel and Hibel opened a drain for the water.
62.39: They made its floods into Earth’s land as if the water were not there.
62.40: Ayar buffeted it with his wings, and as Shehlon stood, it became dry ground.
62.41: Ptahil pounded in the columns, Hibel stretched out the firmament,
62.42: Shitel made its spheres, and Ennosh joined the bow to it.
62.44: Yusmir, Shehrun, and Behron were the carpenters,
62.45: They framed the ship, and made for it a bow and stern.
62.46: Hibel made its neighbor, he brought it to the Jordan,
62.47: and turned it around under Earth. He set up a measure, measured the water,
62.48: and poured the living water, as it entered still waters,
62.49: and the living water wept, as it mixed with still waters.
62.50: Just as living water mixed with still water, darkness mixed with light.
62.51: They brought Yushamen, set him on Earth,
62.53: “Give us your children, so they may orbit Earth,
62.54: and bring light to this world we are making, and we will establish families,
62.55: from which you may take your share.”
62.56: They brought the sun and Zehrun, and they brought the great moon.
62.57: They put them in order and brought them, set them on the Jordan, and told them:
62.58: “You will be a light source, by day on Earth,
62.59: and when you are concealed, you, moon will be a light source in the night,
62.60: so that neither a terrestrial war nor a celestial war will arise,
62.61: and they will have power over Adam and his wife.”
62.62: They received the sun by day and the moon they received by night.
62.63: They brought forth the great Venus, the great Jupiter, the great Saturn,
62.64: and the great Mars, and they made him a ship.
62.65: They brought Little Eve, gave her a share,
62.67: They appointed Yushamen’s sons for eighty years,
62.68: then Yushamen’s sons didn’t want it, and they brought them to the planets.
62.69: Each of them received a share.

63.1: A voice from on high cried out to us. It chose Intellect.
63.2: It sent Intellect to us, from the everlasting abode.
63.3: Intellect goes forth and comes to those who know him and believe in him,
63.4: and those who know his acquaintances. They shook off their white garments,
63.5: their white garments they shook off, and adjusted splendid wreaths.
63.6: They set them on their heads, and went out towards the Intellect.
63.7: They knelt down and bowed before him, and stretched out their bodies.
63.9: “Whence comes your date palm? Whence comes your roots and your date palm?
63.10: Whence comes the one who planted you?”
63.11: The gentle Intellect replied to those who know me, saying,
63.12: “My roots are from Life, and my date palm is from light’s place.
63.13: The men who created my garments are intellects of the everlasting abode.
63.14: My sons made the summoning, and I came to awaken this world.
63.15: Blessed is the one who heeds my speech, and walks along my path;
63.16: Whoever heeds Manda d’Heyyi’s speech will see the Great Life.
63.17: Whoever doesn’t heed Manda d’Heyyi’s speech will fall into a blazing fire,
63.18: and it will be their dwelling place until the great judgment day,
63.19: when I will be a witness against him: I was a herald who called him.
63.20: I called into his ear, but he didn’t listen. I called and he didn’t listen with his ear.
63.21: I showed it to his eye and he didn’t look. I showed it, but he didn’t look with his eye.”
63.23: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

64.1: I have come to this world, to make a creation of Life,
64.2: to make Life’s creation, and draw down the Jordan from top to bottom.
64.3: They brought from Life, those who were from Life.
64.4: They brought living waters to set up Jordans with them,
64.5: to make petitions of the Great, and plant the thriving scions,
64.6: to plant and give them living waters to drink, give them the Great’s speech to hear,
64.7: and the word that Life said to me.
64.8: I teach them praise, and they start to praise the mighty,
64.9: the mighty and the creatures whom they saw. Those come out against me,
64.10: the mighty and the creatures come out, in order to take snares after snares.
64.11: They take snares after snares, and consult one another.
64.12: They consult one another, and plot evil against me.
64.14: “Come, let’s go and ask him about his home. Let’s ask him, and tell him,
64.15: about the place from which he came. Let’s ask him, and tell him,
64.16: ‘This splendor—who clothed you in it? Who clothed you in this splendor,
64.17: so that your appearance is so sublime? So sublime is your appearance,
64.18: and your splendor brightens this world. So sublime is your appearance,
64.19: and your beauty sweetens the worlds.’”
64.20: I spoke to the mighty who were dwelling there, the Seven,
64.21: I spoke, saying to the Seven children of the mortal abode,
64.22: “A great one am I, son of the Great, by whose power I went there.
64.23: I have come to cry Life’s call, and to arouse Life’s tribe,
64.24: to plant the scions of the successful, and the offshoots of the great,
64.25: to plant [them] and teach them good, to teach them prayer and praise,
64.26: so they may start to praise the mighty, so they may praise Splendid Yukabar,
64.27: the man who was a helper, a helper was he,
64.28: from darkness’s place to light’s place.

65.1: In a bright cloud, I sit. From Life’s house, I went there.
65.2: I went there and I came, as far as the abode of the wicked.
65.3: I came upon seven figures, and found them all sitting in mourning.
65.4: All of them were sitting in mourning, and scattered ashes on Spirit’s head.
65.5: They scattered ashes on Spirit’s head, and took pleasure in unpleasant deeds.
65.6: They were speaking with wicked talk, they said with lustful words,
65.8: “Come, let’s assume a false guise, Come, let’s appoint a head.
65.9: Let’s appoint a head, and give out fruits to the world.
65.10: Let’s give out fruits to the world, and issue an empty summons.
65.11: Let’s make a call, like the man who went here. Let’s summon them to worship you,
65.12: let’s make them listen, fill them with perversity, sit down, teach them,
65.14: ‘Why have you abandoned our words? Why have you abandoned our words,
65.15: and changed what we have said?’
65.16: Let’s sit down and tell them, before the strange man goes there.”
65.17: I saw them, mocked them, and laughed at all of them.
65.18: I shone in my abounding splendor, so that I became visible to the nations.
65.19: The nations that saw me grew frightened, and the house’s godhead shook in fear.
65.20: Spirit fell from her throne, and all the nations scattered.
65.21: The Seven trampled their robes, and did not forget what they had done.
65.22: All of them held their heads low, and fell down upon their faces.
65.23: Down they fell upon their faces, they raised [their faces],
65.24: “O Lord, we have really sinned! Please forgive us our sins.”
65.25: As soon as I was armed, and sealed against the nations,
65.26: I spoke and I said to the Seven children of the mortal abode,
65.27: “When I came, to work here, the Great sought to send me
65.28: so I would come to do good. I will do good, and extend a blessing to my friends.
65.29: I will explain to them your wicked advice, in which there is no light.
65.30: I will explain to them your speech, lest they listen to your talk.
65.31: Why would they listen to your words, and why would they remain within your world?”
65.32: My chosen people certainly listened to me, all of them were good.
65.33: They were all good, and they raised their faces to light’s place.
65.35: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

66.1: Way out beyond, in the splendid fruits, in light’s courts,
66.2: in the perfect house, within you, Ayar’s garden, is insight.
66.3: within you, Adam’s garden, is a proclamation, called forth by Life.
66.4: Whatever the great say, they tell stories with glory.
66.5: They say things with glory, they say the proclamation’s words.
66.6: They reveal the secrets that were once held between father and son.
66.7: Before there was this abode, before all this existed,
66.8: before the sun and the moon existed, and went into the world,
66.9: The splendor within its vessel blazed, and the light blazed within their garb,
66.10: the words were hidden, hidden and guarded within their books.
66.11: The winds kept the peace, and settled upon the world’s wilderness.
66.12: The produce that is entirely splendor, and the light that is entirely beams,
66.13: the Lord of Greatness has set and confirmed in the perfect house.
66.14: The great first one spoke, saying to the first, his son,
66.15: “My son, come be a messenger for me, come, bear a burden for me,
66.16: come, for me bear a burden, and tread down the rebellious lands for me.
66.17: Go to the realm of darkness, in the darkness that has no tinge of light
66.18: to the place of the lions, to the den of savage leopards,
66.19: to the place of dragons, to the den of the devastating demons,
66.20: to the place of the liliths, and the Astartes like veiled women,
66.21: to the place of the water-torrents, and the courts of devouring pitch.”
66.22: The first spoke, saying to the great, his father,
66.23: “If I go down, who will bring me up? If I fall down, who will grab me?
66.24: Who will embrace my soul, so that we do not fall into the devouring waters?
66.25: Who will form a solid space for me, so that we do not fall into still waters?
66.26: My wreath, the beams of splendor, who will set it upon my head?
66.27: If the wicked capture me within their fortress, who will be my savior?”
66.28: The great spoke, saying to the first, his son,
66.29: “If you go down, who will bring me up? If you fall down, I will grab you.
66.30: Who will embrace your soul, so that you do not fall into the devouring waters?
66.31: I shall form a solid space for you, so that you do not fall into still waters.
66.32: Your wreath, the beams of light, I shall set upon your head.
66.33: If the wicked throw you within their fortress, I shall be your redeemer.
66.34: Rise in the name of Life, gather the beams of light,
66.35: don the helmet of the worlds, and go to the realm of darkness,
66.36: in the darkness that has no tinge of light.”
66.37: Lions would have surrounded me, devastating demons would have surrounded me,
66.38: Dragons, liliths, and the Astartes like veiled women would have surrounded me,
66.39: water-torrents and fields of devouring pitch would have surrounded me,
66.40: if it were not for the strength from me, if it were not that I am a disciple, a disciple’s voice.”
66.41: He submitted to the man, his creator. The Lord of Greatness said to him,
66.42: “Why have I sinned against you and sent you, and why have I sent you here,
66.43: to the depth in which everything is corrupt, in which none can abide?”
66.44: When Sprout heard this from me, he sent me a staff,
66.45: that bestowed upon me hearing and speech, and said to me,
66.46: “Go slay the lions with it! Go slay the savage leopards with it!
66.47: Go slay the dragons with it! Go slay the devastating demons with it!
66.48: Go slay with it the liliths and the veiled Astartes!
66.49: Go dry up the water-torrents and the courts of devouring pitch.”
66.50: I raised a cry to Life’s house. It had sent me strength and splendor.
66.51: I set in order the things, about which my father had ordered me.
66.52: I crushed the darkness, and established the light throughout.
66.53: I rose without any fault, and had no flaw or imperfection.
66.54: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
66.55: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

67.1: From beyond, an excellency cries out and instructs the man Adam.
67.3: “Do not sleep, and do not lie down. Do not forget what your lord commanded you,
67.4: Do not be a child of the house, and do not be called guilty in Earth.
67.5: Do not fall in love with fragrant wreaths, and take no pleasure in an alluring woman.
67.6: Do not fall in love with perfumes, and do not neglect your evening devotionals.
67.7: Do not fall in love with false shadows, alluring prostitutes,
67.9: Do not drink and become drunk, and do not forget your Lord from your mind.
67.10: When coming and when going, watch out, you’ll forget your Lord!
67.11: When standing and when sitting, watch out, you’ll forget your Lord!
67.12: When coming and when going, watch out, you’ll forget your Lord!
67.13: When resting and when sleeping, watch out, you’ll forget your Lord!
67.14: Say not, ‘I am a beloved son, there is nothing wrong with anything I do.’
67.15: Adam, take a look at the world, a thing in which there is nothing
67.17: He sets the scales upright, out of a thousand, he brings over only one.
67.18: He will bring over one out of a thousand, and out of ten thousand, only two.
67.19: Fragrant wreaths are worthless, they will be as if they had never been [...]
67.20: Everyone who lapses into adultery, his trial will be in the fire.
67.21: Everyone who lapses into theft, will be bound in the dark mountain.
67.22: Everyone who sleeps with his friend’s wife, his trial will be in the fire,
67.24: Everyone who sleeps with a widow should be bound in the dark mountain.
67.25: Everyone who sleeps with [an unmarried] bride, will be tortured in the twin wheels,
67.27: Whoever abandons one and takes another will be tortured in the fire-pots.
67.28: The woman who commits adultery will become kindling for an oven,
67.29: and should not behold Life’s house.
67.30: Everyone who goes to fortune-tellers and false astrologers,
67.31: will be tortured in vessels of ice.
67.32: Everyone who drinks wine in a tavern and gets drunk,
67.33: engaging in drums, revelry, and whoring within it,
67.34: they should tear him apart with asphalt rakes, and he will not behold Abator.
67.35: Everyone who goes unto a songstress and sows his illegitimate seed,
67.36: she gets pregnant by him, takes poison goes out to the dung heap, puts the child down,
67.37: digs a hole and buries it, and with her heel she tramples it,
67.38: and the eyes of the child see its mother but the mother does not see the child.
67.39: The child will die in the dung heap, and its mother will weep secretly for it.
67.40: He will be interrogated in that penitentiary of the enraged and furious dogs.
67.41: She should be interrogated [in that penitentiary of] the deaf and mute,
67.42: and she will not behold the light, and her name should be erased from Life’s house.
67.43: Everyone who approaches his wife, and does not wash in water,
67.44: should dwell in the bowels of Leviathan.
67.45: The woman, who does not wash in water, should be beaten with blow upon blow,
67.46: and the pure name should curse her, and she should not have the final release.
67.47: Light’s watcher should strike her, and her name should be erased from Life’s house.
67.48: The man who sleeps with his wife, that first day when she washes away
67.49: uncleanliness and menstruation, they should raise him into clouds of darkness.
67.50: Everyone who practices usury, and charges interest on gold and silver,
67.51: They should raise him into the dark mountain.
67.52: Everyone who loves gold and silver, and does no good within it,
67.53: should die two deaths instead of one, and get cut off.
67.54: Everyone who breathes in Life’s scent and does not mention Life’s name over it
67.55: should be interrogated in Abator’s house.
67.56: Everyone who does disgusting deeds will be taken by the Seven’s sword and blade.
67.57: Everyone who dyes his hands and feet, and distorts the likeness his Lord ordained for him,
67.58: He will hold the coals in his hand, and he will kindle the flame with his lips.
67.59: He will ask for death but will not die.
67.60: Life will not approach him, and neither let him die,
67.61: nor will he be relieved from his suffering, to rise to see light’s place,
67.62: He will not be condemned in sin’s abode, because of the baptism he received.
67.63: Everyone who loves colorful fabrics and colors will be clothed in darkness.
67.64: They will cover him with gloomy shrouds, and put blazing sandals on his feet.
67.65: Darkness goes out before him, and gloom comes after him.
67.66: He will have demons beside him, because he loved colors and colorful fabrics.
67.67: He will be bound in the penitentiaries until his spirit becomes perfect.”
67.68: To you I am speaking and explaining, the souls of my righteous elect,
67.70: Do not do disgusting deeds, lest you sink down to darkness’ place.
67.71: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
67.72: In the name of the Great Life, and in the name of the precious truth!

68.7: “Who are you, from the Great [Life], and who are you, to rise up to the Jordans?” […]

68.16: Get up, Droplet Steady, whom Life has built and edified.

69.1: The light was planted, and the hidden light shined forth,
69.2: which was planted from the droplet’s light.

69.4: and gave him a response, saying,
69.5: “You are a son of new splendors, you are a son of precious lights,
69.6: You are a son of pure hidden mountains, you are a son safeguarded by Intellect,
69.7: whose name is entrusted to the excellencies and is hidden by the excellencies.”
69.8: Manda d’Heyyi comes and goes until he arrived at Splendid Plant.
69.9: When Splendid Plant saw him, he sprang up from his throne,
69.11: “Light up the giant mirror, in which your ancestors shined,
69.12: Bring light to the settlements, and bring light to the excellencies within them!”

69.15: “You are a son of new mirrors, and you are a son of hidden settlements,
69.16: You are a son of the excellencies’ image, and you are a son of the mighties’ praise.”

69.21: the myrtle who [is the eldest of] all the settlements,

69.23: blessed is the glorious throne on which you sit, blessed is the wand you hold in your hand,

69.27: “Blessed is the creator who created you, he has given you such greatness,
69.28: and made you a great one, like the precious Intellect,
69.29: and made you Truth, beloved by all excellencies.”

69.47: “Come, come, hidden splendor, light that burns in the world,

69.50: glorious king of all the excellencies.”
69.51: When the droplet said so, Manda d’Heyyi bowed down and praised her,
69.53: “They call you Firm on high. By your side, the excellencies gather.

69.55: since you, Droplet, are Firm, you are the first creation.”
69.56: Manda d’Heyyi comes and goes until he arrives at Droplet Pearl.

69.59: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!

70.3: “I shall not be the scales, I am an excellency of the good.

70.5: I shall not stand in these waters, and the souls, who are polluted,
