71.1: When they went forth and came to Abator, Abator was hidden within his shell,
71.3: “Out of all the excellencies, why have you made me the owner of the scales,
71.4: expelled me from my settlement, destroying and devastating my world,
71.5: and removing my bed from me, so that the truth will never be given to me?”
71.6: When Abator said this, Splendid Hibel went to his ancestors,
71.8: “How hidden away is Abator within his shell! He rants from his shell,
71.10: ‘I shall never come out and take the scales, and never be called the owner of the scales.’”
71.11: When Splendid Hibel had said this, the king became filled with rage,
71.12: and cried out in the world. Twice he cried out,
71.13: and the settlements kept silent until the third time.
71.14: Little Sam responded to him, and said to him,
71.15: “I shall go down to the Nether, and be the scale man,
71.16: and be called the era’s head.”
71.19: You will never be the owner of the scales, and never be called reliable and successful.
71.20: Summon Abator, who is a gentle excellency.”
71.21: The triumphant Life speaks, and the light wins, and those who love its name.
71.22: In the name of the Great Life, and in the name of the precious truth!

72.1: When he came to Abator, Abator arose from his throne,
72.2: since the king commanded him, and he is careful of the high king,
72.3: he is careful of the splendor of all the upper worlds.
72.4: Abator comes and goes, and excellencies came to his left and right,
72.5: and they drew near the king and sat down.
72.6: Abator spoke, saying to the Pure Intellect,
72.7: “I am only one of these numerous excellencies; why did you send for me?”
72.9: “Of all the settlements and excellencies like you in all these worlds of light,
72.10: there isn’t anyone gentle like you, you are gentle, and you are efficient.
72.11: Your heart is great, and you will support the souls.
72.12: You will have compassion for the souls, and you will be the judge.”
72.13: And then Abator spoke to Intellect,
72.14: “Tell Splendid Hibel, if he will be the judge, then I will be the owner of the scales!”
72.15: And then Splendid Hibel-Yawar says to Abator,
72.16: “When I am the judge, who will establish the settlements?
72.17: When I am the judge, who will be the king in these worlds?”
72.19: “I shall be the king, and I shall establish the settlements.”
72.20: When Abator said this, Hibel-Yawar clenched his fists,
72.21: and turned into the owner of the scales for fifty-five years.
72.22: He was the scale man, and raised excellencies and settlements.
72.23: When Splendid Hibel said this, the Great Life accepted the blessing,
72.24: and became filled with rage about Abator. He came, cast him down from his throne,
72.25: set him at the Nether Gate, and said to him,
72.26: “Go, and be the judge, as long as the Great Life wants you to be.”
72.27: And then Splendid Hibel said to Sunday,
72.28: “Come, sit in the customs houses, and let me be the owner of the scales,
72.29: and we shall call the settlements into being!”
72.30: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
72.31: In the name of the Great Life, and in the name of the precious truth!

73.1: A white eagle am I, whose ancestors have forgotten him.
73.3: Woe to the excellency whose ancestors hate him!
73.4: Such is the fate of each excellency who heeds his ancestors’ chatter!
73.5: Whoever heeds his ancestors’ chatter, they cast him down, and set him at darkness’ gates.
73.7: I heeded my ancestors’ chatter. I have fallen, and there is no way up for me.
73.8: I have sought, but did not find. I have run, but did not pass.
73.9: I took the blame upon myself, so great is my splendor.
73.10: I set it inside the darkness.
73.11: I have drawn the excellencies’ contempt, and the excellencies will not approach me.
73.12: I am laid upon the bed of darkness, and have rested in the trappings of darkness.
73.13: So, such is the fate of every man, the excellency who sinks into the darkness!
73.14: This crown of mine upon my brow, Zahriel has set it upon my head.
73.15: Gone are the speech and hearing that my ancestors gave me.
73.16: I, Splendid Hibel, am within the darkness, I sit by the sides of the walls,
73.18: I said that I would be great, who has made me so small on Earth?
73.19: I said that I would be gentle, and support the lowly and the poor;
73.20: I said, “Listen to the speech of the Great! How sublime is the turban he has given me!”
73.21: I said that I would be meek and submissive, the path on which the righteous great and small pass;
73.22: I said that I would be king; who has made me for darkness’ place?
73.23: I am concerned about my ancestors, and about unleashing Ur upon them.
73.24: I am concerned about my brothers and sisters, and about unleashing darkness upon them.
73.25: I am concerned about what I’ve planted, only to abandon it at the gates of darkness.
73.26: So, such is the fate of every man, who would be gentle!
73.27: To the excellency who is called gentle, they will give neither wife nor shell.
73.28: Neither wife nor shell will they give him, nor will they give him children to sire.
73.29: They will not settle an excellency called gentle. Sublime is the chinstrap they have given him!
73.30: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
73.31: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

74.1: Excellent Ennosh spoke, praising the man, his creator,
74.3: “How I grieve for my disciples who were cast into darkness!
74.4: How I grieve for my disciples’ children, upon whom were thrown much filth!
74.5: How I grieve for my disciples’ children, upon whom
74.6: Spirit has spread pollution, and cast them down!”
74.7: Excellent Ennosh spoke, saying to Life, his ancestors,
74.8: “If it pleases you, my ancestors, let the span of my disciples be finished,
74.9: and let my disciplines rise to light’s place.”
74.10: Life, his ancestors, spoke, saying to Excellent Ennosh,
74.11: “How could we raise the disciples, whom we seek to replenish the community of souls?”
74.12: Excellent Ennosh spoke and taught, saying to Life, his ancestors,
74.13: “How could the community become full, from the souls you have cast into the dregs?
74.14: “How I grieve for my disciples’ children, who are persecuted in Yawar’s name!
74.15: How I grieve for my disciples’ children, who are slain in Life’s name!
74.16: How I grieve for my disciples’ children, who are persecuted in Life’s name!”
74.17: Excellent Ennosh spoke and taught, saying to Life, his ancestors,
74.18: “If it pleases you, Life, my ancestors, when the span of the house is finished,
74.19: the span of the house will be complete, so let’s stop the fallen house.”
74.20: Life, his ancestors, spoke, saying to Excellent Ennosh,
74.21: “How can we stop the house’s span, since the house’s span is not yet complete?
74.22: The span of the house is not yet finished, while the disciples are still rising.”
74.23: Excellent Ennosh spoke, saying to Life, his ancestors,
74.24: “How can disciples and Mandaeans rise to the light,
74.25: when they from the food that the Twelve’s sects eat,
74.26: and drink what they drink, and Spirit has heaped upon them great filth,
74.27: adultery, debauchery, and fornication, so none among them will rise to the light.”
74.28: The Great Life spoke, saying to Excellent Ennosh,
74.29: “Calm down, calm down, Excellent Ennosh, and may the calm of the good be upon you.
74.30: On account of their names, they will not be cut off from Life’s house.”
74.31: Excellent Ennosh spoke, saying to Life, his ancestors,
74.32: “If it pleases you, Life, my ancestors, then let us stop Earth,
74.33: because the whole community of souls is falling into Ur’s maw.”
74.34: The Great Life spoke, saying to Excellent Ennosh,
74.35: “Calm down, calm down, Excellent Ennosh, and may the calm of the good be upon you,
74.36: because our own portion is in the great dregs.
74.37: We have Nazoreans and Mandaeans trapped in Spirit’s captivity.
74.38: They are trapped in Spirit’s captivity, and Ur, the Lord of Darkness, swallowed them,
74.39: because they made prayer and praise, and he holds captive the fallen house.
74.40: They will not be cut off from Life’s house, nor will their names be destroyed from Life’s house,
74.41: because they have gone down to the Jordan, and taken the baptism and Life’s sign upon them,
74.43: Because they made the evening devotionals, they will be established alongside their ancestors.
74.44: Because of the rewards they have given, and the communion they have taken,
74.45: they will see the pure air, and the persecution that passed over them.
74.46: They will forget it, and he will give them speech and hearing in light’s place.”
74.47: Then Excellent Ennosh made a request to Life, saying,
74.48: “If it pleases you, Life, my ancestors, the community of souls was filled with devotionals,
74.49: because they have been tossed into the dregs, and bear nuisance, persecution and deceit,
74.50: and are blocked by the planets’ secrets, and the name of Manda d’Heyyi
74.51: and the name of Yawar were in their hearts and mouths.”
74.52: The Great Life spoke, saying to Excellent Ennosh,
74.53: “Calm down, calm down, Excellent Ennosh, and may the calm of the good be upon you.
74.54: When Earth perishes, Excellent Hibel will come and go,
74.55: and well-prepared and equipped excellencies will go with him to Ur, the lord of darkness,
74.57: ‘Ur! Open your mouth, so that I might have my share of the dregs!’
74.58: Ur will say to Excellent Hibel,
74.59: ‘Magnificent excellency! Whence comes your share of the dregs?’
74.62: trapped in Spirit’s snares, [yet] they mention the name of Life!
74.64: trapped in Spirit’s snares, [yet] they mention the name of Life!
74.66: trapped in Spirit’s snares, [yet] they speak the name that is mine!’
74.67: And then Excellent Hibel will raise his hand to twist back Ur’s mouth,
74.68: and seize the souls of those who took the sign of Life, and mention
74.69: the names of Life and Manda d’Heyyi, and acknowledge Manda d’Heyyi.
74.70: Then he will take them from Ur’s mouth, and throw them into the great Ocean,
74.72: And then those souls will become like white sesame thrown into living water.
74.73: Then he will perform the great baptism, the great baptism he will perform,
74.74: and enter them into the great communion.
74.75: Then he will lead them through the great water channels.
74.76: The water channels’ excellencies will come to face the souls that were in the dregs,
74.77: tears will form in their eyes, and they will say to them,
74.78: ‘You have been living on Earth, and thus within the home of the sinners.’
74.79: Then they will take them by their right hands, and throne all according to their own glory.
74.80: Their forms are shining and magnificent in the great place, in the perfect house.”
74.81: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
74.82: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime precious light be magnified!

75.1: Over yonder, by the seashore, stands and preaches the Peacock.
75.3: “Who is like me? Is there anyone like me?
75.4: They have set me at the enclosure, and made me the enclosure’s guardian,
75.5: until Earth comes to nought. Until Earth comes to nought,
75.6: darkness’ people come to an end, and the canals are cut off from them.
75.7: I am the Peacock; Life, my ancestors, have laid me low.
75.8: They made me the enclosure’s guardian. I was filled with doubt,
75.9: With doubt, I was filled, and my senses failed.
75.11: ‘Who is there that has done to the Great what they have done to me?’
75.12: I, the Peacock, opened my mouth, and spoke to the Great [Life], saying:
75.13: ‘Of those among you who were deficient, whom did the Great [Life] cause to stumble?
75.14: He started a fight because a folly of mine, the Peacock, displeased the Great [Life],
75.15: and made me the enclosure’s guardian, until Earth comes to nought.’
75.16: When the Great [Life] did this to me, the Peacock, my heart sank into my stomach.
75.18: ‘What sins did I commit against Life’s house, that my own ancestors have dethroned me,
75.19: unseated me from my place, and set me at the worlds’ distant end?
75.20: [They set me] at the world’s distant end, until Earth comes to nought,
75.21: until Earth comes to nought, and darkness’ children perish,
75.22: darkness’ children perish, and the water courses are cut off from them.
75.23: They will sink into the darkness, and light’s children will be raised up.’
75.24: When the Great did this to me, my heart sank into my stomach.
75.26: ‘Why do I stand, and worship, and praise Life, my ancestors,
75.27: when they do not take my blessing on high, and have removed me from my place,
75.28: brought me low and accused me, and made me the enclosure’s guardian.’
75.29: When the Great [Life] did this to me, I said,
75.30: ‘Woe is me, the Peacock, whose decency is exceeded by his stupidity,
75.31: whose beauty has killed him, whose own words have trapped him,
75.32: and whose pride has trapped him.
75.33: Woe to you, whose beauty has killed him, and whose own words brought him low.’
75.34: I spoke, saying to the Great [Life,
75.35: ‘Why was I not meek, like the water that comes from the Euphrates’ mouth?
75.36: Why was I not wise, that all the fools before me,
75.37: all who rebelled were then brought down?
75.38: Why was I not truthful, without a lie in my mouth?
75.39: Why was I not set right, like a platter set before the starving?
75.40: They eat their fill from it, then stand and submit to their lord.
75.41: Hibel submitted to his ancestors, and they called him a beloved son.
75.42: The Peacock did not submit, and they called him a defiant son.
75.43: My ancestors on high [do not take] my blessing.’”
75.44: As the Peacock said this, his voice rose up before his ancestors.
75.45: When his ancestors heard his voice, they wrote him a true letter.
75.46: “They put me in my settlement, and said to me, ‘The Great [Life] has extended truth’s hand to you,
75.47: now put your rage out of your mind.’”
75.48: When the Peacock heard so, he became calm and his heart settled down.
75.49: He started to worship and praise his ancestors from beginning to end.
75.51: In the name of the Great Life, may the sublime light be magnified!

76.1: I come with sandals of precious stones, and on my hands are choice gems and pearls.
76.2: In my left hand, they placed a mace, and the great axe of openings,
76.3: which opens the way before me. I will destroy, I will build,
76.4: I will lay waste, and put up my temple.
76.5: The images which were depicted upon it, I have wiped clean from left to right.
76.6: With a wreath upon my head, I go to ages and generations.
76.7: To ages and generations I go, until I reach Jerusalem.
76.8: I set up a throne and upon it I sat, and spoke in the secrets of my wisdom,
76.9: so that Jerusalem, whose gate was shut, and whose bars and bolts were drawn in,
76.10: from my voice and my declaration, the bolts of its closed gate opened,
76.11: and its bars and bolts were rolled back.
76.12: Jerusalem shone in my splendor, all the scents became fragrant.
76.13: Those who stank, their scent became fragrant with my scent.
76.14: I opened the eyes of the blind, and I cured those with skin diseases.
76.15: I put speech in the mouths of these tongue-tied and mute folk.
76.16: I made these crippled and lame folk walk upon their own feet.
76.17: Christ raised his eyes, and he saw me dimly. He changes his appearance to ask me,
76.18: he twists his tongue, and speaks with me in different ways,
76.20: “Who are you, from the First Life, who went with a wreath upon your head,
76.21: you went to ages and generations, until you reached the gate of Jerusalem.
76.22: You set up a throne and upon it you sat, and spoke in the secrets of wisdom,
76.23: so that Jerusalem, whose gate was shut, and whose bars and bolts were drawn in,
76.24: from your voice and declaration, the bolts of its closed gate opened,
76.25: and its bars and bolts were rolled back.
76.26: Jerusalem shone in your splendor, all the scents became fragrant.
76.27: You opened the eyes of the blind, and you cured those with skin diseases.
76.28: You put speech in the mouths of these tongue-tied and mute folk.
76.29: You made these crippled and lame folk walk upon their own feet.
76.30: Christ raised his eyes, and he saw me dimly, and he changes his appearance to ask
76.31: so he twists his tongue, and speaks with me in different ways,
76.33: “Who are you, from the First Life, and from those well-versed in wisdom?
76.34: Show me your mighty deeds in Jerusalem!”
76.35: I trampled on Earth until it trembled, and the heavens were shaken.
76.36: I wrote a letter to the living water, and my letter was not rejected.
76.37: I made my sign upon the fire, but the fire did not sin against me, Excellent Ennosh.
76.38: Christ raised his eyes, he saw me dimly, and he changes his appearance to ask
76.39: so he twists his tongue, and speaks with me in different ways,
76.41: “If you are coming from the First Life, recite a true letter!”
76.42: I recited the beginning of the letter. I recited about Adam and his wife Eve.
76.43: I recited about the head of all generations, Shitel, Adam’s son.
76.44: I recited about the good scion, who sowed ages and generations.
76.45: I recited about Ram and Rud, until they departed through plague and the sword.
76.46: I recited about Shorbey and Sharhabiel, until they departed through flame and fire.
76.47: I recited about Shem, Noah’s son, until they departed through floods of water.
76.48: For whoever heeded and believed me, a spot is set at light’s place.
76.49: For whoever did not heed me, a spot is blocked from light’s place.
76.50: His name will be erased from my scroll, and his form will become dark and not shine.
76.51: The triumphant Life speaks, and the man who went here triumphs!
